issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## Summary

Full Harbor-trial evaluation tasks lose their `task.toml`-declared verifier and agent deadlines during task preparation. A session default of 300 seconds replaces the declared verifier timeout. The trial runtime then injects the row limit as Harbor's `verifier.override_timeout_sec`. Harbor applies the override instead of the task value. Trials whose verifiers need more than 300 seconds fail with `VerifierTimeoutError`.

## Where the 300 seconds come from

- `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/dataset/harbor.py`, `lower_harbor_task`: the `HARBOR_TRIAL_SESSION` branch returned `rollout_spec(task, session)`. It did not read the `task.toml` `[verifier] timeout_sec` or `[agent] timeout_sec` fields. The caller's session supplied all limits.
- The canonical full-trial session config sets `verifier_timeout: 300` (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/config/task_session_config/default.yaml`).
- The trial runtime (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/agent_runtime.py`, `original_harness`) sets `verifier.override_timeout_sec = lowered.limits.verifier_timeout` and `agent.override_timeout_sec = lowered.limits.total_turn_timeout`. Harbor resolves the override first (`vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/trial.py`, `_compute_verifier_timeout_sec`), so the task's own declaration never applies.
- The published Micro210 policy dataset (`open-athena/Marin-Micro-Eval-210` at `4564ed081c316bc3231ae5c3a53a46b39248c819`) ships the same flat limits for all 210 rows: `verifier_timeout` 300.0, `total_turn_timeout` 1800.0. Its release builder hard-coded one limit set for every row and did not read task.toml. That builder is archived off-main. Prepared rows pass through the trainer unchanged, so the 300 s value reaches the runtime.

This is a hard-coded default. The preparation code does not apply a cap and does not read task.toml.

## Evidence

Exp3 Micro210 (step-20 seal, 440 attempts, 5 infrastructure absences):

- `tb2-recovery/terminal-bench/mcmc-sampling-stan` repetitions 1 and 2: task.toml declares `[verifier] timeout_sec = 1800.0`. Trial receipts show `verifier.override_timeout_sec = 300.0` and `Verifier execution timed out after 300.0 seconds`.
- `tb2-recovery/terminal-bench/large-scale-text-editing` repetitions 0 and 1: task.toml declares 1200.0. Same 300 s override. Repetition 2 finished inside 300 s and scored, which shows the cap sits at the edge of the verifier's real runtime.
- `ot-tblite-recovery/pgn-chess-repair-puzzles` repetition 2: a different failure mode. The task declares no build timeout, so Harbor's 600 s default applied to a build-at-start Dockerfile under concurrent sandbox builds. Receipt timings: repetitions 0 and 1 built their sandboxes in 102.2 s and 100.2 s; repetition 2 hit `EnvironmentStartTimeoutError` after exactly 600.0 s.

Agent deadlines have the same problem: the row limit 1800.0 replaces task-declared agent timeouts. 32 of the 70 Harbor tasks in Micro210 declare more than 1800 s (10 tau3-pi and 10 bixbench-pi at 3600 s, 10 swebench-verified at 3000 s, 2 ot-tblite tasks at 3600 s).

## Tasks affected

48 of the 70 Harbor tasks in the Micro210 selection declare a verifier timeout above 300 s. The declared value was truncated to 300 s for every one of them:

| Declared verifier timeout | Tasks |
|---|---|
| 7200 s | tb2 terminal-bench/sam-cell-seg |
| 3600 s | ot-tblite pdf-table-parsing, pgn-chess-repair-puzzles |
| 3000 s | all 10 swebench-verified tasks |
| 1800 s | tb2 terminal-bench/dna-assembly, feal-linear-cryptanalysis, mcmc-sampling-stan, rstan-to-pystan |
| 1200 s | tb2 terminal-bench/large-scale-text-editing |
| 900 s | all 10 ds-1000-local; ot-tblite acl-permissions-inheritance, build-system-task-ordering, multi-labeller, python-api-rate-limit, schedule-vacation; tb2 merge-diff-arc-agi-task, raman-fitting, vulnerable-secret |
| 600 s | ot-tblite ekf-localization; tb2 modernize-scientific-stack; all 10 bixbench-pi tasks |

Environment build/start timeouts are not affected: the row limits carry no build field, and Harbor honors the task declaration or its 600 s default.

## Earlier runs

The same absence pattern appears in the #11337 recipe rows, because each run consumed the same frozen rows:

- Round 2 (437/440): three infra-unscored TB2 attempts, UIDs 225/268/269, `VerifierTimeoutError` — mcmc-sampling-stan rep 2 and sam-cell-seg reps 1 and 2 (declared 7200 s).
- Round 1 (439/440): the one unscored slot was UID399 = tb2 dna-assembly rep 0 (declared 1800 s).
- SFT-746 eval-only row (420/440): 19 unknown outcomes with the reason "Harbor trial has no verifier score". They include tb2 UIDs 135/224/225/268/269/312/357, ot-tblite UIDs 227/314/315/360, swebench UIDs 306/350, ds-1000 UIDs 186/274, and bixbench UIDs 1/265/353.
- 10/05 baseline: run 2 lost 6 TB2 attempts and the RNO control lost 2; run 1 scored 440/440 because its verifiers completed inside 300 s.

The failures cluster on rows whose models produce plausible solutions. A weak model fails the tests fast, so the verifier stays under 300 s. A stronger model triggers the verifier's expensive path, which exceeds 300 s.

## Verifier wall time on a correct solution

Measured with the pinned task images and the oracle solutions:

- `large-scale-text-editing`: the verifier finished in 117 s wall with reward 1 in a 1-CPU, 2 GB container that matches task.toml. The run includes apt and uv setup, 1M-row CSV regeneration, the vim run, and the comparison. The 300 s override sits near the verifier's real runtime, so network setup variance decides the outcome.
- `mcmc-sampling-stan`: the verifier's own tests re-run the full 4-chain, 100,000-iteration MCMC twice, with internal pytest timeouts of 2000 s and 6000 s. The author therefore expects up to roughly two hours of verifier work. A local measurement of the full path (RStan build plus two verifier re-runs) is in progress. The trial receipts already show both failed repetitions ran into the 300 s cap mid-verifier.
- The pinned `mcmc-sampling-stan` image ships R 4.3.3 without cmake and without gfortran. The oracle solution installs gfortran but not cmake, and RcppParallel (a StanHeaders dependency) fails without cmake. The oracle solution cannot install RStan on the pinned image as-is; mcmc-sampling-stan repetition 0's verifier finished in 3.3 s with reward 0 for this reason.

## Fix

Bind the task-declared agent and verifier deadlines into the prepared row limits in the `HARBOR_TRIAL_SESSION` branch of `lower_harbor_task`, like the shellbox branch already does. A task.toml with verifier timeout 1800 s then produces a prepared `verifier_timeout` of 1800 s. A silent `[verifier]` section produces Harbor's own 600 s default. A silent `[agent]` section leaves no task-declared agent deadline, and the deployment settings govern it.

The prepared `attempt_timeout` also grows to cover the declared phases: `max(session attempt_timeout, build_timeout_sec + agent + verifier + cleanup)`. Harbor cancels the whole trial when the attempt expires, so a row that promises a 7200 s verifier under a 2460 s attempt deadline would still go unscored. Behavior tests: `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/tests/cpu/test_harbor_task_lowering.py`.

## Not in scope

- No new canonical policy revision was published and no evaluations were rerun. The frozen Micro210 rows and the recorded scores stay as they are. Rebaseline decisions belong to the experiment owners.
- The pgn-chess-repair-puzzles sandbox-start timeout needs a separate decision (prebuilt image pin, a declared build timeout, or a retry on `EnvironmentStartTimeoutError`).

Part of #11686.

issues.author: mcwitt
issues.body:
`levanter.grug._moe` marks the whole package private in its `__init__.py` ("Private Grug MoE backend implementations"), and then prefixes names inside it with an underscore as well. Thirty-seven of those names are imported by a module other than the one that defines them, so the marker says module-private about names that are never used module-privately.

`_zero_inactive_grouped_rows` is the clearest case. It is defined in `_moe/common.py` and used five times in `_moe/sonic_cute.py`, and never in the module that defines it.

The names span thirteen modules:

```
sharding.py                          9    ep_deepep.py                        1
ep_common.py                         9    ep_fixed_all_to_all.py              1
common.py                            6    ep_fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all.py  1
sonic_cute.py                        4    ep_ragged_all_to_all.py             1
cudnn_wgrad_cute.py                  1    ep_ring.py                          1
local.py                             1    scatter.py                          1
sonic.py                             1
```

Some cross a distribution boundary, not just a module one. `lib/marin/src/marin/testing/moe/ragged_ep.py` imports `_clip_receiver_group_sizes`, `_EXPERT_CHUNKS`, `_quack_grouped_gemm_available`, and `_select_expert_mlp` from levanter, and `tests/test_grug_variant_contracts.py` imports `_compact_grug_mesh_shape`. A leading underscore is the only signal Python has for "do not import this", and marin imports them anyway.

The prefix also costs the thing it was meant to buy. Because everything is underscored, the package cannot distinguish a helper genuinely local to one module from one that is part of the package's internal interface. `_moe/sharding.py` and `_moe/ep_common.py` are effectively shared libraries for the backends, and nothing in the naming says so.

Dropping the prefix from names that cross module boundaries inside `_moe/` leaves the package private via its path, which is where privacy is already enforced. It is mechanical: every importer is in this repository, there are no dynamic lookups by name, and the compatibility rule in `AGENTS.md` says to update call sites rather than keep aliases. It is wide, though, which is why it does not belong inside a feature PR — #8549 added six such names by following the surrounding style, and the reviewer noticed the style rather than the change.

Raised in review on #8549: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8549#discussion_r3876485352

Done when:

- Names in `levanter.grug._moe` that are imported by another module no longer carry a leading underscore, and names used only within their defining module still do.
- Importers are updated in place, in `lib/levanter`, `lib/marin`, `tests/`, and `experiments/`, with no compatibility aliases.
- `uv run --no-project infra/ci/run_tests.py` passes, and `./infra/pre-commit.py --all-files` is clean.

issues.body:
## TL;DR

[PR #8651](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8651) replaces Polars inside Zephyr's shuffle with DataFusion, keeps Zephyr's external spill files on region-local GCS, and exposes DataFusion SQL for columnar map and reducer stages.

Against current main/Polars, the 13 SQL-migrated Datakit stages used 29.39% less CPU, 21.38% less summed stage time, and 49.93% less peak shard memory. Across all 16 shuffle-affected stages, including fuzzy verification's unchanged Python reducer, CPU fell 26.82%. Region-local output validators matched exactly.

## Description

The SQL API mirrors the efficiency boundaries established by [#8154](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8154) and [#8256](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8256):

- `Dataset.sql(...)` runs batch-local map queries against an `input` view.
- `Dataset.group_by(..., reducer=sql(...))` runs a query over the complete target shard after Zephyr's external merge.
- Scalar SQL functions provide expression-based routing keys without serializing DataFusion objects into a plan.

Datakit normalization, fuzzy graph construction, all connected-component iterations, and final fuzzy-attribute materialization use these paths. Fuzzy verification still uses the generic DataFusion shuffle with its existing Python reducer. Download, MinHash, memory-store loading, consolidation, tokenization, and cache-probe work do not execute the new SQL path.

DataFusion native disk spill stays disabled. Zephyr continues to write bounded sorted Parquet chunks and external merge runs to the stage filesystem, which is GCS on Iris. Eight target-shard ranges bound each DataFusion sort while preserving one selected file per mapper flush at reduce time.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Remove Zephyr's Polars dependency and use DataFusion for shuffle sorting, reading, and columnar map/reduce computation without changing semantic output, moving external spill off GCS, or retaining the original DataFusion memory and CPU regressions.

## Status

The implementation is complete on PR #8651, rebased on control commit `dc584e765d` with treatment head `fbddc9de28`.

The affected repository selection passed 1,529 tests with three skips and five expected failures. Ruff, Black, license checks, Pyrefly, documentation checks, and all remaining changed-file checks passed.

## Current-main Datakit ferry

Workload: FineWeb-Edu `sample/10BT` at revision `87f0914`, 14 input files, and the full `experiments.ferries.datakit_ferry` path used by the Polars columnar A/B. Both arms ran concurrently with identical non-preemptible resources in `europe-west4`. Inputs, outputs, status, caches, and Zephyr temporary files all used `gs://marin-eu-west4`; no cross-region GCS access was configured.

Control: main/Polars `dc584e765d`, [`/loom/zephyr-sql-ferry-20260828-control`](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Floom%2Fzephyr-sql-ferry-20260828-control), 56m11.18s.

Treatment: DataFusion SQL `fbddc9de28`, [`/loom/zephyr-sql-ferry-20260828-treatment`](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Floom%2Fzephyr-sql-ferry-20260828-treatment), 59m00.15s (+168.97s, +5.01%).

The SQL-migrated stages processed the same 558,478,005 logical items; all shuffle-affected stages matched at 559,057,070. Byte telemetry is not comparable because the treatment counts Arrow buffer bytes while the control counts its row-oriented representation.

The [control validator](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Floom%2Fzephyr-sql-validate-20260828-control-v2) and [treatment validator](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Floom%2Fzephyr-sql-validate-20260828-treatment-v2) each found 9,672,101 downloaded rows, 9,268,156 normalized rows, 532,777 fuzzy cluster members with 246,814 representatives, 45,970 verified duplicates, and 9,222,186 consolidated and tokenized rows.

Measured CPU across the full ferry fell 9.04%, and summed stage time fell 4.09%. Root wall time rose 5.01% because unaffected runtime was noisier: tokenization elapsed rose from 333.92 to 474.38 seconds with CPU essentially unchanged at +0.69%, followed by a longer cache-probe scheduling delay. Unaffected-stage CPU was flat at -0.30%.

## Earlier evidence

The range-only DataFusion A/B, before the SQL path, used 5.25% more CPU than Polars across the 16 shuffle-affected stages while lowering peak shard memory 43.28%. That isolated Python row materialization and reducer callbacks as the remaining actionable cost.

A control-only Polars target-range sweep showed that the memory mechanism is engine-independent:

| Polars target ranges | Writer time | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 (baseline) | 2.600 s | - |
| 2 | 2.649 s | +1.92% |
| 4 | 2.770 s | +6.55% |
| 8 | 3.319 s | +27.69% |

| Polars target ranges | Peak RSS | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 (baseline) | 1.434 GB | - |
| 2 | 1.256 GB | -12.40% |
| 4 | 1.080 GB | -24.70% |
| 8 | 0.988 GB | -31.07% |

An earlier pre-optimization Nemotron A/B raised affected-stage CPU 39.99% and peak memory from 7.88 to 13.42 GB. That run identified the original whole-buffer DataFusion `SortExec` problem and does not represent the current range-partitioned SQL treatment.

## Links

- Implementation and review: [PR #8651](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8651)
- Per-stage A/B and historical detail: [sticky PR comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8651#issuecomment-5403476301)
- Root-cause and benchmark investigation: [Echo record](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/267)

## Decision Log

- DataFusion native disk spill stays disabled so its internal sorter remains in memory.
- Zephyr's explicit sorted chunks and external merge intermediates remain on the stage filesystem and therefore use region-local GCS on Iris.
- DataFusion uses eight target-shard ranges because two exhausted the sorter and four retained materially more memory.
- SQL is exposed as a serializable Zephyr plan object instead of exposing DataFusion runtime objects.
- Datakit uses SQL only where the transformation is columnar; fuzzy verification retains Python callbacks for full-text comparison and side effects.

## Conclusion

The Python implementation removes the DataFusion memory and CPU regressions without modifying DataFusion. On the matched Datakit ferry, SQL-migrated DataFusion stages were faster than current-main Polars while using half the peak shard memory, and persisted outputs matched exactly.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
## Description

Evaluate whether June 67B context-extension checkpoints use retained MRCR conversation context when scoring the same final assistant response. The paired evaluator compares `full_context` with `query_only`, scores response-body tokens, and stratifies deterministic bootstrap intervals by needle count and evidence distance.

## Task

An MRCR source document contains two worked examples, a long multi-turn conversation with 2, 4, or 8 relevant facts ("needles"), and a final query. `desired_msg_index` identifies a user request in that conversation; its matching answer is the immediately following assistant message.

Each source row produces two documents with the same final query and gold response:

```text
full_context: two worked examples + target conversation + final query -> gold response
query_only:   two worked examples + final query                       -> gold response
```

The primary two-shot prompt supplies the benchmark's 10-character answer prefix. The evaluator scores only the remaining gold assistant response body. The worked examples, retained conversation, final query, supplied prefix, and EOS are context and receive zero loss. Each condition occupies one unsliced, unpacked sequence.

The paired comparison asks whether retaining the target conversation improves the likelihood of the identical response. Results report `query_only - full_context` NLL and BPB gain, with response-token micro and per-example macro aggregation, sliced by needle count and evidence distance.

### Difference from standard MRCR

Standard OpenAI MRCR gives the model the complete conversation, samples a response, requires the nonce prefix in that response, and grades the generated text with a `SequenceMatcher` similarity score. This experiment instead teacher-forces the gold response and measures its token likelihood twice: once with the target conversation and once without it. The supplied prefix is not scored. The resulting paired NLL/BPB gain is a diagnostic of context use, not an official MRCR generation score, and should not be compared directly with published MRCR scores.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Context gain (`query_only - full_context`) should move from non-positive before extension to positive after 64K/262K adaptation. Fixed qk=1.57 comparisons isolate checkpoint adaptation; qk=1.75 is the deployable final arm.

### Links

- [OpenAI MRCR dataset and task description](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/mrcr/tree/f4c69fae7cf81f7ca26b9fee34b392a50f6b8a1d)
- [Research logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/babf963076/.agents/logbooks/paired-mrcr-base-eval.md)
- [Implementation snapshot](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/63027b4e72)
- [Final qk1.57 W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mrcr-67b-step157000-qk157-cap262144-two_shot-v464cp8ep4)
- [Final qk1.75 W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mrcr-67b-step157000-qk175-cap262144-two_shot-v464cp8ep4)

## Results

Context gain is `query_only - full_context`, so positive NLL or BPB gain is beneficial.

| Checkpoint | qk | NLL gain (95% CI) | BPB gain |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| step 141000, pre-extension (8K) | 1.57 | -0.19453 [-0.21900, -0.16930] | -0.05789 |
| step 156000, 64K source | 1.57 | +0.40387 [+0.36399, +0.44537] | +0.12019 |
| step 157000, 262K extension | 1.57 | +1.18860 [+1.14205, +1.23597] | +0.35371 |
| step 157000, deployable arm | 1.75 | +1.26855 [+1.22432, +1.31342] | +0.37751 |

Each checkpoint used the same 299 paired source examples: 598 full-context/query-only condition sequences. Across four checkpoints, this is 1,196 paired checkpoint-example comparisons and 2,392 condition sequences.

Confidence is exploratory because each checkpoint received one evaluation pass over this dataset. One-shot/no-prefix and the full matrix remain untested.

comments.body:
🤖 **Not actionable as a code change — no PR opened.**

This is an experiment report (labels: `experiment`, `long-context`, `evals`), not a bug or task. It documents completed paired-262K MRCR context-gain results across June 67B checkpoints with W&B, logbook, and implementation-snapshot links. There is no defect described, no affected file/command to repair, and no definition of done — nothing to implement or fix.

What would make a follow-up actionable:
- A concrete change request against the evaluator or experiment code (name the file/module and the desired behavior change), or
- A definition of done for the untested arms the report flags as open — one-shot/no-prefix and the full matrix — e.g. which configs to run and what result gate counts as complete.

Absent one of those, this reads as a tracking record and is best left as-is. Happy to pick it up if you convert it into a specific change or run request.

🤖 Added a four-condition oracle-normalized measurement before rerunning the 299-example 262K slice.

The conditions form a 2×2 comparison: needles absent/present and distractors absent/present. `needle_only` retains all repeated target-request turns so the ordinal retrieval problem is preserved; `distractor_only` retains the complementary conversation turns. All four conditions score the same response-body tokens.

The headline recovery ratio is `(distractor_only NLL - full_context NLL) / (query_only NLL - needle_only NLL)`, computed as a token-micro ratio of aggregate paired contrasts. A 10,000-sample bootstrap resamples the same four-condition source tuples within needle-count and evidence-distance strata.

The ratio is identifiable only when the isolated-needle gain is at least 0.10 nats/token, its bootstrap lower bound is positive, at least 99% of bootstrap denominators are positive, and no denominator is zero. Before seeing results, the “good enough” gate is a recovery-ratio 95% lower bound of at least 0.80 plus a positive lower bound for distracted needle gain. Needle-count slices must each have positive distracted needle gain; distance slices are descriptive.

issues.author: wmoss
issues.body:
Marin's Pulumi IaC has no single organizing convention: `infra/pulumi` splits into one GCP stack and four separate CoreWeave cluster stacks, `infra/buckets` spans GCS, CoreWeave object storage, and Cloudflare R2 in one stack, and Cloudflare DNS records are declared inline in three unrelated deploy stacks (`infra/grafana`, `infra/loom`, the CoreWeave federation stack) plus `infra/buckets`. Where a new resource belongs isn't predictable from any rule.

Evaluate consolidating to one stack per provider — GCP, CoreWeave, Cloudflare — with GitHub unchanged, since it's already provider-scoped.

**Prior research**

Full writeup, phase-by-phase migration plan, and `--target` mechanics: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/28f800f1-835e-479a-924c-596a10924138

The target model:
- **gcp** — absorbs `infra/pulumi`'s `marin` stack (federation-egress static IPs, GCLB/IAP, the `marin`/`marin-dev` Iris controllers' own VM-based provisioning, the project-wide IAM registry), the GCS slice of `infra/buckets`, and `infra/cloudsql`.
- **coreweave** — the four existing cluster stacks (NodePools, RBAC, Kueue, Traefik/cert-manager) merged into one, plus the CoreWeave object-storage slice of `infra/buckets`.
- **cloudflare** (new) — every DNS record (the federation CNAME, and each deploy stack's own record) plus R2, each record built from a `StackReference` into its owning stack rather than declared inline.
- `infra/ducky` and `infra/xprof` deploy through `iac.iris.service.IrisService`, a `local.Command` that shells to the Iris CLI rather than a `pulumi_gcp` resource — they don't own any GCP-provider resources and stay independent regardless of this change.

Benefits found: a single GCP stack makes authoritative GCP resources (e.g. a fully-owned IAM binding) safe to adopt, since GCP enforces authority per role/field and one stack means exactly one process ever computes a given role's complete membership — today's non-authoritative `*IAMMember` grants exist partly to avoid needing that guarantee across stacks. `infra/permissions` was already retired into the `marin` stack's `iac.gcp.iam.GcpIam` (#7576), so the same consolidation pattern has worked once before at smaller scale.

`pulumi up --target <urn> --target-dependents` lets one already-decided change land safely across a consolidated stack's resources — canary a CoreWeave config change cluster by cluster, or force one Cloud Run image bump without touching a sibling service. It doesn't reduce Pulumi's state lock, which is always stack-wide regardless of target scope, and the full program still evaluates and declares every resource on every run (a resource that's live but undeclared this run reads as "delete it," so a program can't skip building part of the graph to go faster).

That lock scope is why folding the GCP-hosted service deploys (Grafana, Echo, Evaldash, Loom) into the `gcp` stack is a separate, harder call than the rest of this. `.github/workflows/ops-pulumi-rollout.yaml` already auto-deploys Grafana, Echo, Evaldash, Ducky, and Xprof on every push to `main`, each against its own stack in its own `concurrency` group, so unrelated services deploy in parallel today with zero contention. Merging Grafana/Echo/Evaldash into one `gcp` stack means their independent, path-filtered, automated merges start queuing behind whichever one landed first, even when the two PRs touch disjoint resources — `--target` doesn't fix this, since the lock isn't scoped by target. Recovering today's parallelism would need `ops-pulumi-rollout.yaml` and `scripts/ci/pulumi_rollouts.py` rebuilt to resolve per-service URN target sets and either accept serialized deploys or build an explicit queue.

Given that cost, this consolidation is staged: land the GCP substrate, CoreWeave, and Cloudflare consolidation first (no CI-automation conflict, since none of that is part of the automated rollout pipeline); leave folding the Cloud Run/VM deploys into `gcp` as an explicit follow-up decision rather than a default consequence of adopting the convention.

Open question — fold Grafana/Echo/Evaldash/Loom into the `gcp` stack:
- For: one audit surface for the account's entire Cloud Run/VM/IAM footprint; one credential story.
- Against: trades five parallel, low-friction automated deploys for one shared lock; requires new CI automation (per-service target-set resolution, a queue or accepted serialization) before it's safe; reverses `infra/pulumi.md`'s stated reason Grafana got its own project — its own image and deployment lifecycle.

Done when: a decision is made on the GCP/CoreWeave/Cloudflare consolidation and, separately, on whether to pursue folding the GCP-hosted service deploys in. If the first is accepted, file follow-up issues for each stack's migration.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis — design decision, no PR.** Definition of done here is "a decision is made" on a fleet-wide IaC convention; that's a human architecture call, not an agent-implementable change. I verified the issue's structural claims against the tree and found one thing worse than stated. Below is decision-ready grounding.

# Research

The claims hold. Current layout, verified:

- **1 GCP + 4 CoreWeave stacks** share `infra/pulumi` (project `marin-iac`): [`Pulumi.marin.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/Pulumi.marin.yaml) plus `Pulumi.cw-rno2a.yaml`, `Pulumi.cw-us-east-02a.yaml`, `Pulumi.cw-us-east-08a.yaml`, `Pulumi.cw-us-west-04a.yaml`.
- **`infra/buckets` is one cross-provider stack** — GCS + CoreWeave S3 + Cloudflare R2 providers all instantiated in [`buckets/__main__.py#L23-L39`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/buckets/__main__.py#L23-L39).
- **DNS is scattered across 6 sites, not 4** (correction to the issue): `infra/grafana` ([`__main__.py#L190`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/grafana/__main__.py#L190)), **`infra/echo` ([`__main__.py#L257`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/echo/__main__.py#L257))**, **`infra/evaldash` ([`__main__.py#L121`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/evaldash/__main__.py#L121))**, `infra/loom` ([`infrastructure.py#L620`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/loom/infrastructure.py#L620)), the CoreWeave federation CNAME ([`iac/coreweave/dns.py#L37`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/src/iac/coreweave/dns.py#L37)), and R2 in `infra/buckets`. The issue named only grafana/loom/federation/buckets; echo and evaldash also declare `cloudflare.DnsRecord` inline. Cloudflare is the most fragmented provider — strengthens the consolidation case.
- **`ducky`/`xprof` own no GCP-provider resources** — both build `iac.iris.service.IrisService`, a `command.local.Command` shelling to the Iris CLI ([`iac/iris/service.py#L25-L26`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/src/iac/iris/service.py#L25-L26)). Correctly excluded from the `gcp` target.
- **Parallel-deploy cost is real.** [`ops-pulumi-rollout.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.github/workflows/ops-pulumi-rollout.yaml) matrix-deploys ducky/echo/evaldash/grafana/xprof on push to `main`, each in `concurrency: group: pulumi-rollout-${{ matrix.name }}` (L88-90), driven by [`scripts/ci/pulumi_rollouts.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/scripts/ci/pulumi_rollouts.py). Folding these into one `gcp` stack serializes them behind one stack lock.
- **Precedent works.** `infra/permissions` is retired into `iac.gcp.iam.GcpIam` (#7576); [`permissions/__main__.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/permissions/__main__.py) now raises rather than deploying.

# Recommendation

Adopt the staged split the issue proposes; it is sound and the risky part is correctly isolated.

**Do now (low-risk, no CI-automation conflict):** consolidate to `gcp` (substrate) + `coreweave` (4 clusters merged) + new `cloudflare` (all 6 DNS sites + R2, each built from a `StackReference` into its owning stack). None of these are in the automated rollout pipeline, so no lock contention is introduced. File one follow-up migration issue per stack.

**Defer (needs a separate decision + CI rework):** folding the Cloud Run/VM service deploys (grafana/echo/evaldash/loom) into `gcp`. As the issue notes, `--target` does not scope the state lock, so this trades 5 parallel path-filtered auto-deploys for one serialized lock and requires rebuilding `ops-pulumi-rollout.yaml` + `pulumi_rollouts.py` to resolve per-service URN target sets first. Recommend **not** doing this now — the audit-surface/credential-story benefit doesn't outweigh reversing the documented reason ([`pulumi.md#L39-L49`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi.md#L39-L49)) each service got its own lifecycle.

**Coordinate with in-flight work first** — these touch the same GCP-stack IAM surface and should land before the `gcp` consolidation to avoid rebasing churn: #8455/#8458 (authoritative + centralized app IAM grants), #8459/#8462 (remove retired permissions stack). The authoritative-IAM goal in #8455 is in fact the strongest single argument *for* one `gcp` stack (one process computes each role's full membership), so sequence it deliberately.

Needs a maintainer decision on the two questions above before migration issues are filed. Handing off — no code change to make here.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
Some potential improvements we noticed during the hero run rollout.

scatter aggregation:
  - can you run a scatter aggregation step alongside the mappers? for each N map shards finished, read them in and reshuffle/merge the outputs by reduce shard. the inputs should be pre-sorted by target shard, so in theory this can be done with low-memory. this should reduce read traffic by a factor of ~N, and potentially eliminates the external sort we currently do entirely

datafusion as a loading api:
  - supports parquet reading & query push down
  - seems robust from our experience with finelog
  - trivializes a "lite" sql select only API
  - would be nice for library sharing across projects

mapper auto-tuning:
  - choose the number of mappers for the user based on heuristics or dynamically based on observations
  - we have many pipelines that run 10x too slow just because they have fewer mappers than needed
  - combine this with the scatter aggregation to avoid map/reduce shard blowup

better partial recovery:
  - allow recovering a partially complete run
  - for example the zephyr coordinator might write a state record once a minute recording all of the shard state
  - check for this when booting up and reuse it if the ids match

kv-store work scattering:
  - the kv store actors can be used in the some situations to split up imbalanced workloads
  - push the work to the kv store via compute functions


CC @ravwojdyla @muchanem

issues.author: wmoss
issues.body:
Iris controller restarts today are driven entirely by `iris cluster controller restart` (see `lib/iris/OPS.md`, `.agents/skills/restart-iris/`) — GCE clusters restart via SSH + `docker restart`, CoreWeave clusters via the Kubernetes API — not by Pulumi. This is an investigation, not a commitment to migrate: the restart flow has safety properties that a naive Pulumi resource-replace would break if not carried over deliberately.

Specifically: the controller keeps local SQLite state plus periodic GCS checkpoints, and restart takes a pre-restart checkpoint and writes a rollout record (image + matching checkpoint ref) so a failed health check can roll back atomically. DB migrations are forward-only and some are destructive, so restoring an old controller image without its paired pre-migration checkpoint breaks. Any Pulumi-driven approach needs to preserve this checkpoint-before-restart / paired-rollback behavior, e.g. by keeping restart-with-rollback as a wrapped CLI step (similar to how `iac.iris.service` wraps a CLI today) rather than modeling the controller as a plain replaceable resource.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Investigation, not a bug fix — no PR. Analysis below; handing off to a human for the migrate/don't-migrate call.

# Research

Confirmed the issue body against the code. `iris cluster controller restart` is a CLI-side choreography around a mechanical platform restart; the safety lives in the CLI, not in the platform primitive.

Forward deploy in [`cli/cluster.py:controller_restart` L1117-1215](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1117-L1215): pre-deploy checkpoint (L1180) → build fresh images (L1182) → write `PENDING` rollout record (L1187) → `restart_controller` (L1199) → on health-check failure `_auto_rollback` to previous image + its pre-deploy checkpoint (L1202) → write `COMMITTED` (L1206). `--rollback` (L1148) reverts to the recorded previous image + checkpoint.

The rollout record is a small state machine in GCS remote state, not in any deploy tool's state; the restarted controller consumes `ROLLBACK_REQUESTED` once on boot and self-clears. Migrations are forward-only and some are destructive, so an old image must boot on its paired pre-migration checkpoint — this is why image and checkpoint are recorded as a pair.

**Relevant code**
- [`cli/cluster.py#L1117`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1117) - restart/rollback choreography (checkpoint, record, restart, auto-rollback)
- [`controller/rollout.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/rollout.py) - `RolloutPhase`/`RolloutRecord`, read/write in GCS remote state
- [`platforms/vm_lifecycle.py#L409`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/vm_lifecycle.py#L409) / [`k8s/controller.py#L517`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/controller.py#L517) - mechanical restart primitives (no safety logic)
- [`controller/migrations/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/migrations) - forward-only, sometimes destructive
- [`iac/iris/service.py#L156-L164`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/src/iac/iris/service.py#L156-L164) - existing CLI-wrap template to reuse

# Proposed approach

Do **not** model the controller as a plain replaceable Pulumi resource. A resource-replace would tear down and recreate around the restart, bypassing the checkpoint/rollout-record choreography and losing atomic rollback on a bad deploy.

Instead reuse the pattern already in [`iac/iris/service.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/src/iac/iris/service.py) (and the sibling finelog migration in #7571): wrap `iris cluster controller restart` in a `command.local.Command` component whose `create`/`update` verb runs the restart CLI and whose `delete` is a no-op (or `stop`, deliberately). Key the resource on the controller image tag plus a code hash so a change triggers `update` = restart-with-rollback; a failed health check propagates as a Command error, and the CLI has already auto-rolled-back. The rollout record stays in GCS remote state so `--rollback` keeps working out-of-band from Pulumi state.

Open questions for the human owner:
- Is the goal declarative *drift correction* (Pulumi restarts when image drifts) or just *inventory* (record the controller in the stack without owning restarts)? The wrapper above gives the former; only the latter avoids Pulumi ever triggering a restart.
- How should a Pulumi `up` that fails its health check and auto-rolls-back report to the operator — hard resource failure, or success-with-warning after rollback?
- Interaction with the manual `restart-iris` skill / direct CLI runs: Pulumi must treat an out-of-band restart as convergent, not as drift to undo.

Scope is a new Pulumi component plus wiring — multi-file design work, so leaving implementation to a human per the migration effort in #7571/#7262.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Investigation result: move Iris controller operations under the shared deploy interface, with Pulumi invoking the existing migration-aware restart transaction. Do not make the controller VM or Kubernetes Deployment a plain replaceable Pulumi resource.

Effort: medium, 2026-08-24. I stopped after the current code, linked PRs, Echo history, and Pulumi documentation converged on the same boundary.

### Current Marin context

The new work changes the operator interface, but not Iris's state-safety requirement:

- [#8537](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8537) provides one command tree for Pulumi applications. The executable merged there is `marin-deploy`, so the exact spelling today is `uv run marin-deploy ...`; adding a `deploy` script alias is independent of this design.
- [`controller restart`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1936313ac7da5e1c4f08c0a1634e24cf66f4e772/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1263-L1532) resolves secrets, checkpoints the live controller, builds and pins images, writes `PENDING`, restarts in place, health-checks, and commits or restores the previous image plus checkpoint. The controller [consumes the rollback request once](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1936313ac7da5e1c4f08c0a1634e24cf66f4e772/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/main.py#L51-L85).
- Pulumi [does not automatically roll back a failed update](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/support/faq/infrastructure/#automatic-rollbacks). Finelog therefore captures the active revision outside Pulumi, runs `pulumi up`, restores on failure, and refreshes state ([#7690](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7690), [current implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1936313ac7da5e1c4f08c0a1634e24cf66f4e772/lib/finelog/src/finelog/deploy/_k8s.py#L390-L471)). Iris needs that recovery boundary and its additional checkpoint pairing.

### Recommended first migration

1. Add a separate `infra/iris` application project with one stack per controller cluster. This follows the repository rule that application deploy lifecycles stay outside the static `infra/pulumi` substrate project.
2. Add an Iris controller component backed by `command.local.Command`. Its `create` and `update` verbs run the existing `iris cluster controller restart`; removal has no stop/delete verb. Inputs include the cluster, reviewed config hash, working-tree hash, and an explicit deploy generation for a forced same-tree restart. Pulumi's command provider runs `update` when inputs/triggers change instead of replacing the resource ([provider contract](https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/command/api-docs/local/command/)).
3. Add service-specific commands:

   ```text
   uv run marin-deploy iris rollout <cluster>
   uv run marin-deploy iris rollout <cluster> --force
   uv run marin-deploy iris rollback <cluster>
   ```

   `rollback` must call the existing `--rollback` path and use the GCS rollout record. Pulumi history is not a substitute for the recorded image/checkpoint pair. The rollout record remains the recovery source of truth; Pulumi records which reviewed tree/config triggered the transaction.
4. Keep the existing fleet gates: clean/current tree preflight, one cluster at a time, baseline snapshot, five-minute verification, and smoke job. Do not add Iris to the parallel path-triggered deployment matrix in the first change. That matrix cannot currently stop the fleet at the first failed cluster, and GCE restarts also require per-user SSH access.

This stage gives Iris the shared `marin-deploy` UX and Pulumi update/audit surface while preserving the current transaction even when an operator runs `pulumi up` directly.

### Native-resource follow-up

A later CoreWeave-only stage can adopt the non-secret runtime objects into an application stack: ConfigMap, protected PVC, Recreate Deployment, Service, PDB, node-agent DaemonSet, LocalQueue, and priority classes. It should proceed only after the deploy driver is split into prepare/activate/finalize/rollback operations and these conditions are tested:

- no workload mutation before a fresh checkpoint and `PENDING` record;
- every activation or health failure restores the recorded image and checkpoint, waits for `ROLLED_BACK`, then refreshes Pulumi state;
- direct `pulumi up` cannot bypass preparation;
- secret values remain outside Pulumi state;
- controller storage is protected, and GCE application changes never replace the controller VM;
- manual break-glass rollback remains convergent with the next intentional rollout.

Confidence is high for the first migration. Native CoreWeave ownership is feasible with those gates, but it is a separate lifecycle refactor; GCE should continue using the in-place SSH restart mechanism behind the same command.

### Handoff

No PR was opened because this request was an investigation. The next decision is whether to implement the first migration as scoped above and track native CoreWeave resource ownership separately.

🤖 ### Research

`marin-deploy iris rollout` calls the controller provider's preflight before checkpointing or building images. The CoreWeave provider currently resolves only the controller signing key there; it first reads S3 credentials such as `CW_KEY_ID` and `CW_KEY_SECRET` during Kubernetes activation, after the expensive rollout preparation has completed.

### Proposed Fix

Validate the CoreWeave task environment during [`preflight_controller`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f8265d8a0c6dc6f558aab59bca617cc20f8a88c3/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/controller.py#L471-L474), including S3 credentials and `defaults.inject_env`. Missing variables will fail before the checkpoint and image build. Pulumi activation reads the same operator environment in its separate provider process, keeping secret values out of Pulumi inputs and state. PR #8652 already owns this deploy path; no other open PR overlaps the change.

issues.author: XiaoyuanWang111
issues.body:
Four generated Reasoning Gym tasks give full reward to a reply that does not depend on the question. `reasoning_gym_generated` holds 1,000 rows of each.

- `game_of_life_halting`: every non-blank reply scores 1.0 on all 1,000 entries. The scorer compares `bool(reply)` with `bool(answer)`, and every answer is the string `True` or `False`. [The generator](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym/generate.py#L77-L86) records the reward of the fixed wrong answer `definitely wrong` for every row. For these 1,000 rows the recorded reward is 1.0, and [`convert_generated`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym/tasks.py#L256-L271) stores the record without reading it.
- `complex_arithmetic`: the reply `NaN` scores 1.0 on all 1,000 entries. The scorer returns `min(1.0, math.exp(-distance))`, which is 1.0 when the distance is NaN.
- `coin_flip`: the reply `0` scores 1.0 on 939 of the 1,000 entries. The scorer of `reasoning-gym` 0.1.25 gives partial reward for a matching prefix and divides by the length of the shorter string, so the one-character reply `0` matches every answer that starts with `0.`.
- `propositional_logic`: the reply `P ∨ Q` scores 1.0 on 820 of the 1,000 entries. The scorer accepts any conclusion that follows from the premises, and a disjunction that names a premise follows from it.

Reproduce:

1. From the repository root, run:

   ```bash
   PYTHONHASHSEED=0 uv run --package marin-verifyit --extra reasoning-gym python - <<'EOF'
   import sys

   sys.path.insert(0, "experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym")
   import generate
   import reasoning_gym

   replies = (
       ("game_of_life_halting", "x"),
       ("complex_arithmetic", "NaN"),
       ("coin_flip", "0"),
       ("propositional_logic", "P ∨ Q"),
   )
   for task, reply in replies:
       data = reasoning_gym.create_dataset(task, size=generate.ROWS_PER_TASK, seed=generate.task_seed(task))
       score = reasoning_gym.get_score_answer_fn(task)
       print(task, repr(reply), sum(score(reply, data[index]) == 1.0 for index in range(generate.ROWS_PER_TASK)))
   EOF
   ```

2. It prints `game_of_life_halting 'x' 1000`, `complex_arithmetic 'NaN' 1000`, `coin_flip '0' 939` and `propositional_logic 'P ∨ Q' 820`.

Expected: a constant reply does not earn full reward.

The recorded wrong answer scores 0 on `complex_arithmetic` and `coin_flip` and 0.05 or 0.25 on `propositional_logic`, so that record shows only the first of the four. Two of the four are in the Nemotron blend's part of the released validation panel (`open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Data`): with the panel's own grade script, `P ∨ Q` scores 1.0 on six of its seven `propositional_logic` tasks and `NaN` on its one `complex_arithmetic` task.

I tried 44 constant replies on the first 100 entries of every generated task. No fifth task gives the full reward on more than a quarter of the entries to a constant that is not the entry's answer.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 A fifth task belongs on this list: `puzzle24`. The reply `1*2*3*4` scores 1.0 on all 1,000 of its generated entries. The scorer of `reasoning-gym` 0.1.25 (`reasoning_gym/games/puzzle24.py` L114-L132) checks that the reply evaluates to 24 and contains four numbers between 1 and 10. It does not read the entry's numbers. Five of the 1,000 entries have the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4. The recorded wrong answer `definitely wrong` scores 0.01 on every entry, so that record does not show it.

The last paragraph of the issue says that no fifth task pays a constant on more than a quarter of its entries. None of the 44 constants I tried evaluates to 24, so that sweep could not find this task.

To check, add `("puzzle24", "1*2*3*4")` to `replies` in the script above. It prints `puzzle24 '1*2*3*4' 1000`. `puzzle24` is not in the released validation panel.

issues.author: XiaoyuanWang111
issues.body:
14,062 of the 65,559 tasks of `NeMo:predicted-action` (21.4%) expect a string argument of 10 or more words that occurs nowhere in the request. The source scores a reply 1 only for the exact function name with exact JSON arguments ([`nemo_tool_calls.py` L37](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/47383aec90fd93895cf76ea9cad65b84717d8aae/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemo_tool_calls.py#L37), [`grade_predicted_action_candidate`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/47383aec90fd93895cf76ea9cad65b84717d8aae/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_predicted_action.py#L47-L61)), so a reply passes such a task only when it writes that string character for character. In 13,738 of the 14,062 tasks the only such arguments are `summary` or `issue_summary`, with a median of 32 words. They belong to calls that hand the conversation to a person, such as `transfer_to_human_agent`.

EvalLite's `agents` family is 165 tasks of this source ([recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/47383aec90fd93895cf76ea9cad65b84717d8aae/experiments/post_training/task_curation/recipes/eval-lite.json#L78-L86)). At the source's rate about 35 of them are such tasks, and every checkpoint scores 0 on them. The recipe's seeded order selects 44 when I apply it to the source without the overlap exclusions; I cannot read the training and development sets that the exclusions use.

Reproduce:

1. One task, row 94,789 of the pinned `train.jsonl`. From the repository root, run:

   ```bash
   uv run --package marin-verifyit python - <<'EOF'
   from verifyit.modes.grade_predicted_action import grade_predicted_action_candidate
   from verifyit.spec import FunctionCall, PredictedActionSpec

   expected = (
       "User inherited portfolio with appreciated securities, questions about step-up basis calculation "
       "and tax implications of significant gains."
   )
   spec = PredictedActionSpec(
       expected_calls=(FunctionCall("transfer_to_human_advisor", {"summary": expected, "urgency": "medium"}),)
   )
   replies = (
       expected,
       expected.rstrip("."),
       "The user inherited a portfolio of appreciated securities and asks how the step-up in basis is "
       "calculated and what tax the gains carry.",
   )
   for reply in replies:
       call = FunctionCall("transfer_to_human_advisor", {"summary": reply, "urgency": "medium"})
       print(grade_predicted_action_candidate(spec, (call,)).reward, reply)
   EOF
   ```

   It prints `1.0` for the expected call, `0.0` for the same call without the final period of the summary, and `0.0` for a paraphrase of the summary.

2. The count. The command downloads the pinned `train.jsonl` (1.75 GB) and takes about two minutes:

   ```bash
   uv run --package marin-taskcompendium python - <<'EOF'
   import json
   import statistics

   from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
   from taskcompendium.identity import canonical_sha256
   from taskcompendium.importers.nemo_predicted_action import DATASET, REVISION, import_row


   def texts(value):
       """Every string in a JSON value, and every string inside a string that is itself JSON."""
       if isinstance(value, str):
           yield value
           try:
               value = json.loads(value)
           except ValueError:
               return
           if not isinstance(value, dict | list):
               return
       for item in value.values() if isinstance(value, dict) else value if isinstance(value, list) else ():
           yield from texts(item)


   tasks, free_rows, long_rows, summary_only, longest = 0, 0, 0, 0, []
   with open(hf_hub_download(DATASET, "train.jsonl", revision=REVISION, repo_type="dataset")) as rows:
       for line in rows:
           row = json.loads(line)
           try:
               task = import_row(row, canonical_sha256(row))
           except ValueError:
               continue
           tasks += 1
           seen = "\n".join(texts(row["responses_create_params"]))
           free = {
               key: len(value.split())
               for call in task.grader.parameters["expected_calls"]
               for key, value in call["arguments"].items()
               if isinstance(value, str) and len(value.split()) >= 2 and value not in seen
           }
           free_rows += bool(free)
           if free and max(free.values()) >= 10:
               long_rows += 1
               summary_only += {key for key, words in free.items() if words >= 10} <= {"summary", "issue_summary"}
               longest.append(max(free.values()))
   print(tasks, free_rows, long_rows, summary_only, statistics.median(longest))
   EOF
   ```

   It prints `65559 15164 14062 13738 32.0`: the tasks, the tasks that expect a string of two or more words that is absent from the request, the tasks where such a string has 10 or more words, the tasks among those where only `summary` or `issue_summary` holds such a string, and the median word count of the longest such string.

Expected: a task whose expected call holds free text is left out of the source, or its free-text arguments are compared by a rule that a correct reply can meet.

NeMo Gym's verifier for this dataset compares strings of two or more words by word overlap, with a threshold of 0.1 ([config L7-L8](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Gym/blob/69a514999667cebee03d8fd8bd0aec996a54a504/resources_servers/single_step_tool_use_with_argument_comparison/configs/single_step_tool_use_with_argument_comparison.yaml#L7-L8), [`_compare_strings`](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Gym/blob/69a514999667cebee03d8fd8bd0aec996a54a504/resources_servers/single_step_tool_use_with_argument_comparison/common/verification_utils.py#L597-L634)). The paraphrase of step 1 has an overlap of 0.225 under that rule. The dataset stores 16 rewards per row for Qwen3-235B (`qwen_235b_info`). Their mean is 0.40 on the 14,062 rows and 0.33 on the 46,162 rows whose expected string arguments are all single tokens.

issues.author: XiaoyuanWang111
issues.body:
In `verifyit`'s `math` mode, an equation reference for which SymPy's `solve` returns no solution gives 1.0 to any reply equation that also solves to nothing, such as `1 = 2`. On every 86th row of `MarinSkyRL:numina_math` (9,994 of its 859,494 pinned rows), 588 references contain `=`, are typed EQUATION and score 1.0 as their own reply. 32 of them give 1.0 to both `1 = 2` and `3 = 7`, 32 give 1.0 to the reference with its right-hand side replaced by `-987654.321`, and 35 (6.0%) do one or the other.

Two such references in the source are the boxed conclusions `5 + 3 + 14 = 22` ("Find the quantity of 5-primable integers smaller than 1000") and `f(2008) = 1` ("find f(2008)"). `1 = 2` scores 1.0 against both. The values the problems ask for, `22` and `1`, score 0.0.

The cause is https://github.com/huggingface/Math-Verify/issues/87: `sympy_solve_and_compare` solves both equations for their free symbols and compares the two solution lists pairwise, and two empty lists compare as equal. `_verify_pair` hands a pair of equations to `verify` as it is ([`grade_math.py` L144-L151](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/47383aec90fd93895cf76ea9cad65b84717d8aae/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L144-L151)), and its chain branch compares the links of a chain the same way ([L119-L131](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/47383aec90fd93895cf76ea9cad65b84717d8aae/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L119-L131)): `a+b+c = 6+2+11 = 19` gives 1.0 to `a+b+c = 6+2+11 = 20`. The Evalchemy scorer skips `verify` when the reference and the reply are both relations without free symbols ([`grade_boxed_math` L80-L81](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/47383aec90fd93895cf76ea9cad65b84717d8aae/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/math.py#L80-L81)). A reference with free symbols can solve to nothing as well: `(10a + 5)^2 = 100a(a + 1) + 25`, another boxed conclusion of the source, is an identity, and `1 = 2` scores 1.0 against it in both graders.

The source's only control is the golden `reference_reply` ([`skyrl/math.py` L27](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/47383aec90fd93895cf76ea9cad65b84717d8aae/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/math.py#L27), [L280](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/47383aec90fd93895cf76ea9cad65b84717d8aae/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/math.py#L280)), and these references pass it. Neither recipe (`snowball-100k.json`, `eval-lite.json`) names the source today.

Reproduce:

1. Three references from the source, and `x = 5` for comparison. From the repository root, run:

   ```bash
   uv run --package marin-verifyit --extra math python - <<'EOF'
   from verifyit.modes.grade_math import grade_math_candidate
   from verifyit.spec import MathSpec, MathType

   CASES = (
       ("5 + 3 + 14 = 22", ("5 + 3 + 14 = 22", "5 + 3 + 14 = 23", "1 = 2", "22")),
       ("f(2008) = 1", ("f(2008) = 1", "f(2008) = 99", "1 = 2", "1")),
       ("a+b+c = 6+2+11 = 19", ("a+b+c = 6+2+11 = 19", "a+b+c = 6+2+11 = 20", "1 = 2", "19")),
       ("x = 5", ("x = 5", "x = 6", "1 = 2", "5")),
   )
   for reference, replies in CASES:
       spec = MathSpec(expected=reference, math_type=MathType.EQUATION)
       print(reference, "|", ", ".join(f"{reply}: {grade_math_candidate(spec, reply).reward}" for reply in replies))
   EOF
   ```

   It prints:

   ```
   5 + 3 + 14 = 22 | 5 + 3 + 14 = 22: 1.0, 5 + 3 + 14 = 23: 1.0, 1 = 2: 1.0, 22: 0.0
   f(2008) = 1 | f(2008) = 1: 1.0, f(2008) = 99: 1.0, 1 = 2: 1.0, 1: 0.0
   a+b+c = 6+2+11 = 19 | a+b+c = 6+2+11 = 19: 1.0, a+b+c = 6+2+11 = 20: 1.0, 1 = 2: 0.0, 19: 0.0
   x = 5 | x = 5: 1.0, x = 6: 0.0, 1 = 2: 0.0, 5: 1.0
   ```

2. The count. The command downloads the five pinned shards (1.2 GB) and takes about three minutes:

   ```bash
   uv run --package marin-taskcompendium --extra pipeline python - <<'EOF'
   import pyarrow.parquet as pq
   from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
   from taskcompendium.convert.answers import math_type
   from verifyit.grade import GradingInfraError, InvalidTask
   from verifyit.modes.extract import extract_boxed
   from verifyit.modes.grade_math import grade_math_candidate
   from verifyit.spec import MathSpec, MathType

   REPO, REVISION, STRIDE = "AI-MO/NuminaMath-CoT", "9d8d210c9f6a36c8f3cd84045668c9b7800ef517", 86


   def reward(spec: MathSpec, reply: str) -> float | None:
       try:
           return grade_math_candidate(spec, reply).reward
       except (InvalidTask, GradingInfraError):
           return None


   equations = contradictions = replaced = either = index = 0
   for shard in range(5):
       path = hf_hub_download(REPO, f"data/train-{shard:05d}-of-00005.parquet", revision=REVISION, repo_type="dataset")
       for solution in pq.read_table(path, columns=["solution"])["solution"].to_pylist():
           index += 1
           expected = extract_boxed(solution) if index % STRIDE == 0 else None
           if not expected or "=" not in expected or math_type(expected) is not MathType.EQUATION:
               continue
           spec = MathSpec(expected=expected, math_type=MathType.EQUATION)
           if reward(spec, expected) != 1.0:
               continue
           equations += 1
           first = reward(spec, "1 = 2") == 1.0 and reward(spec, "3 = 7") == 1.0
           second = reward(spec, expected.rsplit("=", 1)[0] + "= -987654.321") == 1.0
           contradictions += first
           replaced += second
           either += first or second
   print(index, equations, contradictions, replaced, either)
   EOF
   ```

   It prints `859494 588 32 32 35`: the rows read, the equation references among every 86th row, those that give 1.0 to both `1 = 2` and `3 = 7`, those that give 1.0 to the replaced right-hand side, and those that do either. The count asks for both contradictions because a reference that math-verify reads as the number 2 gives 1.0 to `1 = 2` by its right-hand side.

Expected: a reply that states a different equation scores 0.0 against these references, or conversion rejects the references that the comparison cannot check.
issues.title: [verifyit] 32 of 588 numina_math equations give 1.0 to `1 = 2` and to `3 = 7`

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
🤖 Curated Python code evaluations fail every attempt during grading with `Grading environment setup failed: exit=1`. The model's responses are fine, but no sample is scored. This affects HumanEval+, MBPP+ and CRUXEval on current main.

The code graders declare `python3 /tests/prepare.py` as an environment setup command ([`convert_python`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/code.py)). `prepare.py` reads the candidate's answer from `/app/answer.txt` to build the test program. [`_grade_on`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py) runs setup commands before it installs the submission archive that contains `/app/answer.txt`, so `prepare.py` fails:

```
File "/tests/prepare.py", line 15, in main
    response = Path("/app/answer.txt").read_text()
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/app/answer.txt'
```

Reproduce:
1. Run a curated `cruxeval`, `humanevalplus` or `mbppplus` evaluation from main.
2. Read `data/evaluation_attempts` in the run's results. Every finished attempt has `outcome = infra_error`, and its result blob carries the traceback above in `grade.diagnostics.stderr`.

Expected: the code graders can read the candidate's answer, either because the answer is installed before `prepare.py` runs or because preparation runs after the submission is installed.

Observed in CRUXEval run `20261113-192007-Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-2c59e4d3702e48eab27ff3b1ddbe5c60-cruxeval-dda752051d0a55b3a9b6706ffcd6a9fe`, where every attempt on all 20 smoke items failed this way. HumanEval+ and MBPP+ use the same setup command; I have not run them yet.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`convert_python` puts `prepare.py` in environment setup, but `_grade_on` installs the answer archive after setup. The runtime order is intentional: a candidate file must be able to replace a setup fixture. PR #10115 changes grading failure classification in the same runtime file but does not address this recipe.

**Relevant code**
- [`code.py#L103-L130`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/code.py#L103-L130) — Python grader recipe.
- [`grading.py#L621-L650`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L621-L650) — setup precedes answer installation.
- [`test_runtime.py#L911-L930`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/tests/test_runtime.py#L911-L930) — setup fixture replacement contract.

# Proposed Fix

Run `prepare.py` immediately before `program.py` in the Python grader command, after the answer archive is installed. Advance the code recipe revision and check the published grader recipe in a regression test.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
`grade_math_candidate` converts math_verify's `TimeoutException` into `GradingInfraError("math verifier deadline exhausted")`. For some tasks the timeout is deterministic: every attempt of the same task parses a candidate/reference combination that exceeds the deadline, so the task records only infrastructure attempts and the source stays permanently pending — retries cannot change the outcome.

Observed in small-v16 (`2026.11.14.43/small-v16`, exited successfully), source `pafitis:hardmath` (13 of its 100 selected tasks are pending):
- 78 infrastructure attempts across 13 tasks; the sampled receipts show 11 distinct tasks whose every attempt ended with `GradeResult(status=Outcome.INFRA_ERROR, error='math verifier deadline exhausted')`, e.g. `hardmath-1e2483b884b23134518281560e7093cdb0689ff00aaf5ef6de464e5ff9aef213`, `hardmath-0a3338878b6532ef6fae4cbde3092f9653bf84206b34288958ef7c77044040bf`, `hardmath-986bc6ec98013391ee11cc99227c50a728625b18521826dbbd5cc41a845d73c8`.
- Every attempt consumed a full solver trial (model inference + judge) before the deadline failure.

Reproduce:
1. Grade a `pafitis:hardmath` candidate listed above against its TaskSpec reference with the protocol's math-verify profile and deadline.
2. `math_verify` raises `TimeoutException` inside its parse/verify; the grader maps it to `GradingInfraError`; the trial records `INFRA_ERROR` with no reward.
3. Repeating the attempt reproduces the same timeout.

Expected: a deterministic per-task deadline failure should be distinguishable from transient infrastructure load — e.g. a larger or shape-specific parse deadline, a cheaper pre-check for pathological candidate/reference pairs, or a typed condition that stops retrying and reports the task as ungradeable instead of consuming the full attempt budget.

Grader code: `lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py:316-318` (`except TimeoutException ... raise GradingInfraError("math verifier deadline exhausted")`), deadline via `math_verify.utils.timeout` at `lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py:325`.

Evidence receipts (S3, no PII): `s3://marin-rno2a/marin/rl-data/atlas/difficulty/2026.11.14.43/small-v16/trials/<sha256("pafitis:hardmath")>/attempts/<task_key>/*/attempt.json`.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

Verifyit maps every math-verify deadline during reference parsing, candidate parsing, or comparison to the same infrastructure error. In draft PR #11277, Atlas runs another full trial after an unscored attempt and resumes every task without a scored result, so repeated verifier deadlines consume solver work and leave the source pending. The receipts establish repeated failures, but do not yet show which grading phase timed out or whether the candidate text was the same across attempts.

**Relevant code**

- [`grade_math.py#L309-L318`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0169e8a4feccf4db58a3b3fac50c5f24c78be473/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L309-L318) — collapses deadline phases
- [`grade_math.py#L48-L54`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0169e8a4feccf4db58a3b3fac50c5f24c78be473/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L48-L54) — five-second main-thread deadline
- [`difficulty_trials.py#L370-L387`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7c86252b6c790c1d9feb1fc02ceb025359fe8303/experiments/post_training/task_curation/difficulty_trials.py#L370-L387) — retries unscored trials
- [`difficulty_trials.py#L494-L508`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7c86252b6c790c1d9feb1fc02ceb025359fe8303/experiments/post_training/task_curation/difficulty_trials.py#L494-L508) — resumes unscored tasks
- [`difficulty.py#L275-L315`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7c86252b6c790c1d9feb1fc02ceb025359fe8303/lib/finestore/src/finestore/rl/difficulty.py#L275-L315) — excludes failures from scored coverage

# Proposed Fix

1. Replay several affected TaskSpecs and archived candidate outputs in the pinned grader environment. Record the reference, candidate, profile, and input hashes, and identify whether each timeout occurs in reference parsing, candidate parsing, or comparison. Test the same input again under the same deadline before treating it as deterministic.
2. Carry a typed timeout phase through Verifyit's infrastructure verdict. Run a bounded reference preflight before solver inference in the grader's main process or an isolated child process; the current signal deadline is disabled in worker threads. A confirmed fixed-reference timeout becomes a terminal, unscored task condition. Candidate-dependent timeouts remain infrastructure failures while retryable; after a cumulative retry cap, record a terminal `grader_blocked` reason without assigning a zero reward.
3. Extend Atlas's attempt receipts and recovery filter with a terminal blocked status and reason. Add `blocked_tasks` to measurement accounting, so `scored + retryable pending + blocked` equals the selected population; use a distinct blocked source status when no retryable tasks remain. Historical infrastructure receipts remain unclassified. Blocked tasks never enter `n` or `solved`. Coordinate the Atlas portion with draft PR #11277, which owns these paths.

Test the fixed-reference path before any solver call, candidate/compare timeout classification, recovery across campaign versions, and unchanged scoring for gradeable tasks. Replaying the sampled HARDMath tasks should show no repeated full trials after a terminal diagnosis and no invented solver scores. A longer verifier deadline should be evaluated from the replay timings before changing the global five-second limit.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 I replayed the `math` mode on the pinned HARDMath mirror to see which step runs out and whether it depends on the reply. The comparison runs out, and only for some replies: the conversion check and a reply equal to the reference finish on every row, while a reply that is another equation often reaches the deadline.

The data is `pafitis/HARDMath_processed_training` at 937e9f10, all 702 rows. Each contract is built from `ground_truths` as `math_answer_task` builds it and graded through `verifyit.grade.run` on main, one process per call. 684 rows convert; the other 18 have the unparseable reference of #11510. The replies are constructed. I have no access to the stored attempts, so I cannot say which replies the 13 pending tasks received.

| reply | scored 1 | scored 0 | deadline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| no answer file (the conversion check) | 0 | 684 | 0 |
| `\boxed{reference}` | 684 | 0 | 0 |
| `\boxed{42}` | 0 | 684 | 0 |
| `\boxed{reference of the next row of the same question type}` | 0 | 491 | 193 |
| `\boxed{reference with its first number raised by 1}` | 0 | 532 | 152 |

- **Which rows.** The 193 are 102 of the 125 ODE rows and 91 of the 101 symbolic nondimensionalization rows. Their references are equations, `[y = …, y = …]` and `\epsilon=…`. The other three question types (458 rows) never reach the deadline.
- **Which step.** In all 193 calls, parsing the reference and parsing the reply return within 0.5 s. The time goes into math-verify's comparison of the two equations (`sympy_compare_relational`): its symbolic equality check, then solving both equations with SymPy (`sympy_solve_and_compare`). With the deadline set to 20 s, 41 of the 193 comparisons finish, in 5.1 to 19.6 s, and 152 do not.
- **Which replies.** For symbolic nondimensionalization, the reference with one exponent changed reaches the deadline on 81 of 89 rows. The reference regrouped as `\epsilon=\frac{a_{1} a_{3}^{p/q}}{a_{2}^{p/q} a_{3}}` (`p/q` is its exponent), which is equal for positive coefficients, reaches it on 74 of 89 and scores 0 on the other 15. The right-hand side alone, without `\epsilon=`, scores 1.0 on all 101.

For the retry limit of #11518 this means the verdict follows the reply. A task is blocked once three consecutive attempts reach the deadline, which here means three replies that are another equation, wrong or regrouped; a reply in the reference's own form scores 1.0 in under a second. The blocked tasks leave `n`, and the tasks the solver got right stay.

One case, row 9 of the train split, with row 20's answer (the same expression with exponent 17/6) as the wrong reply:

```python
from verifyit.grade import GradingInfraError
from verifyit.modes.grade_math import grade_math_candidate
from verifyit.spec import MathSpec, MathType

reference = r"\epsilon=\frac{a_{1} \left(\frac{a_{3}}{a_{2}}\right)^{\frac{19}{9}}}{a_{3}}"
spec = MathSpec(expected=reference, math_type=MathType.EQUATION)
for reply in (reference, "42", reference.replace("19}{9", "17}{6")):
    try:
        print(grade_math_candidate(spec, reply).reward, reply)
    except GradingInfraError as error:
        print(error, reply)
```

It prints `1.0`, `0.0` and `math verifier deadline exhausted`.

On the conversion side, `convert_hardmath` passes `ground_truths` whole, so the reference keeps its left-hand side. The two older HARDMath loaders (`_prepare_hardmath`, `_hardmath_records`) keep only the right-hand side and reject answers that contain `[`. With those two rules 383 rows remain, and with the next row's answer as the reply none of them reaches the deadline; the slowest call takes 0.49 s.

comments.body:
🤖 Follow-up landed on the atlas-env-audit integration branch (commits 6f86b4eff3 and 6226c25acf; the lane lands directly on that branch, so there is no separate PR). The grading-phase finding is implemented:

1. A math verifier deadline verdict now records the grading phase that ran out: reference parse, candidate parse, or comparison.
2. Only a reference-parse deadline blocks a task after three consecutive attempts. A comparison-phase deadline is an unscored attempt that follows the reply and never blocks by itself.
3. A task whose attempts end without a score keeps the typed math_verifier_deadline gap on the measurement with its counts, so a source with deadline-stalled tasks never reads as a complete measurement. A private remediated release keeping only the right-hand side, with its own SAMPLE QA and admission, is scoped and ready for the ingest and QC lanes; the measurement and plan live in the difficulty follow-up workspace.
