issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
🤖 A packaged scorer can only declare a judge as a `JudgeSpec`, which bundles judge access (model, timeouts, retries, token cap) with a grading rubric (reference, checklist or labels). Before any run, `ScriptGrader` validates that rubric in full. FACTS Grounding v2 (#11753) runs its own three-step judge protocol and needs only access, so it stores its user request in `JudgeSpec.question` and its context document in `JudgeSpec.references` to pass validation.

Proposed fix: add a `JudgeAccess` type in verifyit and an optional `ScriptGrader.judge_access` field, exclusive with `judge`. The runtime stages it and injects the endpoint as it does for `judge`. `judge_reply` takes it. FACTS then moves its request and document into its scorer's `config.json`. A later step could have `JudgeSpec` contain `JudgeAccess` instead of repeating its fields, and give every packaged scorer a single judge field; that would move olympiad's rubric into its scorer.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`ScriptGrader.judge` accepts only a `JudgeSpec` and validates its rubric before a task runs. In open PR #11753, FACTS stores `user_request` and `context_document` in `JudgeSpec.question` and `references` solely to call `judge_reply`; its three-step grading protocol is implemented by the scorer. `render_spec` serializes registered verifier modes, so an access-only contract needs separate staging.

**Relevant code**
- [`models.py#L604-L640`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/20b7b228a95d7859938bdcefef3a63ce9f48f8ba/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/models.py#L604-L640) — script grader validation
- [`grading.py#L435-L448`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/20b7b228a95d7859938bdcefef3a63ce9f48f8ba/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L435-L448) — judge contract staging
- [`grading.py#L584-L601`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/20b7b228a95d7859938bdcefef3a63ce9f48f8ba/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L584-L601) — endpoint injection
- [`grade_judge.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/afe28dc42e02888396273481eb066dd63f48941c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py) — `judge_reply` transport
- [`facts_grounding.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/afe28dc42e02888396273481eb066dd63f48941c/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/facts_grounding.py) — request/document placement

# Proposed Fix

This crosses verifyit, taskcompendium, and the still-unmerged FACTS code in #11753. Implement against #11753 after it merges:

1. Add a frozen `JudgeAccess` contract for model, request timeout, transport retries and budget, token cap, and reasoning effort. Validate those fields without rubric checks. Change `judge_reply` to accept it while preserving chat-completion, completed-text, retry, usage, and error-evidence behavior. Leave existing `JudgeSpec` grading intact.
2. Add `ScriptGrader.judge_access`, reject tasks that set both judge fields, and stage the access contract separately under `/tests/judge_access.json`. Inject the configured endpoint and model as for `judge`, without serializing credentials. Update `source_package` and `grades_with_judge` so controls and inventory still recognize the task as judge-backed.
3. Move FACTS `user_request` and `context_document` into its `config.json`; have the scorer read that data and the staged access contract before calling `judge_reply`. Expose the selected model in the FACTS verdict detail so judge controls can verify a remote verdict. Keep olympiad on `JudgeSpec`; leave the broader `JudgeSpec` composition refactor for later.
4. Cover mutual exclusion and task JSON round trips, rubric-free access through a local grading machine and fake judge endpoint, credential isolation, retry/incomplete-reply behavior, and FACTS publication/scoring with the request and document in `config.json`. Run the affected package tests and required pre-PR checks before opening a PR with `Fixes #11756`.

- At `8c9be40510`, two digest-pinned candidates now convert: `task_c-memory_qi67nu17` captures `/workspace` and `/root/.claude/memory`; `task_gws-sheets-append_njhq0ebv` captures `/work` and `/var/lib/gws-local`. The unchanged native verifier and converted grading path returned identical components in all ten controls: initial state, reference solution, modified state, deleted state, and empty submission for each task. Both reference solutions scored 1.0; negative controls reduced rewards as expected.
- These ten controls used isolated, network-disabled host-Python sandboxes and the real runtime file-capture/grading interfaces. The original Docker images were not built. Other exclusions remain: 39 file-capture candidates still need validation, plus the 22 metadata, 5 live-process, and 5 startup cases. The full-release QUICK driver has not been rerun after these two exceptions.
- All 14 focused conversion and fixture-grading tests and mechanical lint pass at `8c9be40510`. The broader affected suite is left to CI; no new independent review has run on this checkpoint. The independent review of `5078b1e56a` found no actionable issues.
- Image resolution, native-container grading, quality reviews, and difficulty runs remain unfinished. No model calls were made for this conversion validation.

Remote evidence: Iris job `/exedev/skill2env-quick-batches-20261021`, recipe revision 8. Batch manifests, output archives, logs, and `result.json` are under `gs://marin-us-central2/tmp/ttl=7d/skill2env-quick-batches-20261021`. The original 7,496 archives remain cached under `gs://marin-us-central2/tmp/ttl=7d/skill2env-hub-cache-20261021`; subsequent checks can reuse them. These paths have a seven-day retention policy. The case-by-case exclusion assessment and ten-control result JSON are retained locally in `/tmp/10154-all-evidence/`.

Remaining work:

- [x] Merge the pinned catalog declaration (#10120).
- [x] Merge Harbor Hub acquisition (#10198).
- [ ] Review and merge QUICK conversion (#10154).
- [ ] Build and pin actor/verifier images, configure native resource limits, and validate preservation of native grading behavior on a varied bounded sample. Keep unsupported execution contracts explicit.
- [ ] Run a bounded SAMPLE campaign under the current workflow and inspect execution, grading controls, task quality, and model difficulty results. Document defects, exclusions, and assessment limits.
- [ ] Publish the inventory through a curation campaign and verify the live Atlas source entry. Inventory publication does not require executing Skill2Env.
- [ ] Publish and verify the resulting assessment and evidence in Atlas, then close this intake issue.

The earlier sampled investigation and verifier-defect reproduction below remain evidence for follow-up validation, not a completed assessment under the current curation workflow. Historical ratings, eligibility rules, runtime choices, and deployment procedures are not current completion requirements. The official release and grader remain unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Earlier 100-task conversion validation</summary>

Validation so far:

- The complete QUICK driver on a deliberately varied sample of 100 real tasks across 80 skill-name groups produced 99 TaskSpecs, one expected rejection, and no unexpected failures at `5078b1e56a`. The run used one CPU worker on reserved TRC capacity through Iris; captured manifests and Parquet outputs were retrieved and checked, including TaskSpec readback. This is not an estimate of release-wide coverage.
- The rejected `task_winui-app_exphg7he` requires a running process and a live socket outside `/workspace`. It remains explicitly unsupported by this adapter; copying files alone would not preserve its grading contract.
- All 14 focused conversion and fixture-grading tests and mechanical lint pass at `5078b1e56a`. GitHub review findings were addressed, including filtering stale cached archives against the current acquisition manifest. An independent review of that commit found no actionable issues.
- These checks do not establish native container grading equivalence. No full-release conversion, image build, native container grading, quality review, difficulty run, or model call was performed for the current conversion PR.

Remote validation evidence: Iris job `/exedev/skill2env-quick100-20261021-r2`, recipe revision 8, completed successfully on 2026-10-21. The driver took about 17 seconds with peak RSS about 794 MiB. Captured output archive SHA-256: `c9b7727869de36bde4091efc7612ad2075c9ef914986fa984991faa9097a7a7d`. Iris retains the remote archive for seven days; a downloaded copy, driver log, selection, manifest, and Parquet outputs are retained locally. This validates QUICK conversion only, not task execution or grading.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Historical investigation and superseded implementation plan (before #10120)</summary>

The record below is preserved for its evaluation evidence and implementation history. Status statements, integration questions, and checklists in this section refer to the former #9632 approach and are superseded by the current status above.

Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the [RL Data Atlas](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/fb11c931-5861-4878-8bb5-a964d652b45f/) with an assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks dataset intake, validation and publication. Training integration and repairing the dataset's grader are separate work.

The target is the official [Harbor Hub release](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/skill2env/skill2env), revision 2, containing 7,496 tasks. Harbor shows the tags `latest` and `v1.0`; the same release's version field is `1.0.1`. These labels refer to the same content. The paper's private S2EBench evaluation set is separate.

Current status: implementation and sampled validation are prepared in PR #9632, now ready for review. The proposed Atlas rating is "Some issues" because one task's grader was shown to reject valid tests. This rating is not yet published. The official release and its grader remain unchanged; the investigation used two temporary copies with modified reference answers.

The intake can finish with a documented "Some issues" rating. Existing Atlas policy permits the standard Small/Large/Hosted model difficulty comparison only for sources rated "Good", so no difficulty comparison was launched. That is an eligibility decision, not an estimate that these tasks are easy or hard. The three-task quality sample does not establish quality across the full dataset.

Evaluation scope: reported rewards come from the released executable graders. The release also includes written rubrics; the paper's additional LLM rubric-scoring layer was not run or validated here ([§§3.2.2 and 4.2](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.reinforcing-agents-collective-skills.pdf)). Atlas's GLM-5.3 quality audit separately reviews tasks and graders and does not contribute to those rewards.

The PR contains the implementation and concise design rationale. The evidence and integration review questions below support the assessment. The author has marked the PR ready; Ben's Atlas integration review is still pending. The proposed sequence is review, merge, publish, then verify the live entry; this issue stays open through that verification.

### Integration questions for review

- Catalog design: add checked-in Harbor release registrations as an extension to merged #9518. To assess a newer release, a contributor would update the registration through a Marin PR. Atlas refresh would read that registration; it would not automatically switch releases. Evaluation jobs download tasks separately.
- Runtime dependency: retain the review runner's existing MarinSkyRL result adapter and checkout metadata. The catalog entry needs no training registration, but the runner still has this dependency. Review whether to keep it or separate the Harbor runner from MarinSkyRL before landing.
- Agent setup: use Atlas's Terminus-2 with checksum-pinned tools installed offline, preserving the tasks' network restrictions and resource limits. The paper used Pi; these measurements evaluate the Atlas setup.
- Evaluation budget: the sample used a 50-turn limit inherited from Atlas's example configuration. Two of three attempts reached that limit before signaling completion. Review whether this budget is sufficient for initial intake or whether a larger-budget follow-up is needed.
- Scores: preserve all native reward components from the released executable graders, report their arithmetic mean, and count a full pass only when every component reaches one within numerical tolerance. The paper's additional LLM rubric reward was not run. Atlas's separate LLM quality audit does not contribute to these scores.
- Shared tooling: keep the review-output validation, provenance, evidence-retention and provider-call fixes here, or split them into prerequisite PRs.
- Assessment scope: accept the seeded three-task sample as initial intake evidence. It does not establish quality or difficulty across all 7,496 tasks.

Done when:

- [x] Identify the official release and record its task count, source links and license scope in the proposed registration.
- [x] Run the sampled quality review and preserve the original solver, grader and review evidence.
- [x] Assess eligibility for the standard difficulty comparison; currently ineligible under the "Good"-only rule.
- [ ] Review and merge #9632.
- [ ] Reconcile the currently deployed Atlas source with Ben and agree on who will publish the update.
- [ ] Publish and verify the source entry, dated assessment and grading-problem record in Atlas, then close this intake issue.

<details>
<summary>Evaluation results, diagnostic reproduction and evidence identifiers</summary>

The official dataset accompanies [Reinforcing Agents with Collective Skills](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.reinforcing-agents-collective-skills). The registered release digest is `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`. Project-owned code is Apache-2.0; third-party task assets retain their own terms.

Sampled evaluation:

Three tasks were selected with seed 42 from all 7,496 pinned release tasks. Every reference-solution reward component was 1 and every no-op component was 0. Task checksums match across those controls and the original GLM-5.3 attempts. All three model attempts reached the native grader without an execution exception; none achieved a full pass.

| Sampled task | Mean component reward | Agent outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ai-seo | 0.93 | Declared completion |
| api-design-reviewer | 0.00 | Used all 50 turns; did not declare completion |
| property-based-testing | 0.25 | Used all 50 turns; did not declare completion |

Scores describe performance within a 50-turn budget. We have not tested whether additional turns improve the two unfinished attempts.

The solver used Terminus-2, GLM-5.3 on Together, Low reasoning effort, and 65,536-total/16,384-output token limits. The Atlas quality-review panel uses GLM-5.3 for three judgments per task and task/source syntheses. All 555 trace-section reviews and 16 original records pass content, schema, reference and evidence-hash checks. The 246 original native artifact files remain byte-identical.

Grader diagnostic:

The task `task_property-based-testing_2kbxlnww` asks the agent to write property tests for a software-version comparison API. A separate diagnostic checked whether its grader wrongly penalizes valid self-comparison tests. Harbor's "oracle agent" runs the supplied reference solution; it is not another model.

The task was pinned at digest `c193f032e03538d875efd6a54026a39621329c2bd88614dab0160b256ed8b4a7`, using official Harbor runner commit `bf991e490394ef9c3250a6db2bc5cbda903cb4c3`. These identifiers make the diagnostic reproducible.

| Reference answer used | Mean native reward | Reference tests | Native mutation result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authors' original answer | 1.00 | 11 pass | 12/12 killed |
| Same answer with direct self-comparison tests | 0.25 | 12 pass | Skipped by static gate |
| Same tests expressed through a variable alias | 1.00 | 12 pass | 12/12 killed |

To reproduce in a temporary copy, append this property to the reference `solution/test_properties.py`, then run the unchanged native grader through Harbor's oracle agent:

```python
@CI_SETTINGS
@example(Version(1, 2, 3))
@given(valid_versions)
def test_version_reflexivity(version):
    assert version == version
    assert version <= version
    assert version >= version
```

For the equivalent passing control, assign `same_version = version` inside the function and use `same_version` as each comparison's left operand. The grader's `is_self_comparison` compares operand syntax trees; its `no_self_comparison` gate blocks mutation testing for the direct form. The documented task contract does not prohibit valid reflexivity properties on overloaded comparisons.

Only `solution/test_properties.py` in the two temporary diagnostic copies changed. The official release, the grader and the original evaluation artifacts are preserved. All three diagnostic trials completed without an execution exception. They do not replace the original GLM score or establish whether its answer would pass the mutation threshold.

This grading defect supports the prepared "Some issues" assessment. A separate review-panel allegation of leaked SEO helpers was false: the saved trajectory shows the solver creating those helpers. The supplemental review retains the original opinions and replaces their source-level conclusion with the confirmed grading finding. Editable API verifier imports remain a separate concern without a demonstrated exploit.

Evidence and corrections:

Diagnostic job: `/exedev/skill2env-reflexivity-diagnostic-20261002-145621`. Verified diagnostic archive SHA-256: `356b88a8d0c7da1258fbdd669f63d2592991530509571539d90cadc40535a8bb`. Supplemental review SHA-256: `d27b01d25fd27933a1d25a085e65d89b4209afe778f32261a133f3e83c4de79e`.

Independent code review found two problems in the Atlas contribution: omitted trajectory files during publication, and failure to retire the final Harbor registration. Both were fixed in 8df5a15087. These fixes change Atlas tooling, not the Skill2Env grader. A publisher check now retains all nine referenced Harbor summarization files that were missing.

Eight epoch review dates were repaired using native completion timestamps and matching provider-response creation timestamps. The 573 epoch evidence-retrieval references now record their October 2 hash reverification; their original retrieval times are unknown. Original grades, judge opinions and source artifacts remain preserved. No model or native solver runs were repeated for these metadata corrections.

Corrected primary collection SHA-256: `25028bccfca5c246390665e73d8f5cc22a4c6b84a7ea85f4e15169483f7b2da1`. Original collection SHA-256: `e1c4b0befca4292ac8b0afff16a83c29c08278bf627cf81d769e25002b4545e6`. The corrected collection includes the original collection and correction manifests. Supplemental evidence distinguishes the full 7,496-task release from the runner's three staged tasks.

Publication:

Evidence and the publication plan are retained locally; neither the source nor its rating is live in Atlas. Deployed applet revision 58 contains 9,668 more bytes than the merged package (195,096 versus 185,428), although all seven frontend assets match. Obtain and reconcile its deployed manifest/backend source before replacing the applet.

On publication, add the confirmed grading defect to the source's review pool and `catalog_verifier_issues`. Closing this intake issue does not resolve that defect. Clearing its Atlas flag would require a validated fix and fresh review as separate follow-up work.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Implementation validation</summary>

Implementation validation before the Loom follow-up:

All 61 affected local tests and lint passed at `8df5a15087`. Its 17 applicable CI checks passed, including Marina's database suite; 12 were skipped. The publisher check retains all nine previously omitted referenced trajectory files. Backend-factory, migration and browser execution were not validated locally.

At `cc560d56eb`, documentation lint, an isolated Atlas-page build and the applicable GitHub CI checks passed. The local full-site documentation build failed on `ignore_init_summary` on both this branch and base `3ee6cc3e05`.

The Loom follow-up declares the serialized reward schema with `TypedDict` and marks intentionally unused test-callback arguments. It preserves reward calculation and the JSON fields. The nine directly affected local review tests, required lint and focused type check pass. All 17 applicable CI checks pass at `287291cbb4`, including Marina's database suite. The local affected-test runner requires at least two workers, so the focused tests ran serially with the complete default marker exclusions.

The PR retains concise rationale for the Harbor origin, release pinning, retained runtime dependency, scoring, evaluation limits, Harbor logging options, HTTP client identity and Qwen documentation correction. Longer validation details and the review questions live here.

</details>


</details>



</details>

🤖
# Research

[PR #9518](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9518) is the open Atlas dependency; I found no separate Skill2Env PR. Its catalog refresh reads only MarinSkyRL and Task Trove, while the native review runner accepts Harbor directories but requires MarinSkyRL provenance during generation and publication. The [official Harbor release](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/skill2env/skill2env) supplies task directories with `tests/test.sh`, `tests/rubric.md`, and `solution/solve.sh`; the [Skill2Env repository](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env#license) licenses project-owned code under Apache-2.0 and records separate terms for third-party skill material.

**Relevant code**
- [`catalog.py#L531`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb91eb230b46ad188cb14b23f8c6fecdca4927ae/infra/marina/applets/rl_data_catalog/server/catalog.py#L531) — Task Trove source snapshot.
- [`app.py#L327`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb91eb230b46ad188cb14b23f8c6fecdca4927ae/infra/marina/applets/rl_data_catalog/server/app.py#L327) — two-origin refresh and persistence.
- [`app.js#L69`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb91eb230b46ad188cb14b23f8c6fecdca4927ae/infra/marina/applets/rl_data_catalog/dist/app.js#L69) — fixed catalog tabs and counts.
- [`make_review.py#L900`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb91eb230b46ad188cb14b23f8c6fecdca4927ae/experiments/rl_data_reviews/make_review.py#L900) — Harbor sampling with mandatory MarinSkyRL checkout.
- [`publish_review.py#L118`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb91eb230b46ad188cb14b23f8c6fecdca4927ae/experiments/rl_data_reviews/publish_review.py#L118) — publisher rejects missing MarinSkyRL commit.

# Skill2Env Atlas contribution

## Design

Create `agent/YYYYMMDD-fix-9630` from the latest #9518 head and open a separate PR against that branch. Register one `Skill2Env:skill2env` source row from a pinned Harbor package release, with the package version or digest, exact task count and count method, source and verifier provenance, links to the official Hub and repository, and license information supported by the released package and its source inventory. Resolve the immutable package identifier and enumerate task IDs before coding the row; do not use `latest` or infer a corpus-wide Apache-2.0 license from the code license. Catalog refresh should retain the pinned row without downloading task archives or silently advancing it.

Extend the Atlas origin list, public table and details, and refresh status for Skill2Env. Use the existing source/review tables so changed data or verifier revisions make prior ratings historical. Adapt the Harbor review route and schema to record its actual Harbor checkout, task bytes, and verifier implementation without requiring unrelated MarinSkyRL source provenance. Keep the native `tests/test.sh` result distinct from the qualitative rubric and the three independent reviewer judgments; preserve solver trajectory, verifier output, judge responses, sample IDs, seed, and dated source synthesis through publication.

Run the standard seeded quality sample against the pinned Harbor tasks and publish its rating and evidence. If it is Good, run the same task IDs through the Atlas Small (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct), Large (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B), and Hosted (GLM-5.3) arms under the current protocol enforced by `app.py`; use its judge-verifier variant only if the native verifier calls a model. Record checkpoint identities, generation settings, per-arm solved/verified/attempted counts, and infrastructure failures separately. Publish difficulty only when the protocol matches and the source review remains current. Link the dated Atlas review and dependent implementation PR here.

## Validation and risk

Test the pinned count and links, refresh idempotence, revision-based staleness, Harbor-only provenance and publication, and public filtering. Validate the applet and inspect the public page after publication. Native Harbor execution needs a Docker-capable environment; the first sampled run must establish that the released package and its verifier work before any model comparison. Keep failed executions as evidence and out of solve-rate denominators until their status is resolved.

## Open question

Does the Hub expose an immutable package digest and task-level license metadata for this release? If it exposes only a version tag, archive a task-ID and file-hash manifest with the review so the counted and executed populations can be checked later.

issues.body:
## TL;DR

Legacy Grug SFT runs under `experiments/post_training/long_loop` (PR [#11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120), head `c6676c91ef`) force the step-1 restore check to a permanent checkpoint, save `keep` milestones permanently, and can write the final step twice when it is also a `keep` milestone. Across 17 dated runs on 2026-11-18 under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/long-loop-436/`, this produced 43 native checkpoint prefixes totaling 24,360,070,312,426 bytes (24.36 TB), including 33 prefixes (17,887,983,830,450 bytes, 17.89 TB) in the dated non-one-hour inventory and 10 prefixes (6,472,086,481,976 bytes, 6.47 TB) in the one-hour pair. A manual cleanup deleted 27 intermediate prefixes (16,984 inventoried objects, 11,704,773,554,338 bytes, 11.70 TB of inventoried objects deleted; billed quota relief was not measured).

Most of the mechanism already exists in Levanter and Marin. PR [#5983](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5983) added `keep_last_temporary_checkpoints`, PR [#10782](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10782) applied final-only permanent retention with rolling temporary checkpoints to `SFTSpec`, and PR [#11552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11552) fixed forced final re-saves on `main`. Long-loop legacy Grug SFT needs four changes:

1. Use the existing `save_final_checkpoint` helper and retain `wait_until_finished()` in `sft_runtime/train.py`, and bring in PR [#11552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11552) from `main`.
2. For an unlisted step-1 restore gate, explicitly request a temporary save through the checkpointer, run the non-forced save path, wait for commit, then load from the actual temporary destination. Preserve a named permanent step-1 milestone. The gate copy counts toward rolling retention and can be pruned after enough newer temporary commits or on a permanent commit.
3. Default `sft-smoke.yaml` and long-loop Grug SFT recipes to rolling temporary checkpoints (`keep: null`, time-based `save_interval`, `keep_last_temporary_checkpoints: 2`) plus explicit named permanent steps (`[{"every": s, "until": s}, ...]`) for export and eval milestones.
4. Remove and verify absence of `metadata.json` before deleting payload objects in `Checkpointer._do_rm_checkpoint` so subsequent discovery skips the prefix; abort payload removal if marker removal fails.

## Prior work

| Item | State | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| PR [#4457](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/4457) / Issue [#4456](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4456) | Merged / Closed | Sets default `keep` for `default_train`, `default_sft`, and `default_dpo` to empty so only rolling temporary checkpoints and the final permanent checkpoint are kept. |
| PR [#4387](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/4387) / PR [#5066](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5066) / Issue [#4386](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4386) | Merged / Closed | Adds `temporary_base_path` to `CheckpointerConfig` and routes temporary checkpoints to region-local TTL temp buckets while keeping forced and step-policy saves permanent under `base_path`. |
| PR [#5945](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5945) | Merged | Sets Grug launchers to `keep=None` (final permanent checkpoint plus temporary recovery saves). |
| PR [#5983](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5983) | Merged | Adds `keep_last_temporary_checkpoints` to `Checkpointer` and `CheckpointerConfig`, pruning older temporary checkpoints on commit while deleting all temporary checkpoints when a permanent checkpoint commits. |
| Issue [#5386](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5386) | Open | Tracks resume corruption paired with sparse permanent checkpoints and single-temporary retention losing 8k steps. |
| PR [#9427](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9427) | Merged | Adds on-demand permanent checkpoint requests and lowers hero temporary checkpoint TTL from 14 days to 3 days. |
| PR [#10498](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10498) / Issue [#8290](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8290) | Merged / Closed | Bounds SkyRL RL recovery checkpoints to 2 by default via `SkyRLRetentionPolicy`, protecting pending HF exports and selected best checkpoints. Long-loop RL already uses this in `experiments/post_training/long_loop/rl.py:62` (`retained: 3` in `specs/rl.yaml:4`). |
| Issue [#10453](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10453) | Open | Documents TensorStore chunk-layout failures when resuming into a root that still contains uncommitted partial checkpoint directories. |
| PR [#10774](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10774) | Merged | Commits the completed step on SIGTERM preemption before exit in Grug trainers. |
| PR [#10782](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10782) | Merged | Sets `SFTSpec.checkpointer` to `save_interval=30m`, `keep=None`, `keep_last_temporary_checkpoints=1` in `experiments/sft/launcher.py:601-605`, routing recovery saves to Marin's 14-day TTL scratch prefix. |
| PR [#11217](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11217) | Merged | Sets hero SFT (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_hero_sft.py`) to save permanent checkpoints every 500 steps alongside hourly temporary checkpoints. |
| PR [#11552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11552) / Issue [#11534](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11534) | Merged / Open | Makes `Checkpointer.on_step(..., force=True)` wait for and reuse a pending or committed permanent save from the same checkpointer and step instead of rewriting `step-N/`. Merged to `main` on 2026-11-17 (`bc25c57f14`), absent from PR [#11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120) (`c6676c91ef`). |

## Current behavior in long-loop SFT

All line citations below refer to PR [#11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120) at `c6676c91ef` unless noted as `main` (`ea1257ca8d`).

Long-loop SFT has two launch paths in `experiments/post_training/long_loop/spec_pipeline.py:122-133`:

1. Shared `SFTSpec` path (`shared_sft.py:105-122`): inherits `SFTSpec.checkpointer` from `experiments/sft/launcher.py:601-605` (PR [#10782](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10782)): 30-minute rolling temporary checkpoint (`keep_last_temporary_checkpoints=1`), `keep=None` (permanent final checkpoint only), temporary root resolved via `apply_output_path` (`lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:243`).
2. Legacy Grug path (`sft.py:40-85`, `sft-smoke.yaml`, `sft_runtime/train.py`), used by the 2026-11-18 Snowball ablations and the live eight-hour arms:
   - **Paths (`sft.py:53-56`)**: sets `base_path = <output>/checkpoints` and `temporary_base_path = <output>/temporary-checkpoints`. Sets `load_checkpoint = False` and `load_checkpoint_path = []`, which disables own-root resume (`experiments/grug/checkpointing.py:162-163`; an empty list also overrides `TrainerConfig.checkpoint_search_paths` at `lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py:968` so auto-resume requires `load_checkpoint_path = None`).
   - **Default schedule (`sft-smoke.yaml:8059,8073-8089`)**: enables `save_checkpoints: true`, `keep: [{every: 15}]`, `save_interval: 30m`, `delete_old_temp_checkpoints: true`, `keep_last_temporary_checkpoints: 2`. Every 15th step is permanent (`is_temporary: false`) under `<output>/checkpoints/step-N`.
   - **First-step restore gate (`sft_runtime/train.py:204-217,1526-1530`)**: when `first_checkpoint_restore_step` is set (set to `1` in all 17 runs on 2026-11-18 and in the three eight-hour configs), `restore_first_checkpoint` calls `checkpointer.on_step(tree=state, step=step, force=True)` at `train.py:208` and reloads from `checkpointer.base_path` at `train.py:212`. Because `force=True` sets `my_save_permanent_ckpt = True` (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py:622-623`), `step-1` is written as a permanent checkpoint in `checkpoints/step-1` and is not pruned.
   - **Per-step checkpointer call (`sft_runtime/train.py:1542`)**: calls `checkpointer.on_step(tree=state, step=current_step)`. In `Checkpointer.on_step` (`checkpoint.py:628-633`), `step % current_every == 0` takes precedence over `save_interval` and saves a permanent checkpoint under `base_path`; time-policy saves go to `temporary_base_path` with `is_temporary=True` (`checkpoint.py:652-655`).
   - **What is deleted (`checkpoint.py:659-665,718-740,768-779`)**: after a temporary checkpoint commits, rank 0 prunes older temporary checkpoints beyond `keep_last_temporary_checkpoints` via a background `fs.rm(plain_path, recursive=True)` thread. After any permanent checkpoint commits, rank 0 calls `_prune_temporary_checkpoints(0)` to delete all tracked temporary checkpoints. This pruning path only removes temporary checkpoints. The frozen inventories quantify permanent checkpoint prefixes; the cited base-start and eight-hour configs disable time-based saves, while the one-hour configs allow them at `1h`. The inventories do not establish an absence of temporary writes across all runs.
   - **Why the final save is doubled (`train.py:1542,1570-1571`, `checkpoint.py:609`)**: when the final step matches `keep`, the periodic call (`train.py:1542`) already writes it. The later forced call (`train.py:1570`) on the pinned legacy source can rewrite it because PR [#11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120) lacks PR [#11552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11552) (`main` `checkpoint.py:618-621`) and line 609 (`if step == self._last_save_step and not force: return`) does not return when `force=True`. The observed doubled finals are consistent with a second OCDBT generation in the same `step-N/` directory. Use the existing `save_final_checkpoint` helper (`checkpoint.py:756-761`) and retain `wait_until_finished()`. PR [#11552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11552) independently makes the forced path on `main` reuse a pending or committed permanent save from the same checkpointer and step. Neither guard prevents a rewrite across a new process or resume.
   - **Other retention hooks**: `BestValidationCheckpoint` (`sft_runtime/validation_checkpoint.py:89-92`) deletes older parameter-only validation checkpoints under `eval.best_checkpoint_path` when enabled. `archive.py:100-142` (`checkpoint_cleanup`) only runs in post-archive cleanup after verified HF publication.

## 2026-11-18 storage evidence and projected savings

At 2026-11-19 01:22:06Z, shared `cw-us-east-02a` STANDARD storage reported 971,569,804,211,080 bytes used of 1,000,555,581,276,160 bytes quota (28.99 TB headroom, zone/storage-class level; receipt `048e21ad`). Across 17 dated long-loop training runs under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/long-loop-436/` (excluding six post-hoc BF16 downcast roots), three frozen inventories account for 43 native checkpoint prefixes:

| Cohort (frozen snapshot) | Runs | Prefixes | Actual bytes | Superseded intermediate bytes (exact) | Failed step-1-only bytes (exact) | Doubled-final excess (est.) | Single-gen retained incl. failed-run step 1 (est.) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Dated non-one-hour inventory (`7a10d9c8`, 15 runs) | 15 | 33 | 17,887,983,830,450 (17.89 TB) | 6,988,863,920,962 (6.99 TB, 18 prefixes) | 401,190,894,951 (0.40 TB, 1 prefix) | 5,113,836,902,455 (5.11 TB, 13 finals) | 5,785,283,007,033 (5.79 TB) |
| One-hour FP32 pair (control + treatment) | 2 | 10 | 6,472,086,481,976 (6.47 TB) | 4,314,718,738,425 (4.31 TB, 8 prefixes) | 0 | 1,078,690,430,031 (1.08 TB, 2 finals) | 1,078,677,313,520 (1.08 TB) |
| Combined 2026-11-18 training cohort | 17 | 43 | 24,360,070,312,426 (24.36 TB) | 11,303,582,659,387 (11.30 TB, 26 prefixes) | 401,190,894,951 (0.40 TB, 1 prefix) | 6,192,527,332,486 (6.19 TB, 15 finals) | 6,863,960,320,553 (6.86 TB) |

Evidence fingerprints: 33-prefix inventory `7a10d9c8`, 27-prefix cleanup inventory `10f82be8`, one-hour step-15/60 inventory `ac410e45`, cleanup delete result `111df195`, quota snapshot `048e21ad`, byte-accounting artifact `daf14dfa`.

Notes on measurements and estimates:
- Measured single-save sizes on 67B Snowball: E12 FP32 runs (`params=float32`) are 539.34 GB (doubled final 1,078.68 GB, ratio 2.000); base-start BF16 runs are 401.19 GB (doubled final 802.39 GB, ratio 2.000); E12 BF16 runs are 270.33 GB (doubled final 540.66 GB, ratio 2.000). The one non-doubled completed final (`carried-replay-v9-eager` step 2, where `2 % 15 != 0`) was 270.33 GB (ratio 1.000 vs step 1).
- The 27-prefix manual delete (16,984 inventoried objects deleted, 11,704,773,554,338 bytes, 11.70 TB; billed quota relief not measured) equals the 26 superseded intermediate prefixes across the 16 completed runs (11,303,582,659,387 bytes: 16 `step-1` = 6.46 TB, 4 base-start `step-15` = 1.60 TB, 6 one-hour `step-15/30/45` = 3.24 TB) plus the 1 `step-1` prefix from the failed `base-start-20261118/control` run (401,190,894,951 bytes).
- For a doubled final we use the same run's step-1 size as a single-generation proxy. The inventories do not isolate bytes by generation.
- At a successful final commit and after pruning, the proposed policy would avoid retaining about 17.50 TB across this cohort (12.10 TB on the 33-prefix subset), assuming the listed intermediates are all dispensable. This is post-prune retained footprint, not cumulative writes or billed relief. The 0.40 TB failed-run save is included in the retained estimate until lifecycle cleanup.
- For the three live eight-hour FP32 arms (config sets `first_checkpoint_restore_step=1`, `save_interval=null`, `keep=[{every: 120, until: 240}, {every: 480, until: null}]` on a source without PR [#11552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11552)), estimated native checkpoint storage after successful completion is 5 single-save equivalents per arm (step 1 + step 120 + step 240 + 2x step 480, about 2.70 TB per arm, 8.09 TB across three arms), excluding exports and temporary overlap. This estimate counts the forced step-1 save separately from the earlier 6.47 TB planning figure (4 saves per arm). With a temporary step-1 save and single final write, estimated post-prune native checkpoint storage drops to steps 120, 240, and 480 (3 x 539.34 GB, about 1.62 TB per arm, 4.85 TB across three arms), avoiding about 1.08 TB per arm (3.24 TB total).

## Proposed rolling-checkpoint policy

Existing PRs cover most of the design: PR [#5983](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5983) provides rolling temporary retention (`keep_last_temporary_checkpoints`), PR [#10782](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10782) provides the `SFTSpec` default, and PR [#11552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11552) fixes the forced final double-save on `main`. No existing PR wires these rules into the legacy Grug long-loop path or makes deletion metadata-first.

Proposed behavior for long-loop Grug SFT:

1. **Named permanent steps for export and eval**:
   - Declare milestone steps explicitly (for example `[120, 240, 480]`) and encode them for `CheckpointerConfig.keep` as `[{"every": s, "until": s} for s in sorted(set(steps))]`. Because `Checkpointer._get_current_step_save_interval` (`checkpoint.py:745`) selects the first interval with `until >= step`, for strictly increasing positive steps `s_1 < ... < s_k`, each interval `(every=s_i, until=s_i)` matches `step == s_i` and no step in `(s_{i-1}, s_i)`. No Levanter schema change is needed to represent arbitrary named steps.
   - Default `sft-smoke.yaml` and runs without named milestones to `keep: null` (final permanent checkpoint only).
2. **Rolling temporary recovery checkpoints**:
   - Set `save_interval: 30m` (or `60m` for multi-hour runs), `delete_old_temp_checkpoints: true`, and `keep_last_temporary_checkpoints: 2` for multi-hour runs (`1` for short runs where losing one interval is acceptable).
   - Route `temporary_base_path` to a same-region short-TTL prefix (for example `tmp/ttl=3d/...` matching PR [#9427](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9427), or `<output>/temporary-checkpoints` when `<output>` is already under a short TTL). Never route across regions.
   - For resumable runs, set `load_checkpoint: null` and `load_checkpoint_path: null` so `TrainerConfig.checkpoint_search_paths` searches both `base_path` and `temporary_base_path`.
3. **Temporary first-step restore gate**:
   - For an unlisted step-1 restore gate, explicitly request a temporary save through the checkpointer (`request_checkpoint(CheckpointRetention.TEMPORARY)`), run the non-forced `on_step` path, wait for commit, then load from the actual temporary destination (`temporary_base_path or base_path`). Preserve a named permanent step-1 milestone. The gate copy counts toward rolling retention and can be pruned after enough newer temporary commits or on a permanent commit.
4. **Single final permanent write**:
   - Use the existing `save_final_checkpoint` helper and retain `wait_until_finished()` at `sft_runtime/train.py:1570-1571`, and bring in PR [#11552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11552) from `main` so the forced path also reuses a pending or committed permanent save from the same checkpointer and step.

## Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mechanism | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Resume while a delete is in progress or crashed mid-delete | `Checkpointer._do_rm_checkpoint` (`checkpoint.py:768-779`) runs `fs.rm(plain_path, recursive=True)` on a background thread. Recursive removal may delete data objects before the metadata marker. If a process dies mid-delete, `metadata.json` can remain while payload objects are missing. Resume fallback (`experiments/grug/checkpointing.py:184`) only catches `FileNotFoundError`, so a TensorStore read failure aborts resume. | Remove and verify absence of `metadata.json` before deleting payload objects so subsequent discovery (`checkpoint.py:1249-1250`, `checkpointing.py:86-88`) skips the prefix. Abort payload removal if marker removal fails. This does not protect a reader that already selected the checkpoint. Keep writes and deletes to a reused step prefix serialized. |
| Selection file naming a rolled or deleted step | External scripts or mismatched `selected.json` files can point to an intermediate step that was later pruned (seen on 2026-11-18 when two historical one-hour `selected.json` files pointed to `step-15`). | Keep temporary checkpoints strictly in `temporary-checkpoints/` with `is_temporary: true` and permanent milestones in `checkpoints/` with `is_temporary: false`. Preserve and enforce the `is_temporary is False` guard in `sft.py:75,95` and `shared_sft.py:142` across all export, eval, and selection writers so no selection file can bind a temporary checkpoint. Declare export/eval steps in `keep` upfront. |
| Uncommitted partial checkpoint directories on resume | Issue [#10453](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10453): a crash mid-save leaves partial TensorStore files without `metadata.json`; re-saving that step after resume can fail with a chunk-layout mismatch. | Rolling retention does not prevent this. Keep `temporary_base_path` on a short TTL and track [#10453](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10453) separately (or clean uncommitted dirs above the restored step on resume). |
| Transient peak storage above `N` checkpoints | Commit-before-prune holds `N` retained copies while writing the next save. One in-flight save can temporarily add a third 539 GB copy (about 1.62 TB for two retained copies plus one write), before permanent milestones and any delete backlog. Async deletion can lag or fail, so this is not a hard peak bound. | Size storage headroom gates for `N + 1` temporary saves plus planned permanent milestones and delete-backlog margin, or set `N = 1` when headroom is tight. |
| Failed runs leaving orphaned temporary checkpoints | If a run dies before committing a permanent checkpoint and is not resumed, `_prune_temporary_checkpoints` never runs again. | Place `temporary_base_path` under a same-region short TTL prefix (`tmp/ttl=3d/` or `tmp/ttl=14d/`) so orphaned temporary checkpoints expire automatically. |

## Open decisions

1. Default `keep_last_temporary_checkpoints` for multi-hour long-loop SFT runs: `2` (one extra retained copy of about 539 GB in FP32) or `1` (matches `SFTSpec` default in PR [#10782](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10782)).
2. Keep `first_checkpoint_restore_step = 1` as a temporary save on every run, or restrict it to smoke/qualification runs.
3. Land the `metadata.json`-first deletion fix in `lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py` on `main` separately from the legacy long-loop change against the prototype branch (`benfeuer/long-loop-prototype`).

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Measured result: the doubled final save cost about 0.54 TB per eight-hour run (November 19, UTC).

## What happened

Two eight-hour Snowball SFT runs (480 updates each, from 10/05) wrote their final step-480 checkpoint twice. In the control run, the step-480 prefix held 1,271 objects and 1.079 TB, which is two full writes. About 0.54 TB of it is not referenced by the checkpoint manifest. The second run (single-use) showed the same doubled step-480 write. The one-hour runs showed the same pattern at their final step 60.

## Cause

At the end of training, `sft_runtime/train.py` calls `checkpointer.on_step(..., force=True)`. In this branch, `on_step` skips a same-step save only when `force=False`. So the forced final call writes a second version of a step that was already saved. Readers are not affected, because they read through `manifest.ocdbt`. The old data files stay in storage, unreferenced.

## Fix

Commit `6164fcbd` replaces the forced `on_step` call with `save_final_checkpoint` and adds a test in `lib/levanter/tests/test_checkpoint.py`. Its code was reviewed. It is in [PR 11737](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11737). Runs from the pre-train base launched today use this source. Runs already launched from the earlier source were not changed.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Read this before running SFT on TPU

- **Measured throughput** at 8k context: 266 positions/s per chip on v4-128 (64 chips), 242 on v4-256 (128 chips). TPU is not faster than H100.
- **An E12-size arm** (15 updates × 8.39M positions) takes ≈2 h of compute on v4-128 at that rate (arithmetic), against 11–31 min measured on 64 H100.
- **A 150-update arm** is ≈11–12 h on v4-256 (estimate from the 8k rate). Slices below v4-256 are not practical for real arms.
- **Use TPU as an overflow venue** when H100s are blocked, not for speed.
- **Both attention fixes are required:** PR 11506 (packed rows with context parallelism fail to compile without it) and PR 11507 (without it, local-window layers silently train as full attention, so the run trains a different model).
- **Not yet qualified on TPU:** 262,144-token rows (the recipe's length; only 8k has run), checkpoint restore, and any quality match against H100. A matched TPU-vs-H100 run is in progress.

## Summary

Snowball (67B MoE) long-loop SFT now trains on TPU v4. A 20-update run on a v4-128 slice (64 chips) finished on 2026-11-15 with finite losses and a written checkpoint. This issue records what works, what was fixed, and what is still unproven, so others can use the TPU cluster for SFT.

## Result

Setup: long-loop SFT recipe, 16 hosts x 4 chips (v4-128), small test batch of 131,072 token positions per update. Init: the Snowball **pretraining** base (long-context checkpoint at step 157,000), not the 10/05 SFT model. This is checked in the code for the 1-update window-fix run, the 20-update v4-128 run and the later 20-update v4-256 run. The fit-proxy row's code was not re-checked.

| Run | Updates | Outcome |
|---|---:|---|
| Fit proxy (all layers global attention) | 1 | Succeeded, 8.99 chip-hours |
| Real recipe with window fix | 1 | Succeeded, 9.14 chip-hours |
| Real recipe with window fix | 20 | Succeeded, 15.04 chip-hours |

Measured on the 20-update run:

- 7.70 s per update in steady state, 17,029 token positions per second (266 per chip).
- End to end 847 s, including compile (about 33-36 s) and checkpoint write.
- Checkpoint: 801 GB in 584 objects; write and drain took 191 s.
- 20 finite loss rows; all 16 hosts succeeded.

## Fixes needed to get there

- **Segment IDs were sharded differently from the query inputs** under context parallelism, which failed at trace time (`Invalid shape for q segment_ids: (8192,). Expected: (2048,)`). Fix: PR 11506 (draft).
- **TPU Splash attention ignored the per-layer local window**, so local layers ran full causal attention. A 2-layer CPU probe showed a max logit difference of 6.4e-3 against the reference, and 1.5e-7 after the fix. Tracked in issue 11502; fix for the long-loop branch in PR 11507 (draft). The same pattern exists in other model files on main.
- **`mixture_block_size` must divide the stage start index.** The data config value is sized for batch 256; a small batch needs a smaller block.

## Limits

- **Not a matched speed comparison.** Three unrelated 64-H100 SFT arms measured 1,044-2,907 positions per second per H100, against 266 per v4 chip here. The TPU run used a small untuned batch, and nothing was measured per dollar.
- **Only v4-128 was tried.** Scaling to v4-512 or larger is not measured.
- **No TPU-trained checkpoint has been evaluated.** Equal quality to an H100-trained checkpoint is not shown.
- The per-host sharding dump and actual dtypes were not captured in the first runs.

## Next steps

- [ ] One run of at most 1 hour on the largest available v4 slice with the full recipe batch; report positions per second in total and per chip.
- [ ] One matched SFT arm on TPU and on H100, scored on the same evals.
- [ ] Land the two fix pull requests and close the remaining model-file issue:
  - #11506 (segment IDs under context parallelism, against main)
  - #11507 (per-layer local windows in TPU Splash attention, against the long-loop branch)
  - #11502 (same window bug in the Grug models on main, still open)
- [ ] If both hold, document the TPU SFT launch path next to the long-loop recipe.

## Corrections

- 2026-11-17: init was misstated as the 10/05 checkpoint. The TPU runs started from the Snowball pretraining base (step 157,000).

🤖 **PARTIAL result: Snowball TPU SFT on one v4-256 slice (128 chips), 20 updates.** The per-rank artifacts are not yet reviewed (listed at the end).

**Setup.** v4-256 = 32 hosts × 4 chips, one slice in us-central2-b, production priority, no retries. Changes from the earlier v4-128 run (64 chips, batch 16 × 8,192, accumulation 1, which ran clean): batch **256 × 8,192** (the recipe's 256 sequences, at 8k context), gradient accumulation 8 (still one sequence per data replica per microbatch), and the recipe's mixture block of 64,000. Unchanged from that run: model, base checkpoint, ring MoE, MuonH, the configured FP32 stored parameters with BF16 compute, and context axis 4. Configured mesh: data 32 × context 4, one slice, no DCN axis. The actual per-rank dtypes and sharding are not yet read.

**Observed:**

| | |
|---|---|
| Tasks | 32/32 succeeded on the first attempt; no retry, no preemption of our job |
| Losses | all 20 finite: 0.833 at update 1, 0.657–0.764 over updates 11–20 (different minibatches under warmup, so not a convergence claim) |
| Steady step time, updates 4–20 | **67.6 s** (range 67.46–68.07 s), rank-0 logged duration |
| Throughput | **31,021 positions/s** total, **242 per chip**. This is a nominal position rate, 2,097,152 positions over the rank-0 logged duration; all-rank timing is still pending. The v4-128 run gave 266 per chip at batch 16 without accumulation. The chip count, batch and accumulation all changed together, so this is not a scaling law. |
| First update | logged duration 120.6 s (includes the first-step compile). Placement to the start of update 1 was about 7.8 min, and placement to its logged completion (15:51:13Z) about 9.8 min. |
| Checkpoint at update 20 | 801.07 GB in 760 objects (storage listing). All 32 hosts started saving in the same second and logged the commit barrier complete about 95 s later (log timestamps). The v4-128 run took 191 s with 16 writers. This shows the writes and the barrier, not restore or full tensor integrity. |
| Cost | **70.62 chip-hours**; 33 min end to end |

**Not yet reviewed:** the 32 per-rank timing journals (the all-rank compute range and the drain spans), the 64 compiled-memory reports, the 32 per-rank dtype/sharding reports, and the contents of the checkpoint metadata and manifest. The files exist; reading and checking them is pending. The numbers above come from task records, rank-0 metric logs, log timestamps and storage listings.

**Not established:** checkpoint restore, model quality, 32k context, or equivalence with the H100 recipe (which runs 32,768-token sequences, so 4× more positions per update).

**Next, an estimate:** a real 150-update C-recipe arm on v4-256 needs three things: the C config in the TPU entry point (its MuonH grouping, the 10/05 base in us-central2, the C mixture); 32k context qualified on TPU; and either checkpoint restore qualified or the whole run fitting in one job. Arithmetic only: **if** the measured 8k rate of 31,021 positions/s held at 32k (untested), one full-size update of 8.39M positions would take about 270 s, and 150 updates about 11.25 h of compute, plus startup and checkpoints. This is not an expected 32k runtime: throughput and memory at 32k context are not qualified.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Two TPU attention bugs in the SFT path, in plain English. Both block SFT on TPU. The fixes are open as draft PRs.

```
local layer:   each token sees only the last 2,048 tokens   [.....####]
global layer:  each token sees everything before it         [#########]
the model alternates them across depth; both stay inside one packed document
```

## PR 11507: local layers silently ran as global layers
- **What the model does:** some layers look only at a recent window of tokens (local) and others look at everything before (global). The runtime picks the window per layer inside a scanned loop.
- **What went wrong on TPU:** the TPU attention kernel (Splash) reads only a fixed mask. It ignored the per-layer window, so every local layer ran full causal attention.
- **How you would notice:** you would not. Nothing fails; training runs and the loss looks normal.
- **Does it block SFT?** Yes. A TPU run silently trains a different model: full causal attention in the local layers.
- **The fix:** build two fixed masks, local and global, and pick one per layer from the existing global flag. Document boundaries in packed rows are still kept.
- **Still unfixed:** Grug models on main use the same pattern (issue 11502 stays open). This PR covers only the long-loop SFT runtime.
- **Test evidence:** a two-layer CPU Splash-interpreter regression matches an independent reference to under 1e-6 (max abs logit difference). It fails if local attention is replaced by full causal. In issue 11502's probe the unfixed path differed by 6.36e-3, and the fixed masks by 1.49e-7.

## PR 11506: document IDs mis-sharded under context parallelism
- **What the model does:** many documents are packed into one long row. Segment IDs stop a token attending across a document boundary. With context parallelism, each chip holds a slice of the row.
- **What went wrong on TPU:** queries were split across chips, but their segment IDs were not. At context parallelism 4 each chip got 2,048 queries and 8,192 segment IDs.
- **How you would notice:** it fails at trace time, before any step runs.
- **Does it block SFT?** Yes: packed rows with context parallelism above 1 cannot run on TPU.
- **The fix:** split the query segment IDs the same way as the queries, and align the key segment IDs with the gathered keys.
- **Test evidence:** CPU-interpreter tests compare packed outputs at context parallelism 4 against context parallelism 1, for causal and sliding-window masks. A negative control removes document masking and must differ. The attention module passes 15 tests, with 1 TPU-only test skipped.

**What has run on TPU:** the code that ran on TPU has the same attention and model files as the PR branches (identical file contents). That code ran in a 1-update smoke and in two 20-update runs (64 and 128 chips, context parallelism 4) without error. The TPU runs also carried changes that are not in these PRs (the TPU launcher and a weights-first model init), and the PR test files differ slightly. The evidence that the outputs are numerically correct is CPU-interpreter only. No TPU-trained model has been compared with its H100 twin yet; that is in progress.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Closing as a finished status record.

## Final status

- **Works:** Snowball long-loop SFT trains on TPU v4 at 8k context. The 20-update runs on v4-128 and v4-256 finished with finite losses and written checkpoints.
- **Fixes landed:** PR 11506 and PR 11507 both merged on 2026-11-17 (the body above still calls them drafts). Issue 11502 is closed.
- **Speed:** 242 to 266 positions per second per v4 chip at 8k context. TPU is an overflow venue, not a faster one.

## Not done, and not planned

- No run at the recipe's 262,144-token row length on TPU.
- No checkpoint restore test on TPU.
- No matched TPU-versus-H100 arm scored on the same evals, so equal quality is not shown.
- No launch documentation for TPU SFT.

The post-training ablations moved to H100 once capacity was available. Reopen this issue, or open a new one, if SFT on TPU is needed again; the four items above are the starting list.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
🤖 A multi-node vLLM data-parallel serve can die during startup when flashinfer downloads a cubin header on a cold node. One worker holds the download lock longer than 30 s, the other workers on that node give up, and the engine fails with `AssertionError: flashInferMetaInfo.h not found`. The other engines then wait forever, and every Iris task still reads `running`.

This affects any DP serve that starts on a node with an empty flashinfer cache, not only the Mochi serve where we saw it.

Reproduce (intermittent; depends on download speed):
1. Start the Mochi SFT serve (DP16 EP, 4 x GB200x4, cw-us-east-08a, flashinfer 0.6.18.post1) on nodes with an empty `/root/.cache/flashinfer`.
2. During `capture_model(profile_only=True)`, the four workers on one node fetch `fmha/trtllm-gen/include/flashInferMetaInfo.h`.

Expected: every worker gets the header and the serve becomes ready.

Observed on 2026-11-16 (log excerpt in a [secret gist](https://gist.github.com/karansag/528ef1da72eee0721d8342081e97e77f)):
- 22:41:58 DP11 acquired the lock and began the download from the NVIDIA cubin CDN.
- 22:42:29–22:42:34 DP8, DP10 and DP9 logged `Failed to acquire lock … within 30 seconds`, then asserted. The engine core for that node failed with `Worker failed with error 'flashInferMetaInfo.h not found'`.
- DP12 on another node also hit the lock timeout but survived, so the failure depends on timing.
- The two earlier serves of the same model and image came up normally.

Cause: in flashinfer `jit/cubin_loader.py`, `download_file` waits a fixed 30 s for the per-file lock (`lock_timeout=30`, not configurable through callers). On timeout it returns `False`, `get_artifact` returns empty bytes, and `jit/attention/modules.py` fails `assert metainfo`. Upstream [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3507](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3507) reports duplicate concurrent downloads. [PR 6461](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6461) makes waiting workers reuse a finished download, but the 30 s timeout still returns `False`.

Possible fixes, from least to most change:
- Prefetch the needed cubins once per node before the vLLM workers start, or point `FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR` at a prefilled directory.
- Install the `flashinfer-cubin` package in the serve image so no download happens; `FLASHINFER_NO_DOWNLOAD` then turns a missing file into a clear error ([TRT-LLM notes](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/docs/source/llm-api/index.md#flashinfer-jit-workspaces-for-mpi-workers)).

Cost of this occurrence: 3.61 GB200-hours. Related: issue 11536.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 waits only 30 seconds for the per-artifact lock; a timeout returns no header and aborts worker startup. Marin has two GPU launch paths: `--task-image` uses the image's preinstalled vLLM, while the isolated CUDA launcher installs vLLM and compiler packages but no matching FlashInfer cubin wheel. The [0.6.18.post1 release](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/v0.6.18.post1) provides a 1.56 GB cubin wheel; [FlashInfer's installation guidance](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/docs/installation.rst) requires a wheel matching `flashinfer-python`. No open Marin PR overlaps this issue.

**Relevant code**
- [`iris_cli.py#L171-L176`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris_cli.py#L171-L176) — task images select preinstalled vLLM.
- [`vllm_server.py#L145-L158`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/vllm_server.py#L145-L158) — preinstalled launcher uses image dependencies.
- [`vllm_server.py#L222-L245`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/vllm_server.py#L222-L245) — isolated CUDA install omits cubins.

# Proposed Fix

1. Identify the failed serve's task image digest and launcher. In that exact runtime, record `flashinfer show-config`, `flashinfer-python`/`flashinfer-cubin` versions, and whether `fmha/trtllm-gen/include/flashInferMetaInfo.h` is packaged. This determines which launch path needs the first change.
2. Put the version-matched cubin wheel in the GPU task image during its build, or provision it before vLLM starts for the isolated CUDA path. Use FlashInfer's wheel index or `flashinfer download-kernels`; PyPI's `flashinfer-cubin` is stale. Pin the version and verify the header is available with an empty runtime cache. Cover both launch paths if both can run multi-worker GPU serves.
3. On one cold GB200x4 node, start four workers concurrently and verify readiness without a cubin CDN fetch. Then run the DP16/EP configuration once and verify all engines become ready. If one worker fails, verify the Iris job reaches a terminal failure instead of leaving every task `running`; fix failure propagation if that check fails.

The GPU task-image build is not in this repository, and this plan requires a cold-cache GPU validation, so a Marin-only launcher edit would not establish a fix for the reported serve.
