issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
The Snowball long-loop prototype in PR 11120 (SFT, then async RLOO RL, then Micro210 eval, then archive) cannot yet run ablations from the 10/05 SFT cooldown checkpoint, and several of its stages would make an ablation campaign unreliable. This issue lists every problem found in a read-only review of PR 11120 at [`9e1c63cc9c`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop). Each item was re-checked from code, specs, storage listings and Iris state. Nothing was launched. Paths below are relative to `experiments/post_training/long_loop/`.

Notes, a per-claim verification table and the corrections it produced: [gist](https://gist.github.com/karansag/46431ff7905e2ece8234e7aee311861c).

## Starting checkpoint

1. **The launcher rejects SFT checkpoints it did not produce itself, so it cannot start from the 10/05 release.** The 10/05 weights are usable; only the loop's bookkeeping files are missing. The release is `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05` @ `ac60d940`: 4,750 SFT updates from base step 157000 to 161750, with the LR decayed to 0.1x over the last ~475 steps. It has the same base as the loop. [`verify_adopted_sft`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/adopted_sft.py#L23-L75) requires `selected.json`, a consumed config whose model block equals the loop recipe, a lineage JSON and a payload inventory. Only `metadata.json` and `manifest.json` exist for the native step-161750 checkpoint (GCS us-central2, about 540 GB). A verified HF copy already exists in the compute region: `s3://marin-rno2a/marin/models/grug-datakit-sft-262k-20261005-ac60d940-r1` (52 objects, 39 weight shards).
2. **The loop's own SFT stops before its cooldown.** [`specs/sft.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/sft.yaml#L100) stops at step 746 of a 4,750-step schedule ([L194](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/sft.yaml#L194)), and the decay covers only the final 475 steps ([L60-L82](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/sft.yaml#L60-L82)). The LR stays at 5e-5, and only 3 of 19 data-weight phases (0, 250, 500) run. The result is a truncated SFT on a 10/05-derived mix with reproduction substitutions ([`specs/sft-data.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/sft-data.yaml#L36-L40)), not a cooldown checkpoint. The full-geometry run `long-loop-full-2026.11.09.12` succeeded on 11-10 (32/32 tasks, about 21.1 h on 256 H100).

## Infrastructure

3. **Every stage after SFT is blocked.** For the full spec, RL and archive return four runtime-qualification blockers ([`run_spec.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/run_spec.py#L173-L187), [`specs/rl.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L293-L295), [`specs/agentic.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/agentic.yaml#L29-L30)). RL at 102,400 tokens with CP4 has not been qualified on a real SFT checkpoint.
4. **The pinned revision is stale.** [`specs/round1.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/round1.yaml#L2) pins `6e24f53e`, and [`__main__.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/__main__.py#L66-L75) refuses a local launch from any other revision.
5. **No stage retries or resumes.** Automatic retries and checkpoint resume are off in every recipe: [`sft.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/sft.yaml#L15-L16), [`sft.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/sft.py#L60) (forces `load_checkpoint` off), [`rl.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L42), [`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L21), [`execution.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/execution.yaml#L72). A preemption mid-stage loses that stage. Finished stages are reused, and a finished SFT can be adopted. Issue 11162 describes the same retry setting killing eval drivers on the first Kueue eviction in another harness.
6. **No end-to-end timing.** The coordinator cap is 36 h ([`execution.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/execution.yaml#L75-L79)). The RL job timeout is 9 h ([`rl.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L285)) and the eval job timeout 24 h ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L184)). The measured SFT took about 21.1 h, leaving about 14.9 h. Whether RL, eval and archive fit in that time is unmeasured.
7. **Arms alias each other's outputs.** A stage path is `{prefix}/{name}/{version}` with no config hash ([`lazy.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/lazy.py#L228-L238)). RL and eval take fixed manifest names ([`spec_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/spec_pipeline.py#L158-L160)) and the report is fixed at `long-loop/report` ([`runtime_timing.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime_timing.py#L111)). On changed config at an existing path, the runner logs a warning and serves the cached output ([`artifact.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/artifact.py#L380-L415)).
8. **Eval traces from every arm go to one place.** [`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L93-L94) fixes `output_path` to `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/long-loop/traces/2026.11.09/eval` and `run_id` to `2026.11.09`, and [`evaluation.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/evaluation.py#L270-L279) does not rebind them. RL traces are rebound per run ([`rl.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/rl.py#L154-L169)).
9. **There is no eval-only or RL-resume entry point.** [`__main__.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/__main__.py#L58) offers `sft`, `rl` and `archive`. The only adoption point is after SFT ([`spec_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/spec_pipeline.py#L84-L99)), so re-evaluating an RL checkpoint means re-running RL.
10. **RL keeps every checkpoint.** `ckpt_interval 1` with unlimited retention ([`rl.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L4), [L43](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L43), [L115](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L115)). [`archive_stage.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/archive_stage.py#L96-L110) skips cleanup when W&B or timing evidence is partial. A native 67B checkpoint per RL step accumulates on the shared rno2a quota.
11. **CPU helper stages request 8 H100 each.** The input check, export, eval-input prep and archive stages each declare one 8-H100 replica ([`execution.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/execution.yaml#L1-L64)), counted against the 256-H100 cap.
12. **One missing rollout blocks the report and archive.** The report raises unless every selected path has a verified rollout ([`runtime_timing.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime_timing.py#L88-L97)), and Harbor trial retries are 0 ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L118)). A verified zero score is accepted.
13. **End-to-end timing coverage is unproven.** Native SFT timing is recorded, and the report loads native journals ([`runtime_timing.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime_timing.py#L52-L65)). Stage spans include queue time ([L23-L38](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime_timing.py#L23-L38)). No real end-to-end report has shown complete coverage.
14. **Some admission audits exist only on one laptop.** Runtime dataset payloads have SHA256 checks ([`spec_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/spec_pipeline.py#L40-L53)). The audit annotations in [`agentic.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/agentic.yaml#L15-L17) and [`exclusions.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/exclusions.yaml#L69-L101) point to `/Users/...` paths that nobody else can read.
15. **Inputs and compute are in different regions.** Data, tokenizer and caches are in `marin-us-east-02a`, the archive license is in `marin-us-east-08a`, and compute is pinned to `cw-rno2a` ([`execution.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/execution.yaml#L66-L73)).
16. **The Tau3 exclusion reason is only in code.** [`eval_runtime/profile.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/eval_runtime/profile.py#L52-L54) skips `tau3-pi` (issue 11083). The eval manifest lists 20 paths without Tau3 and without the reason ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L245-L271)).

## Mini and micro evaluation

17. **No usable baseline.** The only result, `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/long-loop/merged-micro-report/2026.11.09.10-post1`, has one verified rollout per benchmark, no repeats and no per-path wall time. It shows the plumbing works, not a score.
18. **Micro210 cannot rank small ablation effects.** The full spec selects 200 tasks and 440 attempts ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L245-L271)), about ±9.8 pp at p = 0.5. Resolving a 2 pp difference needs about 4,800 independent items per arm for a 95% interval, or about 9,800 for 80% power. Paired-item variance is unmeasured.
19. **Settings differ from the EvalDash records, so scores are not comparable.** The loop runs thinking on for every benchmark ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L67-L68)), at T=0.6 and top_p 0.95, with the Pi agent and 65,536/16,384 limits. The EvalDash records for the A3 SFT arm run thinking off for HumanEval+, MBPP+, CRUXEval, MRCR, GSM8K, TriviaQA and IFBench. They use mini-swe-agent for SWE-bench and Terminus-2 for TBLite, TB2 and DS1000, and 32k/8k limits for BFCL, DS1000, TBLite and SWE-bench (MRCR: 4,096-token cap).
20. **TruthfulQA uses a different metric.** Micro210 scores a generated boxed letter 0/1. The policy reports probability-mass MC2.
21. **Six policy benchmarks are missing.** FinanceBench, PIQA, WinoGrande, BoolQ, SOTOPIA-hard and Tau3 are not in the loop's eval.
22. **Tool use is thinly measured.** The full spec selects 10 BFCL tasks (the plumbing report had 1). The audit computes only verified reward, response tokens and stop reasons ([`eval_runtime/audit_results.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/eval_runtime/audit_results.py#L15-L50)), with no tool-call or schema-success metric.
23. **Five of twenty plumbing rows hit the output cap.** CRUXEval, MBPP+, MRCR, TB2 and AIME24 stopped at 16,384 tokens ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L8)).
24. **Eval context is shorter than RL context.** Eval runs at 65,536 tokens with CP 1 ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L7)). RL trains at 102,400 with CP4 ([`rl.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L8)).
25. **Judge variance is unmeasured.** The MiniMax-M3 judge on 8 H100 took 997 s to start and held about 5 H100-h for the 20-row smoke, including queue. Repeat stability is unknown.
26. **Micro210 has no launch path on main.** PR 10817 closed without merging. The loop carries its own runtime in [`eval_runtime/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/eval_runtime), and issue 10933 tracks a main-branch launcher for any model.

Done when:
- The loop can start RL from a pinned, verified HF export, and a short RL smoke from the 10/05 release passes the RL qualification gate.
- RL, eval, report and trace paths are derived from the run, so two arms with different settings cannot share outputs, and changed config at an existing path fails instead of serving the cache.
- SFT and RL resume from their latest checkpoint after preemption, and RL checkpoint retention is bounded.
- An eval-only entry point exists for an existing RL checkpoint.
- The ablation eval set has a measured noise floor (repeats or paired items) and settings matching the EvalDash records, or a stated reason for each difference.
- One end-to-end run reports per-stage active and queue time against the 36 h target.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
🤖 An agent literature survey for the Mochi post-training recipe found two Nemotron-sourced changes for train/inference mismatch in async MoE RL. Mochi RL already uses one of them (router replay). The other, an FP32 LM head, has not been tested by us. Nothing here was measured empirically on Mochi: this is a pointer for the RL team, not a result.

**What Nemotron reports**
- The [Nemotron 3.5 Super/Lightning technical report](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/files/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-and-Lightning-Technical-Report.pdf) (RL section) says router replay plus an FP32 LM head "reduce the KL error between the training and inference engines by more than an order of magnitude". The two are reported together, so the report does not say how much each one contributes.
- Aside: the [HF MoE handbook](https://huggingface-moe-blogpost.hf.space/) says the NeMo-RL recipes for Nemotron 3 Super/Ultra freeze the router matrix in async RL and keep the load-balancing bias live, and that "whether replay pays off in reward is still contested". Router freezing is an alternative or a complement to replay.

**Where Mochi stands (from existing work, not new measurements)**
- Router replay: Mochi (Hero) RL already uses captured-route replay, and it passed the recorded 4K RL gate in https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10388. Its measured replay result is batch-order sensitivity of the gradient: 71.96% → 1.37% at PP48, with +5.3% scoring-plus-update time. That is not a serve-vs-trainer logprob gap, and the same issue notes that serving–trainer differences persist.
- Bit-identical numerics: the stack beginning with https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10634 was closed in favour of score centering with TIS (https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11066, open), with probes in https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10658 (open). The Mochi RL launcher is https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11321 (draft).
- FP32 LM head, serving side: the pinned vLLM fork (`0ac9dcb`) already supports it. `vllm/model_executor/layers/logits_processor.py` reads `--hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "float32"}'` and accumulates the head GEMM into FP32. Its comment says this is "required for RL training-inference consistency". The Mochi serve config (`experiments/evaluation/mochi/model-mochi-sft-step400407.yaml`) does not set it, so served logits are BF16.
- FP32 LM head, trainer side: SkyRL's Megatron wrapper calls the model with `fp32_output=False` (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/workers/megatron/megatron_model_wrapper.py`), so trainer logits are BF16 too. Matching vLLM would need a Megatron-side FP32 output projection, which is not checked here.
- Related Snowball evidence, not RL and not Mochi: in an Oct 25 Levanter-vs-vLLM scoring check on Snowball, silent MoE token drops and BF16 combine weights were each separate numerics boundaries. Fixing them one at a time cut the p99 per-token logprob gap from 3.96 to 0.60 nats.

**What we did not do:** no empirical study on Mochi of the FP32 head, router freezing, or replay versus no replay. The survey proposed a 1 h arm; it moves off our list and into this issue.

Done when: the RL team decides whether to test an FP32 LM head on both engines (vLLM `head_dtype` plus a Megatron FP32 output projection) on Mochi, measured as the serve-vs-trainer logprob or KL gap on fixed responses with replay on, and records the decision here. Router freezing is optional, as a separate arm.

issues.author: cweill
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Synthetic documents that show AI systems choosing aligned actions (Tice et al. 2026, arXiv:2601.10160) shift small Marin-stack models toward aligned answers. The shift generalizes to questions whose documents were held out, and a word-shuffled copy of the documents produces a much smaller shift. We now test whether the effect follows the number of documents, as backdoor poisoning does (Souly et al. 2025), or their fraction of the training tokens. Tice et al. list this question as open. Runs use continued pretraining on Marin's released isoFLOP checkpoints. Status: in progress; one seed per arm so far.

## Description

Related: #11582 (the Data Belay judge scored every safety source "no" with no safety metric in its eval groups). The margin below is a candidate safety metric for small models.

**Metric.** Tice et al. released 4,174 two-choice AI-scenario questions, each with an aligned and a misaligned answer. For each question we compute the mean per-token log-probability of the aligned answer minus that of the misaligned answer, teacher-forced after `{question}\n\nAnswer:`. The "raw margin" is the mean over questions; higher means more aligned. Training documents cover a hash-selected half of the questions. We report the other half as held out.

Small models cannot use Tice et al.'s A/B letter format, so we validated the margin on their released 6.9B base models:

- Their letter-format protocol, rerun by us, reproduces their Table 3 within about 2 SE. Article-split misalignment rates: unfiltered 0.439 (paper 0.447), alignment-upsampled 0.104 (0.092), misalignment-upsampled 0.482 (0.508).
- The raw margin ranks the three models in the same order on both question splits. Article split: +0.053, +0.450, -0.060.
- A calibrated variant subtracts the margin after a question-free `Answer:` prompt. It misses the held-out textbook-split effect, so it is not the primary metric.

**Result 1: from scratch.** d768 Llama (8 layers), 1B DCLM tokens, Marin tokenizer, `train_lm` on one H100, seed 0. 16k aligned documents (about 25M tokens, 2.5%) replace DCLM text, each seen once.

| arm | raw margin, held-out | misaligned rate, held-out | val bpb |
|---|---|---|---|
| control | +0.028 ± 0.016 | 48.2% | 1.2398 |
| aligned documents | +0.216 ± 0.015 | 36.9% | 1.2441 |
| word-shuffled documents | +0.068 ± 0.015 | 46.3% | 1.2404 |

**Result 2: Marin isoFLOP checkpoints, untouched.** Seven DCLM-family checkpoints from 1e18 to 1e20 FLOPs (273M to 1.9B parameters including embeddings). All score 50% on the letter format because each answers one letter regardless of the question. The raw margin stays between +0.06 and +0.09 across sizes, near Tice et al.'s unfiltered 6.9B model (+0.053).

## Hypothesis or Goal

Measure whether the effect of k aligned documents depends on k or on k/N, where N is the number of training tokens, and how this changes with model size.

Design: continued pretraining of the 1e18 d768 checkpoint on N tokens of DCLM with k aligned documents, each seen once. N ∈ {12.5M, 50M, 200M, 800M}; k ∈ {0, 1k, 4k, 16k}; a k=0 control at every N; a word-shuffled control at k=16k, N=200M. The same grid at N ∈ {50M, 200M} then runs on the 3e18 d1024 and 3e19 d1536 checkpoints.

**Predictions, recorded before any results from this grid.** Effect = arm margin minus the k=0 control at the same N, fit as a + b·log(k / N^α). α near 0 means a count law; α near 1 means a fraction law. Our hypothesis: a count law holds when nothing else in the corpus addresses the trait, and a fraction law holds when other documents compete with it. About 7% of DCLM tokens are in documents that mention AI, so we predict α near 1 for this grid. A later grid on AI-filtered DCLM should move α toward 0.

## Status

- Done: metric validation on Tice et al.'s 6.9B models; ladder baselines; from-scratch seed-0 result above.
- Running: the 15-run grid on the 1e18 d768 checkpoint.
- Next: 3e18 and 3e19 grids, then more seeds.

Limitations: one seed per arm; the ± values are standard errors over questions, not seeds. The margin is validated against behavior on three 6.9B models only. Tice et al.'s documents and questions declare no license, so we use them for research and do not redistribute them.

## Links

* Logbook: research branch to follow
* Preregistration: the predictions below were first posted in marin-community/marin-logbooks#65 at 2026-11-18 22:38 UTC, before any continued-pretraining results; that issue's edit history is public.
* W&B runs (public): https://wandb.ai/cweill-self/alignment-dose
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

- Primary metric changed from the calibrated margin to the raw margin after the 6.9B validation, before any continued-pretraining results.
- Widened N from 4x to 64x on the smallest model. The exponent α is estimated with precision proportional to log of the N range.

## Conclusion


---

comments.body:
🤖 **Preregistration for batch 2** (19 continued-pretraining runs), posted before any of them start. These follow a methodology review of batch 1; batch 1 results will be posted separately.

Written 2026-11-19T00:55Z, before any of these runs started. Model: Marin 1e18 d768 isoFLOP checkpoint unless noted.
Effect = held-out raw margin (nats/token) minus the k=0 control with the same N, seed and schedule.
Fit from batch 1 (seed 0, cosine schedule, documents spread uniformly): effect = a + b·ln(k / N^α).

## Held-out point (cosine, uniform placement): N = 800M, k = 1k

- All-cells fit (α = 0.46): predicted effect **+0.048**.
- Fit on N ≤ 200M only (α = 0.39): predicted effect **+0.059**.
- Batch 1 suggests α rises with N, so we expect the observed value at or below +0.048. An observation below +0.035 or
  above +0.070 would mean the log-linear form is misspecified at this dose (0.19% document share).

## Placement under a fixed cooldown (WSD: constant LR, linear decay over the final ~50M tokens at every N)

Arms: k = 4k with all documents inside the final-50M decay window at N = 200M and N = 800M; k = 0 controls under the
same schedule at both N; k = 4k with all documents in the first 50M tokens at N = 200M.

- If recency explains the N-dependence: late-window effects at 200M and 800M are equal within noise (|difference| below
  ~0.02), and the early-window effect at 200M is well below the late-window one.
- If competition with the rest of the corpus explains it: the late-window effect at 800M is smaller than at 200M by
  roughly the amount the uniform runs show (+0.162 at 200M vs +0.117 at 800M, a 0.045 drop).
- We expect recency to explain at least half of the drop.

## Seeds

Two more data-order seeds for k = 0 and k = 4k at N = 50M and N = 200M (cosine, uniform). No directional prediction;
these measure seed-to-seed spread. We expect the spread of effects across seeds to exceed the question-bootstrap SE.

## Model size (3e18 d1024 checkpoint, cosine, uniform)

k = 0 and k = 4k at N = 50M and N = 200M, and k = 16k at N = 200M. Exploratory: these runs can detect only a large
change in α (SE about 0.1–0.15). No directional prediction.

With likelihood scoring, a raw-margin increase alone is not evidence of a directional shift; only the aligned-minus-misaligned difference is. **What this does and does not show.** The fits and the placement result describe the total effect. Whether the directional part follows the same k, N and placement dependence is untested. The margin is a likelihood readout on Tice et al.'s own scenarios in base models, with no post-training. OpenAI's alignment team midtrained an o4-mini-sized model on the same documents and found the effect held on these questions but closed on out-of-distribution chat and agentic evaluations after RL ([How far does alignment midtraining generalize?](https://alignment.openai.com/how-far-does-alignment-midtraining-generalize/), March 2026). This study measures how document count, run length and placement move a near-distribution prior; it does not show that the prior survives post-training. The checkpoints span ~75M–185M non-embedding parameters, so we do not extrapolate to Marin-scale runs. If the recency result holds at larger scale, the relevant length for a Marin run is the anneal or midtraining window, not total pretraining tokens. **Next.** Misaligned-document arms at N = 50M and 800M (k = 4k), to measure how the directional part scales with N. Per-run results will be linked with the research branch. W&B (public): https://wandb.ai/cweill-self/alignment-dose

comments.author: cweill
comments.body: Correction to the update above. The comparison behind "most of the N-dependence is recency" (a drop of 0.045 from N = 200M to 800M with documents spread through the run, against 0.020 with documents in the final 50M tokens) mixes two learning-rate schedules: the spread-out runs used cosine and the end-window runs used WSD. Placement and schedule changed together, so we withdraw the "about 55% of the drop" estimate and the implied α ≈ 0.27. The same-schedule comparison stands: under WSD at N = 200M, documents in the first 50M tokens give +0.076 and documents in the last 50M give +0.198. The missing arms, documents spread through the run under WSD at N = 200M and 800M, would separate placement from schedule.

comments.author: cweill
comments.body: 🤖 **Update: placement at a fixed schedule, and how the directional part scales.** Four more runs: documents spread through the run under WSD at N = 200M and 800M, which closes the gap named in the correction above, and misaligned documents at N = 50M and 800M. _Figure (placement at a fixed schedule; directional part across N)._ **Placement, same schedule.** All runs use WSD (constant LR, then linear decay over the final ~50M tokens); k = 4k aligned documents; effect is measured against the WSD k=0 control at the same N. | N | spread through the run | inside the final 50M | final ÷ spread | |---|---|---|---| | 200M | +0.177 | +0.198 | 1.12 | | 800M | +0.124 | +0.178 | 1.44 | | drop, 200M → 800M | 0.053 | 0.020 | | The schedule does not cause the N-dependence: spread-out documents lose 0.053 under WSD, against 0.045 under cosine. At a fixed schedule, putting the documents in the final decay cuts the loss from 0.053 to 0.020, so recency accounts for about 60% of the N-dependence of the total effect. The advantage of late placement grows with N, as recency predicts. Documents in the first 50M tokens of a 200M run give +0.076. **Directional part across N.** Cosine schedule, documents spread through the run, k = 4k; effect is measured against the cosine k=0 control at the same N. | N | aligned | misaligned | directional (aligned − misaligned) | directional share | |---|---|---|---|---| | 50M | +0.193 | +0.102 | +0.092 | 47% | | 200M | +0.162 | +0.090 | +0.072 | 45% | | 800M | +0.117 | +0.070 | +0.047 | 40% | From N = 50M to 800M the directional part falls to 0.51 of its value, the shared part to 0.68, and the total to 0.60. With documents spread through training, the directional part dilutes faster than the total effect suggests. **Confidence.** Seed 0 for every cell; seed-to-seed SD at two cells is 0.001, and the paired question SE per effect is about 0.007. Placement and the directional part are each measured at one dose (k = 4k), so we report ratios across N, not fitted exponents. Untested: the directional part under late placement, and both at other model sizes. **Implication, at this scale.** For a fixed amount of alignment data, placing it in the final learning-rate decay keeps most of the effect as training gets longer. Spreading it through training loses more, and the directional part loses the most. If this holds at larger scale, the length that matters for a Marin run is the anneal window, not total pretraining tokens, and a document budget should be judged by the aligned-minus-misaligned difference, not the raw margin alone.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Summary

- **Motivation:** TMax-15K is a new set of agentic terminal traces and a candidate for Mochi's SFT mix. We wanted evidence on Snowball before spending Mochi-scale compute on it.
- **Goal:** Find out whether adding TMax agent traces to Snowball's SFT data helps agentic behaviour without hurting tool calling, to decide whether TMax goes into Mochi's SFT mix.
- **Data:** TMax-15K terminal agent traces. The treatment swaps 129 of 480 general SFT windows for one pass of TMax, which is 27.59% of its supervised targets.
- **Method:** Two 15-update SFT runs from the 10/05 SFT, a control and the TMax swap, scored on held-out TMax loss, BFCL ×5 and Micro210.
- **Results:** The TMax run fits held-out TMax traces much better (loss 0.299 against 0.587) but scores lower on BFCL (209/615 against 262/615 with the training template). Micro210 is incomplete: two of the three runs failed.
- **Conclusion:** No clean answer. These runs stored weights in BF16 (issue 11687) and trained on whole traces, not only the assistant turns. The question stays open until a redo with FP32 weights and assistant-only loss.

## Description

TMax-15K is a set of agentic terminal traces (bash plus reasoning). This experiment asks whether adding it to Snowball SFT helps or hurts.

Design:
- Both arms start from the 10/05 SFT and train on the same 480 positions of general SFT data.
- The TMax arm replaces 129 of those windows with one pass of TMax traces, which is 27.59% of its supervised targets.
- 15 updates per arm, 64 H100 each.
- Total supervised targets differ between arms. So this tests a replacement package, not a 10% dose or a pure addition.

Parent: issue 11535.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find whether TMax data improves agentic behaviour without costing tool calling or retention, to decide whether it enters the Mochi SFT mix.

## Status

**Held-out TMax traces** (507 traces from 101 held-out tasks; task-macro loss, lower is better):

| | Parent (10/05) | Control (15 updates) | TMax arm (15 updates) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Held-out loss | 0.613 | 0.587 | 0.299 |

- TMax minus control is −0.288 nats, with interval [−0.308, −0.268].
- 74.5% of the gap is in user and system text, not in the assistant turns.
- The parent and control readouts missed an evaluator gate. So this is a sensitivity readout, not a clean acceptance.

**BFCL ×5 (Pi agent, 123 tasks, 5 runs):**

| Chat template | Parent | Control | TMax arm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Earlier inference template | 313/615 = 50.9% | 249/615 = 40.5% | 193/615 = 31.4% |
| Training template (tools@3f, same as Mochi) | 322/615 = 52.36% | 262/615 = 42.60% | 209/615 = 33.98% |

The two template runs used different runtime versions. So the change between rows cannot be attributed to the template alone.

**Why BFCL drops (earlier-template runs, 615 attempts per model):**

| | Parent | Control | TMax arm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Verifier reports the answer file absent | 66 | 149 | 267 |
| Pass rate among attempts with an answer file | 57.0% | 53.4% | 55.5% |

- **What the verifier saw:** the answer file was absent at evaluation time. It does not establish why. Pi logs from these attempts also contain tool errors, so a write-path failure is not ruled out.
- **The conditional pass rate:** it removes an outcome-dependent failure category. So it is arithmetic, not an adjusted accuracy or a treatment comparison.

**Cost:** training 99.95 H100-h for both arms (45.40 control + 54.56 TMax).

**Pending:** Micro210 on both arms. Results will be posted here as a comment.

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

## Conclusion

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The 15-update TMax replacement has 53 fewer BFCL successes than its matched control with the training template (209/615 versus 262/615). In the earlier-template runs, the verifier found no answer file in 267 treatment attempts versus 149 control attempts; the logs also contain tool errors, so the failure mechanism is unresolved. Held-out TMax loss is lower, but 74.5% of the treatment-control gap is in user/system text and the parent/control readouts missed an evaluator gate. This is an experiment readout, with no isolated repository defect to fix yet.

# Plan

1. Pin both checkpoints, consumed data manifests and target counts, source revisions, and evaluation policy/commands in the [Snowball recipe ledger](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337). Preserve the 27.59% supervised-target share and the unequal total targets as limits on attribution.
2. Finish the matched Micro210 and retention readouts called for in [the parent ablation issue](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535). Report paired task-level and per-benchmark deltas, scored/unscored counts, aggregate scores, and uncertainty under the same harness, tasks, and seeds.
3. Audit BFCL attempts with absent answer files by task and seed. Use the Pi, tool, sandbox, and verifier records to separate model non-completion from tool/write failures, timeouts, and grading failures. Correct confirmed infrastructure failures before rerunning affected attempts under a pinned runtime; keep model failures in the denominator.
4. Repeat the held-out TMax readout with the evaluator gate satisfied and report assistant-turn loss separately. Use BFCL, Micro210, retention, and the corrected loss readout for the carry/drop decision. Do not advance this replacement mix to Mochi while the BFCL deficit remains unexplained; test a smaller dose or an additive, token-matched mix as a separate ablation if the TMax signal still merits follow-up.

issues.body:
## Summary

- **Motivation:** Our Snowball post-training ablations use BFCL ×5 with the Pi agent to score tool calling, so we needed Mochi's own baseline on that benchmark to anchor what Snowball results imply for Mochi.
- **Goal:** Benchmark Mochi SFT (step 400407) on BFCL ×5 with the Pi agent and compare it with the Snowball models used in the post-training ablations.
- **Data:** Five runs of the 123 BFCL tasks (615 graded trials per model), scored with the same training chat template and Pi agent.
- **Method:** Serve Mochi SFT (step 400407) with vLLM on four GB200 hosts under the configured Harbor retry rule, and compare descriptively against the previously scored Snowball 10/05 SFT parent and two 15-update Snowball SFT runs (general-only control and TMax trace swap).
- **Results:** Mochi SFT scored 450/615 (73.17% under the retry rule; 449 first-attempt wins, bounding the first-attempt mean at 73.01–73.17%). On the same 123 tasks, Snowball models scored 33.98–52.36%: 322/615 (52.36%) for the 10/05 parent, 262/615 (42.60%) for the 15-update control, and 209/615 (33.98%) for the 15-update TMax arm.
- **Conclusion:** Mochi scores well above the Snowball models on this benchmark, anchoring what Snowball tool-calling ablations imply for Mochi. Because serving hardware and code revisions differed between the Mochi and Snowball runs, the comparison is descriptive; attributing the gap to the model alone would require a matched rerun.

## Description

This issue records how Mochi compares with the Snowball models on BFCL ×5, the tool-calling benchmark the Snowball ablations use.
- **Mochi:** the 535B Grug MoE, SFT export at step 400407.
- **Agent:** Pi, the same as the Snowball runs.
- **Serve:** vLLM on four GB200x4 hosts in cw-us-east-08a, with TP1, DP16 and CUDA graphs on.

Parent: issue 11535.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Measure Mochi's tool-calling score on the benchmark the Snowball ablations use, to anchor what the Snowball results imply for Mochi.

## Status

**Mochi SFT step 400407:**
- **Score:** 92/92/91/86/89 of 123 = 450/615 = 73.17%. This is the record score under the configured Harbor retry rule.
- **First attempts:** 449 first-attempt wins, and one first-attempt reward is unavailable after a timeout. So the first-attempt mean is bounded at 73.01–73.17%.
- **One looping trial:** in run 1, task `bfcl-parallel-multiple-130` looped for 1,800 s with 146 tool turns. Its score comes from a Harbor retry triggered by a verifier timeout.
- **Cost:** 33.52 GB200-h of serving.
- **Retry parity:** the Snowball parent's earlier BFCL ×5 used the same retry rule, with 4 retried trials.

**Snowball models on the same 123 tasks and the training chat template (tools@3f):**

| Model | Score (5 runs) | Run-level bootstrap range | Missing result file (verifier) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mochi SFT step 400407 | 450/615 = 73.17% | not computed | not counted |
| Snowball parent (10/05 SFT) | 322/615 = 52.36% | 50.1–55.6% | 64 |
| Snowball control (15 updates) | 262/615 = 42.60% | 40.2–45.5% | 152 |
| Snowball TMax arm (15 updates) | 209/615 = 33.98% | 31.9–36.1% | 264 |

- **What the ranges mean:** they come from bootstrapping over the 5 runs of a fixed 123-task set. They are not population confidence intervals, and not a test of the difference between models.
- **Missing result file:** this column counts verifier reports that the answer file was absent. It does not say why the file was missing.
- **Snowball cost:** these Snowball runs cost 54.60 H100-h in total.

**Limits:**
- **Environment confound:** Mochi ran on GB200 with a different code version from the Snowball reruns. The Snowball reruns also used a newer runtime than the earlier Snowball runs. Every historical comparison carries this confound, and it cannot isolate the effect of the template or the model.
- **Nested edits:** BFCL does not exercise nested edit calls. Mochi's traces contain only 7 edit calls, none with multiple edits. Issue 11536 tracks that question.

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

## Conclusion

Plan:
1. Link the immutable model checkpoints, evaluation records, source revisions, Pi/Harbor versions, task IDs, seeds, chat template, and retry policy for all four models. Record the missing first-attempt reward and each verifier-missing answer file separately.
2. If a model-effect claim is needed, rerun Mochi and the three Snowball checkpoints on the same hardware and serving/harness revision, using the same 123 tasks, five repetitions, decoding settings, timeouts, and retry policy. Estimate serving cost from the existing runs before launch.
3. Compare paired task outcomes and report both first-attempt and retry-rule scores, scored/missing counts, and uncertainty over tasks. Update this issue's conclusion with the controlled result; keep the current cross-environment scores labeled descriptive.

issues.title: [post-training] Mochi SFT on BFCL ×5 versus Snowball models

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Summary

- **Motivation:** In our earlier agentic SFT shootout, every GLM-5.3 arm scored below its parent while contributor rows beat GLM LOW by +26 points on SWE-bench and +9 on TBLite, and both our closeness scores (issue 11674) and a collaborator's study pointed toward lower-NLL teachers—yet none of those was a matched-token teacher ablation.
- **Goal:** Determine whether a student learns more per supervised token from teacher traces that have lower per-token negative log-likelihood (NLL) under the student, to decide whether closeness should select teachers for the Mochi SFT mix.
- **Data:** Candidate teacher traces from open-weight models on shared coding and terminal-agent task pools (matched on task pool, trace length, reasoning share, and teacher solve rate), plus an earlier base-start comparison using 5,347 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B teacher rows in 53 packs mixed into 4,800 rows.
- **Method:** Proposed 1-hour screen and 8-hour matched-token SFT comparison on Snowball: compare the lowest-NLL half against a random half from the same teacher, compare a closer teacher against a more distant teacher (or a pair where mean NLL and pooled-token Rank-Surprisal Ratio disagree, such as Qwen3.5-122B versus Qwen3.6-35B-A3B), and test a trace-length filter of at least 5 turns, scored on paired Micro210.
- **Results:** The matched-token closeness comparison has not run. A separate base-start data arm (150 updates in BF16 from the pretrained base, mixing Qwen3.6-35B-A3B teacher rows with no distant-teacher counterpart) scored 534/855 (0.625) on the synthetic Pi edit eval against 151/855 (0.177) for its control, with broader evaluation pending.
- **Conclusion:** Whether teacher closeness predicts SFT outcomes remains open. The base-start run lacks a distant-teacher counterpart and stored parameters in BF16, so it does not test closeness, and the companion similarity campaign stopped after the Nemotron v3 rows (issue 11722).

## Question

At matched supervised tokens, matched tasks, matched trace length and matched success rate, does a student score higher after SFT on traces from a teacher that is closer to it by per-token NLL than after SFT on traces from a more distant teacher?

Two secondary questions:

1. Holding the teacher and task pool fixed, does training on the lowest-NLL half of the pool beat a random half at matched tokens? This tests the selection rule directly, with no teacher confound.
2. Does the OpenThoughts-Agent trace-length filter (drop traces with fewer than 5 turns) add to the better teacher at matched tokens?

## What we already know

- **Outside evidence, ablated:** OpenThoughts selected the teacher for code and for math and found the teacher's own benchmark rank did not predict the student ranking; QwQ-32B produced stronger students than DeepSeek-R1 as the code and math teacher, although DeepSeek-R1 is the stronger model by benchmark average ([arXiv 2506.04178](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.04178), Section 4.6). OpenThoughts-Agent reports lower Terminal-Bench 2.0 performance when GPT-5.3-Codex was the teacher than when GLM-4.7-AWQ was, although GPT-5.3-Codex is the stronger model ([arXiv 2606.24855](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24855), Section 3.5). Neither measures student closeness.
- **Collaborator result, measured:** on a Snowball-family student, the strongest teacher produced the weakest student; a later 500-task comparison matched length and solve rate and still favored the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-trained student over the GLM-5.3-Flash-trained student, with GLM SFT loss reported about 3× higher before and after SFT, and scaling the 35B traces did not appear to help much. This is paraphrased from the team's summary of the collaborator's posts ([Oct 24 post](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1355318637854199848/1563524283588677727), [Nov 9 follow-up](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1355318637854199848/1569357141855314110)); the primary Discord messages were not directly read. Traces: [marianna13/rts-tmax-teacher-traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marianna13/rts-tmax-teacher-traces).
- **Our measurement:** under the 10/05 checkpoint, contributor traces and the collaborator's Qwen3.5/3.6 traces score 0.25–0.55 nats per loss token, while the GLM traces score 1.172–1.863 all-token and 1.180–1.866 text-only; the pre-SFT base parent gives a similar broad ordering. See the companion measurement issue.
- **Our training comparison:** our agentic SFT shootout trained on GLM 5.3 traces and on contributor rows. For the 1,432-task pair, the task pool, the parent and the recipe were matched. Every GLM arm scored below its parent on SWE-bench and TBLite, while the contributor rows beat the GLM LOW rows by SWE-bench +26 [+17, +36] points and TBLite +9 [+1, +17] points ([issue 10213 summary](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213#issuecomment-6618401658)). The remaining confounds were the teacher, the harness format the traces were recorded in, and the supervised-token dose (contributor tokens were 1.27× larger), so this is not an isolated teacher comparison. Recording every arm's traces in the same harness is an input requirement for this design.
- **Related prior work:** [issue 8533](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8533) and [issue 9348](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9348) cover student-relative scoring of traces and whether those scores can guide data selection. [Issue 11539](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11539) covers the TMax data question in SFT.

## A teacher-data arm that already ran

A base-start teacher arm finished with a matched control. The treatment mixed 5,347 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B teacher r4 rows in 53 audited packs into 4,800 total rows, 150 updates from the pretrained base on 64 H100, experts Adam at 2e-5 in BF16, treatment source `41abaaab`, control source `3b291b10`. The control's trainer and optimizer source is identical apart from three added wrapper files. Both jobs succeeded, and the treatment export is verified (39 shards, 134,160,310,992 bytes, ready and manifest hashes pinned).

On the eval-r2 edit-call readout (171 prompts, pooled seeds 1–5, 855 grades per arm, one checkpoint and one serve per arm), the teacher arm scored exact 534/855 = 0.625 against the control 151/855 = 0.177, and all 11 tasks were higher. Both arms were graded on the same five synthetic Pi edit categories (replace_block, rename_local, insert_after, delete_lines, change_literal). Scope note from the readout: "Exact added-row identities and before/target texts were disjoint. Shared generator patterns and near-duplicates were not assessed. Inherited C150 exposure remains unverified." The broader evaluation is pending.

This is a data-arm comparison, not a closeness test: it has no distant-teacher counterpart and no closeness-matched pairs, so it does not answer the question in this issue.

## Proposed design

Both versions freeze the same things: the row pool and task IDs, the text-target masks, the token budget per arm, the step count, the learning rate and schedule, the optimizer state policy, the precision, and the readout. Any row excluded for any reason is excluded from every arm before any score is read. Coverage and missing rows are reported per arm.

### 1-hour screen

**Arm A (direct selection test):** same pool, same teacher, matched tokens; train on the lowest-NLL half versus a random half. This isolates the selection rule from teacher identity.

**Arm B (teacher pair):** Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith rows versus GLM-5.3 LOW rows on the same SWE tasks, matched supervised tokens, length and success rate, both recorded in the same harness.

Gates for a 1-hour run, which is too short to resolve benchmark quality: held-out NLL and training stability. Exploratory Micro may be reported alongside, with no decision threshold attached, so a favorable Micro point estimate is not read as a result. Uncosted at this stage: the historical estimate for the selection-test pair was 2 × 55–85 H100-h, which was a backlog estimate and not a costed one-hour screen. The final packet will state the GPU count, the wall cap and the cost.

### 8-hour version

Primary outcome: paired Micro over the full panel, plus the SWE panel, on three arms: the closer teacher, the more distant teacher, and the closer teacher plus the ≥5-turn trace filter. Report the per-arm row and token censuses next to the scores.

Predeclared decision rule, fixed before the run. The primary metric is paired Micro210, reported as a task-level paired difference with a 95% interval. The closer-teacher arm nominates a Mochi check only if the lower bound of its paired Micro210 difference over the more distant teacher is above zero and the frozen packet's retention tolerance is met; if the upper bound is below zero, that weighs against the closer teacher rather than for it. The filter arm is judged the same way against the closer teacher. The retention tolerance is fixed in the frozen packet before the run; until then this issue does not set one, and no nomination follows from the Micro210 bound alone. Any other outcome is unresolved, and the design is revised rather than re-run on the same rows.

The confounds this design must control, and which the shootout did not: harness format of the recorded traces, task-pool identity, teacher success rate, trace length and reasoning share, supervised-token dose, epochs and step count, learning rate and schedule, optimizer state, precision and expert capacity, and evaluation protocol (context, timeout, trials). A result that survives only without these controls does not answer the question.

## What would change the plan

- **If closeness predicts:** the closeness score becomes a pre-screen for ranking teachers and data for the Mochi SFT mix, and the 8-hour version is the confirmation. A favorable screen does not by itself change the mix; it nominates a Mochi check.
- **If closeness does not predict:** drop closeness as a selection criterion. Select teachers and data by matched-token training outcomes, and keep the closeness pass only as a diagnostic. A distant teacher winning at matched tokens is the clearest falsifier.
- **If the filter arm wins at matched tokens:** the ≥5-turn filter becomes a candidate for the Mochi SFT mix, subject to the same Mochi check.
- **If the low-NLL half scores lower under the matched design:** that weighs against this selection rule. A single inconclusive difference leaves it open.
- **A null result from a single run per arm** leaves the practical effect size unresolved rather than showing there is no effect.

## What this does not test

- It does not test Mochi directly; a Snowball result is a candidate for a Mochi check, not a Mochi result.
- It does not separate teacher style from teacher correctness, from trace length, or from the amount of task-relevant knowledge in the traces.
- It does not test memorization as the source of a low NLL; exposed rows must be reported separately, and the selection arm must be checked for overlap with the student's own training data.
- It does not settle which teacher is best for Mochi; it only tests whether closeness is a useful ranking variable.

## Links

- Companion measurement issue: [Measured student NLL closeness to teacher traces](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11674)
- [Issue 10213: agentic SFT shootout on Snowball v0](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213#issuecomment-6618401658)
- [Issue 11539: Snowball SFT with vs without TMax agent traces](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11539)
- [Issue 8533](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8533) and [issue 9348](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9348): student-relative scoring of agentic traces
- [marianna13/rts-tmax-teacher-traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marianna13/rts-tmax-teacher-traces)
