issues.title: [post-training] Does teacher closeness predict SFT outcome?

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Summary

- **Motivation:** The Mochi post-training plan has to choose teachers for the SFT mix, and prior studies found that a teacher's own benchmark rank did not predict student outcomes. If student closeness predicts how much a teacher's traces teach, a cheap scoring pass could rank candidate teachers before full training runs.
- **Goal:** Measure how predictable candidate teachers' agentic traces are under a frozen Snowball student checkpoint, to see whether closeness separates candidate teachers before running matched-token SFT comparisons (issue 11673).
- **Data:** 14 trace cells (9,943 scored rows) spanning contributor SWE-smith and TMax traces plus five open-weight teachers (Qwen3.5-122B, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen3.8-27B, and GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM v7) across shared task pools.
- **Method:** Score each trace cell under frozen Snowball 10/05 SFT and the pre-SFT base checkpoint for token-weighted mean NLL (all loss tokens and text-only) and, in a single pass under 10/05, pooled-token Rank-Surprisal Ratio (RSR) with ranks capped at 100.
- **Results:** Under Snowball 10/05, contributor traces and the collaborator's Qwen3.5/3.6 cells scored 0.25–0.55 nats per loss token (lowest: Qwen3.5-122B at 0.253 on TMax and 0.332 on the second collaborator pool), Qwen3.8-27B scored 0.952 and 0.978, and GLM cells scored 1.172–1.863 all-token (1.180–1.866 text-only). The pre-SFT base ranked the 13 shared cells in the same order, 0.085–0.158 nats higher. Across all 14 cells, pooled-token RSR and mean NLL had a Spearman rank correlation of −0.125 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B had lower RSR than Qwen3.5-122B despite higher NLL), and 1,752 of 1,954 baseline Kimi SWE-smith rows overlapped the 10/05 training mix.
- **Conclusion:** Closeness separates the candidate teachers strongly, and much of that separation is already present before SFT, but mean NLL and pooled-token RSR disagree on which teacher is closest. The closeness tables are no longer being extended; whether either metric predicts SFT outcomes remains untested (issue 11673).

## Why we measure this

The Mochi post-training plan has to choose teachers for the SFT mix. If student closeness predicts how much a teacher's traces teach, we can rank candidate data with a cheap scoring pass instead of a full training arm. Three different kinds of evidence make that worth testing, and they do not all point the same way.

**Outside evidence, ablated.** OpenThoughts ablated the teacher model directly and found that the teacher's own benchmark rank did not predict the student's ranking: QwQ-32B produced stronger students than DeepSeek-R1 when it was selected as the code or math teacher, even though DeepSeek-R1 is the stronger model by benchmark average. The reported values are overall student averages after selecting that teacher for code and for math, not teacher scores ([arXiv 2506.04178](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.04178), Section 4.6 and Table 8). OpenThoughts-Agent reports the same pattern for agentic traces: selecting GPT-5.3-Codex as the teacher gave lower Terminal-Bench 2.0 performance than selecting GLM-4.7-AWQ, despite GPT-5.3-Codex being the stronger model ([arXiv 2606.24855](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24855), Section 3.5). Neither paper measures student closeness to the teacher traces. In these ablations, teacher strength was not the right ranking variable; neither identifies closeness as the substitute.

**Collaborator result, measured.** A collaborator's teacher study on a Snowball-family student (Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12, two epochs, batch 32, LR 1e-5) found that the strongest teacher could produce the weakest student. A later 500-task comparison matched length and solve rate and still favored the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-trained student over the GLM-5.3-Flash-trained student; she reported GLM SFT loss about 3× higher before and after SFT, and that scaling the 35B traces did not appear to help much. This is paraphrased from the team's summary of her posts, which link the primary Discord messages: [Oct 24 post](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1355318637854199848/1563524283588677727), [Nov 9 follow-up](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1355318637854199848/1569357141855314110). The released traces are public: [marianna13/rts-tmax-teacher-traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marianna13/rts-tmax-teacher-traces) at revision `bc3de8cb`, CC-BY-4.0, five teachers on the same two task pools, one attempt per task, every verified trial kept whether or not it was solved. This is a motivating observation, not a causal proof.

**Our measurement, this issue.** We scored our own student's NLL on those teacher traces and on our contributor rows. Our numbers put the GLM traces furthest from the student, the same direction as the collaborator's training outcome.

**Our own training comparison, measured but not matched.** Our agentic SFT shootout trained on GLM 5.3 traces and on contributor rows (Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith, Qwen3.6-27B TMax) on the same 1,432 tasks, parent and recipe. Every GLM arm scored below its parent on SWE-bench and TBLite, while the contributor rows beat the GLM LOW rows by SWE-bench +26 [+17, +36] points and TBLite +9 [+1, +17] points ([issue 10213 summary](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213#issuecomment-6618401658)). The contributor tokens were also 1.27× larger, and the teachers and harness formats differed, so this is not an isolated teacher comparison. A collaborator's separate write-up reports 46.5% on SWE-bench Verified random-100 from a 12.8% starting checkpoint using Qwen3.8-27B CalibForge plus Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith traces, and 50.5% after RL ([blog post](https://lukedhlee.github.io/blog/2026/10/21/turning-snowball-into-a-coding-agent/)); we have not independently verified those values.

**How to read the contrast.** The two sets of experiments used different teachers and had different outcomes, which is consistent with the closeness hypothesis. It does not prove it, because other things also differ: the data and task pools, the student checkpoint (our shootout used Snowball v0 and v0.1; the collaborator's used the general-SFT 09-21 checkpoint), the recipe and dose (3 epochs at 1e-6, versus the collaborator's epochs followed by RL), the evaluation protocol (32k context, 1,800 s, one trial, versus 64k, a 3× timeout and three repeats), the harness the traces were recorded in, and stack fixes the collaborator applied for training precision and expert capacity that our arms predate.

**Where the evidence is weak.** The controlled teacher ablations are dense 7B–32B students (Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3-8B/32B), not a 67B MoE and not a 535B MoE. The two Snowball comparisons involve near-versus-distant teachers but are not matched-token teacher ablations. Closeness could matter at 7B and not at our scale, or the reverse.

**Hypothesis.** A student may learn more per supervised token from traces it already finds likely, because it is imitating behavior closer to its own distribution. If this holds, the closeness score ranks candidate teachers and data for the Mochi SFT mix. If it fails, teacher and data selection must be decided by matched-token training outcomes, and the closeness score is only a diagnostic.

**What would falsify it.** A distant teacher winning at matched tokens and matched tasks, a near teacher losing, a closeness ranking that does not match the outcome ranking across several teachers, or low NLL explained by the student having already seen the rows rather than by the teacher's style.

**Baseline and RSR measurement.** This report gives the mean per-token NLL baseline. We scored these cells with Snowball using Rank-Surprisal Ratio (RSR), the mean target-token rank divided by the mean negative log-likelihood under the student. The paper proposes RSR to capture both alignment and informativeness and reports a mean absolute Spearman correlation of 0.86 with post-training reasoning performance across five students and trajectories from 11 teachers. [Paper abstract](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14249v5) In a separate agentic study, Qwen3-8B scored assistant tokens with ranks capped at 100. Mean RSR recovered the published ordering of four teachers on a source-balanced OpenThoughts-Agent sample of 1,000 trajectories per teacher. Trajectory length, mean NLL, error-retry rate and tool-action ratio failed to recover that order in this sample. The separate data-selection test was inconclusive. [Issue 9348](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9348), following [issue 8533](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8533). The pooled-token RSR subsection below gives the Snowball 10/05 results and their limits.

## What we measured

Per-token NLL of one frozen student on candidate teacher traces, in nats per supervised loss token, token-weighted. "Text" excludes target tokens whose id is ≥128000 (chat-template specials), which are 0.2–1.5% of loss tokens. The per-trace mean is the unweighted mean of per-row means. Every value below is a mean over whole cells; the cells are not paired with each other except where an equal-task gap is stated explicitly.

Two reviewed datasets exist, and they are not the same rows or the same pass count:

- **Single pass, four cells (all loss tokens):** 8,540 rows in four cells, one pass, no training, zero missing rows. These four values are whole-cell, all-loss-token means. This is the run quoted in the issue 11535 status comment.
- **Three-pass campaign (text-only; 500 tasks per internal cell, 250 per collaborator split):** three internal 500-task cells (contributor, GLM v7 LOW, GLM v7 HIGH), ten collaborator cells (five teachers × two pools, 250 tasks each), and one 10/05-only contrib-full cell.

Cell names in plain words:

- **contrib:** our contributor rows on 500 shared tasks — Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith (250 tasks) plus Qwen3.6-27B TMax (250 tasks).
- **contrib-full:** every contributor plain row, 2,978 rows, one task each. It is not paired with any other cell. Its full-pool mean was 0.283 versus 0.294 for the sampled 500-task cell; that comparison alone does not establish sample representativeness.
- **glm-low / glm-high:** GLM 5.3 v7 traces at the LOW and HIGH reasoning-effort settings, on the same 500 tasks as contrib.
- **collaborator cells:** the released five-teacher trace sets on the collaborator's two task pools, RTS and TMax-legacy, 250 tasks per split, one attempt per task; summarization gives several rows per trial.

## How we measured

- **Scorer:** `experiments/post_training/teacher_nll/score.py` at commit `5e2ba6e9b87db5038211da796ef0e5779f2fe637` (SHA256 `45a84de6789f89fb173e190b2db937505c2008a0510964e97d35c91359640b3f`). Direct vLLM prompt-logprob scoring, TP1/DP8 with expert parallel, prefix caching off, 73,728 context, 7,168 batched tokens, 32 sequences, one completion token per prompt. The loss weight at position *i* scores token *i*+1, the trainer's convention; no masked token is converted into a target.
- **Students:** 10/05 SFT `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05` at revision `8c76b22a`, and the pre-SFT parent `open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8` at revision `058ecaf2`. No distributed-loader flag; weights load from the Hub on the GPU host.
- **Single-pass cells:** the scorer reused the frozen token IDs and loss masks; no re-rendering, truncation or trajectory deduplication. Seven original SWE holdout rows were scored for completeness and remain ineligible for training.
- **Campaign cells:** rendered with the 10/05 tokenizer and chat template, byte-identical to `grug_sft/tokenizer/2026.09.18`, with `enable_thinking=True` passed explicitly. The collaborator's traces were re-rendered independently and matched 100/100.
- **Parity check against the trainer:** the 16 rows of a smoke step-0 batch scored 0.380693 under vLLM versus 0.380914 from the native trainer, a difference of −0.00022 nats against a 0.01 gate.
- **Passes:** the campaign cells are three full passes, each in a fresh engine process, with a pass spread of ≤0.0003 nats; the base parent is one pass. The single-pass cells are one pass under 10/05.
- **Intervals:** 95% bootstrap, 10,000 resamples over tasks, seed 20261113, rows clustered by (family, task). Paired gaps use the shared task set. Text-only means are reported without intervals; the all-token and base-text columns carry the campaign's own within-cell bootstrap.

## Results

### Three-pass campaign

The table below is the campaign's complete results table: three passes per cell, 95% bootstrap intervals over tasks, the 10/05 text-target column, the 10/05 per-trace mean, and the pre-SFT base text column. The all-token column carries the interval. Text-only and all-token values are kept separate and are not interchangeable.

| Cell | All loss tokens | 10/05 NLL [95% CI] | 10/05 text | 10/05 per-trace | Base text NLL [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| marianna qwen3.5-122b-a10b-fp8 tmax | 1.22M | 0.253 [0.242, 0.264] | 0.254 | 0.248 | 0.394 [0.382, 0.406] |
| contrib-full | 12.90M | 0.283 [0.279, 0.286] | 0.281 | 0.284 | not run |
| contrib | 1.97M | 0.294 [0.285, 0.302] | 0.290 | 0.292 | 0.432 [0.422, 0.442] |
| marianna qwen3.5-122b-a10b-fp8 rts | 3.49M | 0.332 [0.304, 0.357] | 0.334 | 0.431 | 0.453 [0.429, 0.480] |
| marianna qwen3.5-9b tmax | 3.06M | 0.400 [0.375, 0.421] | 0.401 | 0.487 | 0.507 [0.482, 0.530] |
| marianna qwen3.6-35b-a3b tmax | 1.30M | 0.416 [0.369, 0.457] | 0.417 | 0.390 | 0.524 [0.476, 0.565] |
| marianna qwen3.5-9b rts | 5.59M | 0.449 [0.423, 0.475] | 0.451 | 0.603 | 0.545 [0.513, 0.581] |
| marianna qwen3.6-35b-a3b rts | 4.02M | 0.548 [0.513, 0.573] | 0.550 | 0.589 | 0.656 [0.625, 0.679] |
| marianna qwen3.8-27b rts | 4.34M | 0.952 [0.917, 0.984] | 0.954 | 0.978 | 1.074 [1.042, 1.103] |
| marianna qwen3.8-27b tmax | 2.61M | 0.978 [0.941, 1.012] | 0.979 | 0.992 | 1.077 [1.043, 1.110] |
| glm-low (v7 LOW) | 1.39M | 1.172 [1.101, 1.241] | 1.180 | 0.919 | 1.320 [1.253, 1.386] |
| glm-high (v7 HIGH) | 2.96M | 1.303 [1.244, 1.359] | 1.311 | 1.191 | 1.469 [1.418, 1.519] |
| marianna glm-5.3-flash tmax | 1.73M | 1.854 [1.823, 1.884] | 1.858 | 1.808 | 1.944 [1.912, 1.976] |
| marianna glm-5.3-flash rts | 5.43M | 1.863 [1.819, 1.902] | 1.866 | 1.802 | 1.952 [1.907, 1.990] |

Values are 3-decimal roundings of the retained analysis JSON for these cells; the JSON values govern. GLM LOW's token-weighted mean (1.172) is well above its per-trace mean (0.919): a minority of long, high-NLL traces carry much of its mass.

What the numbers show:

- Under 10/05, the contributor traces and the collaborator's Qwen3.5/3.6 cells score 0.25–0.55, while the GLM cells score 1.172–1.863 all-token and 1.180–1.866 text-only.
- On shared cells the base text means were 0.085–0.158 nats higher, with similar broad ordering.
- On the same 500 tasks, v7 HIGH is further than v7 LOW and the paired gaps exclude zero: +0.131 [+0.077, +0.186] text-only and +0.130 [+0.076, +0.185] all-token for 10/05; +0.149 [+0.097, +0.200] for the base text.
- Contributor minus glm-low on the same 500 tasks: −0.889 [−0.958, −0.821] for 10/05 text and −0.888 [−0.955, −0.820] for base text. Restricting to TMax, the family with no contributor trajectory copies identified by the overlap scan, gives −1.076 [−1.147, −1.004] for 10/05 text and −1.071 [−1.145, −0.997] for base text. On SWE-smith the gaps are −0.405 [−0.445, −0.366] and −0.461 [−0.511, −0.412].
- The collaborator's qwen3.8-27b cells (0.95–0.98) sit far from the other Qwen teachers.

### Pooled-token RSR, ranks capped at 100

Rank-Surprisal Ratio (RSR) is the mean target-token rank divided by the mean negative log-likelihood under the student; the paper interprets lower RSR as better informative alignment. We ran it with the same Snowball 10/05 student on the same 14 cells, in one pass over 9,943 rows in one fresh engine. The run reproduced the earlier mean NLL on every cell, largest difference 0.000131 nats per token. Each cell's value is the sum of capped ranks over loss tokens divided by the sum of NLL over those tokens, so longer scored rows carry more weight.

| Cell | Mean NLL | Pooled-token RSR, ranks capped at 100 | Tokens over the cap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-122B, TMax | 0.253 | 4.668 | 0.01% |
| Our contributor rows, all | 0.283 | 4.390 | 0.03% |
| Our contributor rows, 500 tasks | 0.294 | 4.317 | 0.04% |
| Qwen3.5-122B, RTS | 0.332 | 3.861 | 0.03% |
| Qwen3.5-9B, TMax | 0.400 | 3.518 | 0.02% |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, TMax | 0.416 | 3.403 | 0.03% |
| Qwen3.5-9B, RTS | 0.449 | 3.315 | 0.03% |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, RTS | 0.548 | 2.962 | 0.05% |
| Qwen3.8-27B, RTS | 0.952 | 3.029 | 0.38% |
| Qwen3.8-27B, TMax | 0.978 | 3.218 | 0.48% |
| GLM 5.3 v7 LOW (ours) | 1.173 | 4.420 | 1.78% |
| GLM 5.3 v7 HIGH (ours) | 1.303 | 4.296 | 1.85% |
| GLM-5.3-Flash, TMax | 1.854 | 4.620 | 3.22% |
| GLM-5.3-Flash, RTS | 1.863 | 4.205 | 2.53% |

What this shows:

- The two measures disagree. The rank correlation between pooled-token RSR and mean NLL over the 14 cells is −0.125, so "closest teacher" depends on which measure is read.
- By mean NLL the collaborator's teachers order 122B, 9B, 35B-A3B, 27B, GLM (closest first) on both task pools. By pooled-token RSR the RTS order is 35B-A3B, 27B, 9B, 122B, GLM (best first), and the TMax order is 27B, 35B-A3B, 9B, GLM, 122B.
- GLM-5.3-Flash has the highest mean NLL on both pools, and the highest pooled-token RSR on RTS and the second-highest on TMax, behind Qwen3.5-122B.
- Our contributor rows have low mean NLL, but their pooled-token RSR values (4.317 and 4.390) fall inside the range of the four GLM cells (4.205–4.620).

Limits of this RSR measurement:

- **Aggregation.** Our column is a pooled-token ratio: the sum of capped ranks over loss tokens divided by the sum of NLL over those tokens, which weights longer scored rows more. The paper's formula in its appendix A.8 uses the ratio of sums of trajectory-level means. On our data, taking the ratio of summed row means gives a correlation of −0.108 with pooled mean NLL and puts Qwen3.5-9B lowest on both RTS and TMax. Row-to-trajectory equivalence is unverified.
- **The cap.** "Tokens over the cap" is the share of a cell's loss tokens whose rank exceeds 100, so the cap changed those terms. Without the cap of 100, several cells change a lot (Qwen3.5-122B RTS is 55.97 instead of 3.861).
- **Rank convention.** The rank is the serving engine's tie-inclusive rank: 1 plus tokens with a strictly higher logprob plus other tokens with an identical logprob. On the 16 parity rows, a strict comparison reduced the all-loss-token capped rank sum by 0.11% (141 of 128,420) and the text-only sum by 0.10%. This was measured on the parity rows only.
- **Logit dtype.** The logit dtype used for the ranks is unverified.
- **Scope.** One pass, one student, one serving build. No training-outcome inference is drawn.

### Single pass, four cells (all loss tokens)

| Cell | Rows / tasks | All loss tokens | 10/05 NLL |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Contributor Kimi SWE-smith baseline | 1,954 / 1,954 | 8,851,457 | 0.262938 |
| Contributor Qwen expanded TMax | 5,154 / 1,010 | 17,235,047 | 0.311926 |
| GLM LOW matched SWE | 466 / 466 | 887,535 | 0.679589 |
| GLM LOW matched TMax | 966 / 966 | 3,626,719 | 1.386275 |

8,540 of 8,540 rows validated with zero missing; 74,969,846 prompt tokens and 30,600,758 loss tokens. These four values are whole-cell, all-loss-token means, not paired comparisons; the only paired numbers from this run are the equal-task gaps reported here: contributor minus GLM LOW is −0.371116 nats on the 466 shared SWE tasks and −0.896427 on the 966 shared TMax tasks. GLM LOW has 1,432 shared tasks overall, not a trajectory for every contributor task; no missing LOW examples were invented.

**Overlap caution for the Kimi number:** 1,752/1,954 baseline SWE-smith rows met the AgentTrove overlap rule; prior exposure could contribute to the 0.263. No TMax trajectory copies were identified under this scan (0/1,024 baseline; 0/4,156 expanded).

### Why the two tables differ

They measure different rows with different methods. The campaign scored each cell three times and reports task-bootstrap intervals. Teacher comparisons are paired only within a shared task pool; the paired gaps resample those shared tasks. The one-pass table scores 8,540 rows over four differently sized cells exactly once, so those four means are unpaired whole-cell averages. The GLM figures also come from different pools: the campaign's glm-low/glm-high are GLM 5.3 v7 at two effort settings on our 500 tasks, while the one-pass GLM LOW cells are the 466-task matched SWE and 966-task matched TMax subsets. That is why 1.172 (campaign) and 0.680 (one-pass SWE) describe different row sets rather than contradicting each other.

## Open questions

These are open questions raised by the three-pass table, not findings.

1. **Is the Qwen3.5-122B number about closeness, or about trace shape?** It has the lowest NLL of any teacher (0.253 TMax, 0.332 RTS), ahead of the 9B (0.400, 0.449) and the 35B-A3B (0.416, 0.548). On the same 250 TMax tasks the 122B cell has 1.22M loss tokens against 3.06M for the 9B cell. Length has not been controlled.
2. **Why is Qwen3.8-27B far from the other Qwen teachers?** Its cells are 0.952 (RTS) and 0.978 (TMax), close to the GLM v7 numbers (1.172 and 1.303), while the other Qwen teachers are 0.253–0.548.
3. **Why does the pre-SFT base give the same broad ordering?** It ranks the same 13 cells in the same order, 0.085–0.158 nats higher on every cell.
4. **Which summary should be read?** Token-weighted and per-trace means disagree in some cells: Qwen3.5-122B RTS is 0.332 token-weighted and 0.431 per-trace; GLM v7 LOW is 1.172 and 0.919.
5. **Why does the task family change the number?** RTS is higher than TMax for the Qwen3.5-122B, Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B cells (0.332 vs 0.253; 0.449 vs 0.400; 0.548 vs 0.416), and lower for Qwen3.8-27B (0.952 vs 0.978).
6. **How much of this measures the text rather than the student?** The score mixes teacher-to-student distance with how predictable the text is to any model. A control would score the same traces with one or two unrelated open models; a length-matched comparison would hold trace size fixed.
7. **Does Rank-Surprisal Ratio change the ranking?** Yes. Across these 14 cells, the Spearman correlation between pooled-token RSR and mean NLL is −0.125. In a comparison of Qwen3.5-122B with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, mean NLL is lower for 122B and pooled-token RSR is lower for 35B-A3B on both pools. Which measure predicts SFT outcomes remains open. See the pooled-token RSR subsection for the measurement limits.

## Row overlap with the 10/05 SFT mix

A low NLL can mean the teacher writes like the student, or that the student already saw these rows. We checked both, on CPU. The inventory pass read only the small per-document offset arrays; the exact-compare and 50-gram passes then inspected token content.

- The inventory read the offsets of all 216 stores in the 10/05 mix (3,862 parts, 21,493,925 documents, 237.06B tokens). The exact compare ran on all 216 stores; the loss-span 50-gram scan ran over the 162 agentic stores (54.61B tokens), covering all 3,862 parts.
- "In 10/05" means the row's best store is `agenttrove` with ≥10% of its loss-span 50-grams covered.

| Row set | Rows | In 10/05 | Median coverage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline SWE-smith (contrib-full) | 1,954 | 1,752 (89.7%) | 0.43 |
| Expanded new SWE-smith | 511 | 465 (91.0%) | 0.44 |
| Tier-2 SWE-smith | 1,270 | 1,157 (91.1%) | 0.43 |
| Baseline TMax | 1,024 | 0 | 0.00 |
| Expanded new TMax | 4,156 | 0 | 0.00 |

- No TMax trajectory copies were identified by the scan. The 13 TMax rows at 0.09–0.22 coverage share task content with another teacher's traces, which is task overlap, not trajectory overlap.
- 3 SWE rows are byte-exact after tail normalization; the rest are re-serialized, so prose and thinking grams match while JSON-formatting grams do not (coverage around 0.43). 361 SWE rows were not found (202 baseline, 46 expanded, 113 tier-2).
- The 10/05 store `agenttrove` is `open-thoughts/AgentTrove` at `b395a43`: 525,521 normalized rows, including 4,724 Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith rows. The mix also includes Qwen3.6-27B traces, the teacher of the contributor TMax half. Those are different task sources, but the same teacher's style is in the SFT data.
- Row-level flags, using the 500-row contributor campaign cell: 238 of 500 rows carry the campaign's overlap flag (237 of 250 SWE-smith, 1 of 250 TMax). This is the campaign's row-flag join, a separate route from the `agenttrove` ≥10%-coverage rule used in the table above, and the two counts are not interchangeable. Descriptively, the flagged rows dropped −0.172 nats from base to 10/05 and the unflagged rows −0.112, against a −0.106 median for the 12 non-contributor cells. This is observational and confounded with task family: the flagged rows are almost all SWE-smith, and only 13 unflagged SWE-smith rows exist. It does not establish a mechanism.
- Counter-evidence against exposure explaining the ranking: the pre-SFT base, which never saw the 10/05 SFT data, already puts contributor traces far closer than GLM on the same tasks, with the same paired gap as 10/05, so exposure alone does not account for the ranking.

## Limits

- Likelihood is not quality. A lower NLL means the traces are more predictable under this scorer, rendering and loss mask. It says nothing about correctness, usefulness as SFT data, or downstream gains.
- The cells are not all paired. Our 500-task cells pair with each other; the collaborator's cells pair with each other. Cross-group values differ by task mix as well as by teacher.
- The collaborator's cells give several rows per trial where summarization was used. Every row is scored and tasks are the resampling unit, so token-weighted means let longer traces weigh more.
- The collaborator's dataset card records a rendering difference between teachers: earlier-turn reasoning is preserved for Qwen3.8-27B and GLM-5.3-Flash but dropped for Qwen3.6-35B and the Qwen3.5 models, and the 27B and GLM traces reason about 3–6× longer per turn. Part of the NLL separation may therefore reflect rendering and trace length rather than style alone.
- Base cells are one pass and 10/05 cells are three passes, so base-versus-10/05 and 10/05-versus-10/05 comparisons do not share the same replication structure.
- The three cell families have different row and task counts, so cross-family comparisons are descriptive.
- Overlap flags come from an n-gram scan with a 10% coverage threshold, not from byte comparison; they can under- or over-flag re-serialized rows.

## Not yet measured

- **Mochi closeness: specified, not run.** A reviewed spec scores Mochi u0 on the same 13 teacher-trace cells (6,965 traces, 99.1M tokens, 39.1M loss tokens), with a three-layout packing control and a pre-registered comparison of the GLM-versus-Qwen gaps between Mochi and the Snowball base. It rides on a shared zero-step evaluation job that has not been launched, needs the parent export and a GB200 envelope, and has no clear to run. It is a nomination step for a later 8-hour data-arm follow-up, not a teacher selection, and it does not make Snowball a teacher-selection screen.
- **Open models and Inkling:** additional teacher cells for other open models and for Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small are in preparation. No reviewed numbers exist yet, so none are reported here.
- **No matched-token training comparison.** No SFT arm has been trained on high- versus low-closeness data at matched tokens. The design is in the companion experiment issue: [Does teacher closeness predict SFT outcome?](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11673).

## Evidence

- Single-pass cells, four cells: `s3://marin-rno2a/tmp/ttl=14d/closeness-scores/task442-20261113-r1/` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-rno2a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D14d%2Fcloseness-scores%2Ftask442-20261113-r1%2F)); per-row means `per-row-mean-nll.jsonl` SHA256 `bf282a019175dcd55520a80c5a58776dfc49e0db42f2e21ba06d4371f52550b2`; execution manifest SHA256 `3ddcfaaaa9529ef1a9248d6acac8b24e10991eb2b03f7eccdc1aa8e94d4e268d`. These 14-day objects expire around 2026-11-27.
- Three-pass campaign, cells and runs: `s3://marin-rno2a/tmp/ttl=14d/teacher-nll/cells/` and `s3://marin-rno2a/tmp/ttl=14d/teacher-nll/runs/` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-rno2a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D14d%2Fteacher-nll%2F)). Named run prefixes: `1005-5e2ba6e9-run-a`, `1005-5e2ba6e9-run-b`, `1005-5e2ba6e9-run-c`, and `base-skew8-5e2ba6e9`. Text-only columns come from the campaign's retained per-cell analysis outputs for the 10/05 and base passes.
- Pooled-token RSR pass: `s3://marin-rno2a/tmp/ttl=30d/teacher-nll/runs/1005-rsr-cbf7a7a3/pass-0/` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-rno2a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fteacher-nll%2Fruns%2F1005-rsr-cbf7a7a3%2Fpass-0%2F)), job `/karan/teacher-nll-direct-80caf89c`, scorer branch `task/teacher-nll-rsr` at commit `cbf7a7a3d56695815ba08659a1edc40ee703115b`. Reviewed table object `rsr-table.json` SHA256 `7369b0424d46171abc1a3b66a3f4d84595c15093c99914202a09eacbb51f1143`; receipt SHA256 `58e97cc789a57e12181403eb962b9802881a151396f64436bc4561d1f2852ded`; pre-registered gates SHA256 `9eb8f882b9a917fe020a1f8e2bc080a4c4c297e70d61c408a84418e9b12616b0`. The 30-day objects expire around 2026-12-18.
- Overlap scan: `gs://marin-us-central2/tmp/ttl=14d/teacher-nll/overlap/84a20180/` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#gs%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-central2%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D14d%2Fteacher-nll%2Foverlap%2F84a20180%2F)); per-row file `per-row-overlap.jsonl.gz` SHA256 `7309c850916d5434450e3cbe7f941b12e94ca27f103ea6f73924a4f93626da4c`. A retained local archive of the same scan exists; the GCS copy is the shared one, and no S3 mirror has been independently verified.
- Row-level flags: the campaign's per-row exposure sidecar, which carries overlap flags rather than bootstrap output, described in the campaign note.
- Collaborator traces: [marianna13/rts-tmax-teacher-traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marianna13/rts-tmax-teacher-traces) at revision `bc3de8cb90341da0259404e9d054a73978e04a64`, CC-BY-4.0.

# Research

The 13-cell campaign measures Snowball's token-weighted NLL, but no matched-token training result tests whether its ranking predicts SFT gains. Trace length, reasoning retention, task pool, and prior exposure can change the score; cross-pool means are descriptive. [#11673](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11673) already specifies the matched training comparison, and no open PR addresses this measurement follow-up.

# Plan

1. Pin the exact 13 campaign cell manifests, scorer revisions, row IDs, masks, and retained per-row outputs before the 14-day evidence objects expire. Record missing rows and checksums; keep contrib-full separate because it has no paired cell.
2. Score target-token rank capped at 100 and RSR on those same rendered rows under the 10/05 SFT checkpoint and pre-SFT parent, using the existing NLL masks. Verify token positions and NLL against the retained campaign outputs before interpreting RSR.
3. Report NLL and RSR rankings within each shared task pool, with task-clustered intervals and per-cell token and length censuses. Split the contributor comparison by task family and overlap flag, including the TMax subset with no identified trajectory copies; keep all-token and text-only results distinct.
4. Pass the resulting teacher ranking and confound checks to [#11673](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11673) for its matched-token, matched-task training arms. Change the Mochi teacher shortlist only after that issue's predeclared evaluation gate; the pending Mochi u0 scoring also needs its parent export and GB200 envelope before launch.

issues.title: [post-training] Measured student NLL closeness to teacher traces

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Summary

- **Motivation:** Earlier closeness measurements scored candidate teachers under Snowball (issue 11674), leaving open which open-weight models Mochi SFT itself is closest to and whether Mochi is a near or far teacher for Snowball.
- **Goal:** Measure which open-weight models Mochi SFT (535B-A23B, step 400407) is closest to in likelihood and next-action behavior, and check whether Mochi's teacher closeness ranking matches Snowball 10/05's.
- **Data:** 50-row pilot slices from the 14 trace cells in issue 11674, 7 additional Nemotron v3 cells (5 in-mix and 2 held-out; Nemotron v3 is 80.64% of the 968,596 SFT packs shared by both models), 200 shared prompt cuts for next-turn continuations, and 100 train-side TMax terminal-agent tasks.
- **Method:** Score the 14 pilot cells and 7 Nemotron v3 cells under Mochi SFT and compare with Snowball 10/05's NLL and capped RSR; score Mochi's greedy and temperature-0.7 continuations at the 200 cuts under Snowball 10/05 and compare extracted command strings; run Mochi as a Terminus-2 agent on the 100 TMax tasks.
- **Results:** Mochi had lower NLL than Snowball 10/05 on all 14 pilot cells (gaps of 0.04–0.32 nats/token; Spearman rank correlation 1.000 over cell NLL) and on all 7 Nemotron v3 cells (0.03–0.06 nats/token on the 5 trained cells and 0.05–0.07 on the 2 held-out cells). At the 200 cuts, Snowball 10/05's pooled NLL was 0.384 on teacher turns, 0.255 on Mochi temperature-0.7 turns, and 0.130 on Mochi greedy turns. On the 100 TMax tasks, 27 of the 63 tasks that received a verifier reward passed (42.9%); the other 37 had no reward because of sandbox, verifier, or deadline limits.
- **Conclusion:** Mochi and Snowball 10/05 rank the 14 candidate teacher cells in the same NLL order, with larger Mochi NLL gaps on the more distant Qwen3.8 and GLM cells and smaller gaps on Nemotron v3. Because these are likelihood and descriptive agent measurements on small pilot slices (and 37 of 100 TMax tasks lacked a verifier reward), they do not test which teacher produces better SFT outcomes (issue 11673).

## Description

Parent: [issue 11535](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535). Companion measurements: [issue 11674](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11674) (Snowball student NLL closeness to teacher traces) and [issue 11673](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11673) (does closeness predict SFT outcome).

- **(a) Mochi as scorer.**
  - Mochi scores a pilot sample from each of the 14 trace cells in issue 11674, then the full cells if feasible.
  - The existing 10/05 token IDs and loss masks are the reference inputs. We will pin the shared tokenizer and template and verify token-ID and scored-position parity on the scoring route before publishing side-by-side results.
  - Reported per cell: mean NLL (all loss tokens and text-only), pooled-token RSR with ranks capped at 100, and the share of loss tokens above the rank cap.
  - The 14-cell comparator is the one-pass pooled-token RSR subsection of issue 11674.
- **(b) Mochi as teacher.**
  - Mochi continues teacher traces at seeded assistant-turn positions.
  - Snowball 10/05 scores the original teacher turn and Mochi's turn at the same position, paired.
  - Each comparator with prompt logprobs scores the same rendered assistant content, conditioned on the same preceding history, using its own tokenizer. We report nats per UTF-8 byte of the scored content, document token-boundary handling, and use the original teacher turn and the comparator's own continuation as within-scorer references.
- **(c) Behaviour.**
  - At the same cut positions and with the same tool schema, compare the next-action type and tool name, then compare a prespecified named argument for supported tools.
  - Report coverage and counts for no-call, invalid and unknown outcomes.
  - Compare BFCL ×5 per-task outcomes only where task, harness and repeat accounting permit a matched comparison.
- **Agent traces.** Select train-side TMax terminal and/or SWE-smith tasks. Identify and pin the original recording harness before calling the traces harness-matched. Keep verifier-confirmed successes as a candidate set for separate review.

Candidate models (availability and routing to be verified): Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, Qwen3.8-27B, GLM-5.3-Flash, GLM 5.3, Kimi-K2.5, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MiniMax-M2.5, gpt-oss-120b.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find which open-weight models' traces and behaviour are closest to Mochi, and whether Mochi is a near or far teacher for Snowball, as inputs to choosing teachers and data for the Mochi post-training mix.

## What this cannot show

- Likelihood and agreement are not quality.
- They do not show what training on a trace set would do; issue 11673 tests that.
- Low NLL can reflect prior exposure.
- Per-byte NLL across tokenizers is directional likelihood only. Tokenization and serve conventions differ materially between models.
- For likelihood scoring, we plan three fresh scoring passes on the same rows and report the within-setup spread. Generation and behaviour repeat counts are reported separately.

## Data rule

- The scoring and continuation prompt sets are measurements and do not become training data. They are excluded from the candidate trace set.
- Agent runs use train-side tasks only, bound to the frozen eval and TMax holdout deny lists before any run.

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:

🤖

# Research

[#11674](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11674) has Snowball NLL and capped-rank results for the 14 trace cells, but its Mochi u0 pass has not run; this issue targets a different checkpoint, Mochi SFT step 400407. The existing [BFCL ×5 readout](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11538) supplies a Mochi baseline, but its Snowball comparison differs in hardware and code version. No open PR links to #11722, and none of these measurements answers the matched-turn or agent-trace questions here.

# Plan

1. Freeze a measurement packet before any GPU run: the Mochi SFT export and serve revision, all 14 input-cell revisions and row IDs, 10/05 token IDs and loss masks, shared tokenizer/template, sampled assistant-turn cuts, tool schema, task IDs, seeds, and a GPU/time budget. Preserve the [expiring per-row Snowball artifacts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11674) before their stated November 27 TTL. Keep the standalone contrib-full cell separate from paired comparisons.
2. Run a small Mochi scoring pilot on every cell. On the retained 16-row parity fixture, check token IDs, target positions, and prompt-logprob indexing against the frozen masks, then compare Mochi serving loss with a native-model loss check. Report the gate result and measured cost before expanding to full cells. For each eligible full cell, run three fresh scoring passes and publish all-token and text-only NLL, pooled-token RSR at rank cap 100, over-cap share, task-clustered uncertainty, and pass-to-pass spread.
3. Freeze shared seeded assistant-turn cuts for teacher continuation and next-action agreement. Score the original and Mochi turns with Snowball 10/05 as paired rows. For each comparator that supports prompt logprobs, score the same assistant content under its own tokenizer and report nats per UTF-8 byte, boundary handling, the original-turn reference, and its own-continuation reference. Record models that cannot serve or score under the frozen protocol instead of filling gaps with unmatched results.
4. At those same cuts and tool schema, report next-action type, tool-name agreement, and a prespecified argument for supported tools, with explicit no-call, invalid, unknown, and denominator counts. Use [#11538](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11538) for BFCL context; compare per-task ×5 outcomes only after task IDs, harness, and repeat accounting match.
5. Pin the original TMax/SWE-smith recording harness and the frozen eval/holdout deny lists before train-side agent runs. Keep verifier-confirmed successes in a separately reviewed candidate set, excluding all scoring and continuation prompts. Publish manifests, coverage, cost, and null results here; pass any teacher-selection claim to [#11673](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11673)'s matched-token training gate.

**Pilot results: Mochi (hero-sft-step400407) vs Snowball 10/05 on the 14 scored cells. Mochi has lower NLL than Snowball 10/05 in all 14 pilot cells, and all pre-registered tolerances pass.**

**Extracted command-string agreement, greedy / T 0.7, 50 cuts per pool**
The heuristic compares the first whitespace-delimited field ("word") and the stripped string ("exact"), with completion and JSON fallbacks. It does not match tool identity or verify validity.

**k=20 throughput check for a soft-target experiment (same serve)**
- **Inputs:** 324 single conversations, two from each of 162 sampled general training-cache sources, with 4.34M input positions attempted.
- **Rate:** at concurrency 8 over 5.53 minutes, the client made 58.6 requests/min and processed 768k input positions/min on successful requests (4.25M total). The median successful request was 4.9 s and the longest 63 s.
- **Failures:** six requests returned HTTP 502 (1.9%), at lengths of 2.7k–30.7k positions. The length relationship and cause are unresolved. No timeouts were recorded.
- **Payload:** successful replies used about 1,390 raw JSON bytes per input position.
- **Top-20 mass:** among successful requests, the median rank-≤20 returned mass fell in the ≥0.999 histogram bin for both all scored positions and assistant targets. The fifth percentile fell in that bin for all scored positions and in the [0.998, 0.999) bin for assistant targets. The top bin includes overflow because the histogram clamps. This is a binned measurement, not a mass-closure check.
- **Projections for 164 packs (43.0M positions), at the measured successful throughput and payload rate:**
  - about 0.93 h at concurrency 8;
  - about 60 GB of raw HTTP JSON;
  - storage at 20 entries × 6 bytes: about 5.16 GB for all inputs, or about 1.92 GB at the observed 37.3% assistant-target share. With a 21st slot for the actual token, up to about 5.42 GB and 2.02 GB respectively, before overhead.
  - The pilot observed 6/324 HTTP 502s. Any larger run should predeclare retry and coverage accounting.

**Next (planned):** a train-side TMax agent run at T 0.7; Snowball 10/05 NLL on Mochi's continuations vs the teacher's turns at the same cuts; Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B scoring of Mochi's continuations.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
**Mochi as a Terminus-2 agent on 100 train-side TMax tasks at T 0.7: 27 of the 63 tasks with a verifier reward passed (42.9%, Wilson 95% 31–55%). The other 37 tasks have no reward because of sandbox, verifier or deadline limits, so this is not a success rate for all 100.**

**Run**
- Harbor + Terminus-2 on Daytona, one attempt per task, no retries. The model was served through the shared endpoint at temperature 0.7, top_p 1.0 and fixed seed 20261119 on every request.
- **Tasks:** 100 train-side TMax tasks, none in the E12 TMax training rows. Held-out, eval and earlier measurement tasks were excluded.
- **Run 1** (concurrency 8, 600 s build limit): 17 tasks received a verifier reward; 75 hit the environment-start timeout, 7 had a cancellation-phase error after that timeout, and 1 was killed by tmux.
- **Rerun of those 83** (concurrency 4, 1,800 s build limit, 3 h 45 min deadline): 46 more received a verifier reward, and 2 additional tasks reached the verifier but timed out there without a reward.

**Final status of the 100 tasks**
| Status | Tasks |
|---|---|
| Verifier reward 1 | 27 |
| Verifier reward 0 | 36 |
| Verifier timed out after the agent finished | 2 |
| Sandbox build failed (provider `BUILD_FAILED`) | 6 |
| Terminal session killed mid-run | 3 |
| Cancelled or not started at the rerun deadline | 26 |

- **Selection:** The 63 tasks with verifier rewards are those whose sandboxes built in time and whose verifiers returned rewards. They are not a random sample; heavier images may be under-represented. The 2 verifier timeouts are not scored. The deadline tasks are the last in a hash order.
- **Format:** no trial ended on a format failure. Invalid-JSON turns were recovered on the next turn.
- **Agent runs:** median 12 turns and about 11 minutes per trial in the rerun (run 1: 11.5 turns, about 10 minutes).
- **Scope:** Snowball/Mochi base-mix TMax exposure is unverified; these tasks are only known not to be in the E12 TMax training rows. There is no baseline agent on the same tasks in this run.
- **Label:** "shared endpoint, unpinned serve; vLLM, tp 1, bfloat16, 262,144 ctx (owner screenshot, 2026-11-19)". `/v1/models` showed the same model id and root before and after each run.

comments.body:
**Nemotron v3 in the Mochi vs Snowball 10/05 similarity table. Nemotron v3 is 80.6% of the SFT packs for both models; they trained on the same 216-store mix. Mochi's NLL is lower than Snowball 10/05's on all seven Nemotron v3 cells. The gap is 0.03–0.06 nats/token on five cells both models trained on, and 0.05–0.07 on two held-out cells. These sit at the small end of the 14 existing cells' range (0.04–0.32).**

**1. Nemotron v3 share of the SFT data**
- **One mix for both models:** Mochi's store manifest equals the 10/05 run's `allocations_tokens` for all 216 stores, with 0 mismatches. Both runs read each store once, in proportion to its packs, plus replay. For 10/05, `sft_fraction` is 0.7965.
- **Units:** packs of 262,144 tokens; padding is not subtracted.

| Nemotron v3 families | Packs | % of SFT packs |
|---|---|---|
| Math (math_v2, v3, v4) | 327,290 | 33.79 |
| Coding (competitive_programming_v2, cuda_v1) | 115,099 | 11.88 |
| Multilingual (v1, v2) | 107,434 | 11.09 |
| Math proofs (v1 Lean, v2) | 62,723 | 6.48 |
| Finance (finance_v1) | 38,143 | 3.94 |
| Science (science_v2) | 36,270 | 3.74 |
| Agentic / tool calling (agentic_v1, v2, opencode_v1) | 33,183 | 3.43 |
| Chat / instruction following (v2, v3) | 30,981 | 3.20 |
| SWE (swe_v1, swe_v2 openhands) | 18,855 | 1.95 |
| ARC-AGI (arc_agi_v1) | 10,603 | 1.09 |
| Safety (v1, v2) | 515 | 0.05 |
| **All nemotron_sft_v3 (64 stores)** | **781,096** | **80.64** |
| All SFT (216 stores) | 968,596 | 100 |

- Of all 10/05 training draws, including replay, Nemotron v3 is about 64% (0.7965 × 0.8064).
- **Not counted above:** 34 other stores (5,662 packs, 0.58%) are traces from GLM, MiniMax and Qwen models on Nemotron-Gym tasks.

**2. Which models generated the Nemotron v3 data (from the dataset cards)**

| Family (% of SFT packs) | Generator named on the card | Open weights |
|---|---|---|
| math_v3 (20.4) | DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale (chain of thought), DeepSeek-V3.2 (Python tool use) | yes |
| competitive_programming_v2 (11.9) | not stated | — |
| math_v2 (10.6) | gpt-oss-120b | yes |

- No single generator dominates.
- Families or splits whose card names only DeepSeek-V3.2/V4 or gpt-oss-120b make up 40.5% of the SFT packs: math_v3, math_v2, math_v4, finance_v1, math_proofs_v2, and the 2,781 packs of instruction_following_chat_v3's instruction_following split. Those two are the clearest open-weight candidates for scoring in the reverse direction.

**3. Mochi and Snowball 10/05 NLL on Nemotron v3 cells**
- **Cells:** 50 documents each, drawn by a fixed hash order from the in-region training stores. The assistant-only mask is the same as in the 14 existing cells.
- **Same scoring paths as the 14 cells.** Snowball: the [11674](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11674) scorer, unchanged. Mochi: k=0 prompt logprobs, averaged over 3 passes.
- **All five cells were in both models' SFT (one epoch).** These are exposure-positive reference cells, not a held-out similarity measure.

| Cell (in SFT: yes, both) | Scored tokens | Mochi NLL | Snowball NLL | Mochi − Snowball (95% CI) | Capped RSR, Mochi / Snowball |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| math_v3 | 724,261 | 0.4648 | 0.5114 | −0.047 (−0.051, −0.042) | 2.92 / 2.79 |
| competitive_programming_v2, python | 1,189,715 | 0.5910 | 0.6528 | −0.062 (−0.067, −0.056) | 2.50 / 2.41 |
| math_v2, high | 791,059 | 0.7381 | 0.7696 | −0.032 (−0.035, −0.029) | 2.75 / 2.75 |
| multilingual_v1 | 468,994 | 0.5150 | 0.5527 | −0.038 (−0.046, −0.031) | 3.15 / 3.06 |
| opencode_v1 | 129,621 | 0.1357 | 0.1672 | −0.032 (−0.038, −0.026) | 8.07 / 6.84 |

- The CI is a descriptive paired bootstrap over the 50 documents.
- **Training data does not mean low NLL.** math_v2 high sits at 0.74–0.77 nats/token for both models even though it was trained on. Four of the 14 existing cells sit lower (0.26–0.29 for Snowball).
- **Gaps:** Mochi is lower on every cell, by 0.03–0.06. That is the same direction as all 14 existing cells, where the gap runs from −0.039 (Qwen3.5-9B TMax) to −0.321 (GLM-5.3-flash TMax).
- **Selection:** in the competitive-programming cell, 11 of the first 61 candidates were longer than the scorer's 73,727-token limit and were skipped. So that cell under-represents the longest solutions.

**Gates**
- **Snowball parity-16 (packet A):** the largest per-row difference is 0.0021 nats/token, against a 0.025 tolerance: pass.
- **Mochi per cell over 3 passes (packet A):** NLL spread at most 0.00015 nats/token and capped-RSR spread at most 0.008: pass.
- **Mochi control row (packet A): fail, by 0.14 nats.** It was scored 6 times, and its summed NLL took three discrete values: 472.80, 473.57 and 474.94. That is a 2.14-nat spread against the pre-registered 2.0.
  - **What this does to the reading:** on the row's 3,691 scored tokens, the spread is about 0.0006 nats/token. That is about 50–110 times smaller than the Mochi − Snowball gaps of 0.03–0.06 in the five cells, and each cell was stable across passes (spread ≤ 0.00015 nats/token).
  - The control-row spread is small relative to the observed cell gaps, but this single control does not bound serve variation for every cell. Because the pre-registered control gate failed, the section-3 comparisons remain descriptive and could still be affected by serve variation.
- **/v1/models:** identical before and after every pass. The Mochi serve label is "shared endpoint, unpinned serve; vLLM, tp 1, bfloat16, 262,144 ctx (owner screenshot, 2026-11-19)"; its build and commit are unknown.

**4. Held-out Nemotron v3 cells: not in SFT; pretraining exposure unknown**
- **Source:** two Nemotron v3 partitions that are registered in our pipeline but were not packed into either SFT.
- **Rows:** 50 rows from the first 400 lines of each pinned file. They were rendered with the stores' own pipeline at the packing commit. That pipeline reproduces training-store documents token for token: 29/29 on cuda_v1, plus 12/12 on each held-out partition's in-SFT sibling, checked independently.
- **What "held out" covers:** these trajectories were not in SFT, but the same tasks may have been. Agentless shares SWE task sources with the in-SFT openhands_swe trajectories, and agent_skills_question_tool shares its question generator with in-SFT agent_skills.

| Cell (not in SFT) | Generator (card) | Scored tokens | Mochi NLL | Snowball NLL | Mochi − Snowball (95% CI) | Capped RSR, Mochi / Snowball |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| swe_v2 agentless | DeepSeek-R1-0528 | 163,472 | 0.5254 | 0.5998 | −0.074 (−0.084, −0.066) | 2.70 / 2.57 |
| opencode_v1 agent_skills_question_tool | Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct | 147,972 | 0.2269 | 0.2769 | −0.050 (−0.059, −0.042) | 5.25 / 4.61 |

- **Gates (all pass):**
  - Snowball parity-16: largest per-row difference 0.0028 nats/token.
  - Mochi control: 0.001-nat spread over 6 scorings.
  - Per-cell 3-pass spreads: at most 0.0002 (NLL) and 0.002 (RSR).
- **Reading:**
  - On these two held-out cells, Mochi is again lower, by 0.05–0.07 nats/token. That is slightly more than on the five exposure-positive cells (0.03–0.06).
  - Both models score the held-out opencode subset higher (0.23 / 0.28) than the in-SFT opencode_v1 cell (0.14 / 0.17).
  - These are descriptive comparisons on 50 rows each; the subsets differ, not only the exposure.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
🤖 **Literature review and three proposed one-hour Snowball SFT experiments testing external Mochi soft targets (Beyer et al., arXiv:2106.05237) and full-vocabulary self-anchoring (Ambient SFT, arXiv:2611.23229).**

## Summary

- **Motivation:** In the one-hour FP32 Snowball SFT pair, hard-label edit and TMax traces scored 337/855 (.394) against 222/855 (.260) for the control on the edit-call eval, but averaged 39.47% vs 41.59% on Micro210 suite and 14.99% vs 20.00% on Micro210 agent. We wanted to check whether teacher soft targets or temperature-matched self-anchoring could help transfer or retention.
- **Goal:** Review teacher soft-target distillation (Beyer et al., arXiv:2106.05237) and full-vocabulary temperature-matched self-anchoring (Ambient SFT, arXiv:2611.23229), and design one-hour Snowball SFT experiments to test whether soft targets or self-anchoring help agent transfer or retention.
- **Data:** Three proposed one-hour FP32 Snowball SFT experiment designs (60 updates each): Mochi top-20 plus residual-tail KL on Mochi traces, prefill-only Mochi soft targets on general replay, and full-vocabulary temperature-matched KL (T=2.5) anchored to the starting checkpoint.
- **Method:** Literature review, experimental design, and CPU-tested draft trainer implementations for full-vocabulary temperature matching (PR 11726) and cached top-k KL (PR 11727).
- **Results:** No GPU training runs were executed. Both trainer PRs remain CPU-tested draft reference code only.
- **Conclusion:** All three experiments are unrun and parked (PR 11726 and PR 11727 remain parked drafts, and the 10/05 self-anchoring experiment was dropped because the plan no longer continues SFT from 10/05, issue 11687). Whether soft targets improve agent transfer over hard-label SFT remains untested.

## Parent, scope, and context

Parent: [issue 11535](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535). Background SFT results: [issue 11687 SFT summary](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11687#issuecomment-7000153313) and [one-hour edit-call comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11687#issuecomment-6996439113).

**Scope for all three proposals:** Train-side only; nothing has been run yet for these designs. Each proposal requires verified held-out separation across generation, scoring, and training, plus a fixed one-hour decision rule before scaling to eight hours. Lower held-out teacher NLL measures imitation of the teacher; edit-call, BFCL, Micro210, and general retention are separate outcomes. Experiments 1 and 2 test transferring Mochi's existing capabilities into Snowball as a proxy for soft vs hard distillation; diagnosing Mochi's own weaknesses is tracked separately under [issue 11535](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535).

In the one-hour FP32 pair (`60` updates, fresh state, LR `2e-5`), hard-label `E12-B + TMax` scored `337/855` (`.394`) on `eval-r2` versus `222/855` (`.260`) for its matched general-only control (`+13.45` pp, higher on all 11 tasks). On Micro210 (two repeats of one BF16 export per arm), treatment averaged `39.47%` suite and `14.99%` agent versus `41.59%` suite and `20.00%` agent for control: suite difference `−2.13` pp (missing-outcome bounds `−2.96` to `−1.25` pp; control repeat spread `3.06` pp) and agent difference `−5.01` pp (missing-outcome bounds `−8.45` to `−0.95` pp; control repeat spread `6.32` pp).

Current infrastructure facts and input-parity gates:
- **Shared Mochi probe:** A shared Mochi serve with an unpinned build accepted `k=20` on the probe. The observed response included the actual token in addition to the top-20 when it was outside that set.
- **Tokenizer and template parity:** Mochi and Snowball 10/05 share the same pinned/configured `128,256`-token tokenizer and chat template; request-level token-ID parity against the unpinned serve still requires verification before scoring.
- **Checked student MoE routing:** The checked Snowball SFT student path runs with `expert_axis_size = 1` (local `sonic` MoE kernel, dropless with `0` dropped assignments). Dropless local routing applies to the checked student path and says nothing about teacher input identity.
- **Unpack/repack gate:** Snowball packs multiple documents into `262,144`-token rows isolated by `segment_ids`, whereas a single-prompt completions request attends across the full prompt. Any cached-logprob distillation must unpack rows into single conversations before Mochi scoring, repack with matching `segment_ids`, and gate on identical prefix token IDs, boundary masks, position semantics, and target-token offsets, reporting coverage for any unalignable documents.

## Paper review: Beyer et al. (2106.05237) beside Ambient SFT (2611.23229)

[Beyer et al. (2021 / CVPR 2022)](https://arxiv.org/html/2106.05237) study image classification distillation as **function matching** from a stronger external teacher, testing consistent views, mixup, long schedules, and a temperature sweep (reaching `82.82%` ImageNet top-1 with ResNet-50 from a BiT teacher at `9,600` epochs). Four takeaways and our adaptations connect to Snowball SFT:

1. **Consistent inputs:** In Beyer et al., student and teacher must see the exact same input view. Applying that principle here means gating distillation on the unpack/repack alignment check above rather than relying on tokenizer configuration or student-side dropless routing alone.
2. **Soft targets vs narrow hard labels (our hypothesis for agent transfer):** Beyer et al. showed that matching a strong teacher's soft targets transferred well across broad vision inputs; whether the same carries over to broad agent-capability transfer in LLMs is our hypothesis to test. By contrast, programmatic one-hot `E12-B` edits target a narrow synthetic fixture, and `TMax` (`allenai/tmax-sft`, Qwen3.6-27B traces) comes from a different teacher checkpoint; Snowball's use of those traces applies full-trace CE over all roles (supervised target shares in the selected `123` packs: `47.5%` assistant, `33.4%` tool outputs, `13.9%` user prompts, `3.9%` system/schemas, `1.3%` role headers).
3. **Patience vs our short budgets:** Beyer et al. found benefits from long vision-distillation schedules and reported their best ImageNet result at `9,600` epochs. Our one-hour run is `60` updates (`0.1579%` of 10/05 SFT) and an eight-hour run is `480` updates (`1.2632%` of 10/05). One-hour runs are directional screens, not tests of the patient ceiling.
4. **Top-$k$ truncation bridge:** [Busbridge et al. (2025), Appendix G.4](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.08606#A7.SS4) report that mixing top-$k$ distillation with ground-truth CE at `k=128`, `lambda=0.7` reached validation loss within `0.01` nats of full distillation in their setup. That result motivates mixing CE with truncated KL, but it did not test our `k=20`, residual-tail, teacher-generated-label objective.

[Ambient SFT (arXiv:2611.23229)](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.23229) uses a frozen pretrained scorer at `T=2.5` (full vocabulary, omitting Hinton's $T^2$ factor) in its instruction-tuning recipe; anchoring continuation SFT to frozen `10/05` is our adaptation. Ambient SFT Appendix D.5 raises temperatures for poorly fit sources; turning the regularizer ON/OFF per source is our proposed change, and the paper does not establish a Snowball new-skill tax.

| Dimension | [Beyer et al. (`2106.05237`)](https://arxiv.org/html/2106.05237) + [Busbridge App. G.4 (`2502.08606`)](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.08606#A7.SS4) | [Ambient SFT (`2611.23229`)](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.23229) (our `10/05` adaptation) |
|---|---|---|
| **Teacher** | Stronger external model (Mochi) | Frozen starting checkpoint (Snowball `10/05`) |
| **Temperature & vocab** | $T=1$, explicit top-20 + actual token + residual tail bin | $T=2.5$ (no Hinton $T^2$ factor), full `128,256` vocabulary |
| **Hypothesis for Snowball** | Test whether soft targets transfer Mochi behavior better than narrow synthetic/hard labels | Test whether full-vocab tail anchoring reduces forgetting during short continuation SFT |
| **Fits Mochi `k=20` endpoint?** | **Yes at $T=1$ with CE mix + residual tail bin** (actual Mochi top-20 mass coverage to be measured on a pilot sample) | **No — requires full vocabulary in-trainer:** $T=2.5$ spreads mass past rank 20, breaking the tail anchor |

## Proposed one-hour Snowball experiments

All three proposals share a **one-hour scale**: `60 × 32 × 262,144 = 503,316,480` scheduled positions per arm (`0.1579%` of 10/05 SFT, FP32 stored parameters). Under the continuation rule from `10/05`, carried FP32 optimizer state at cooled-down LR `5.094738e-6` is the default. Using a `10`-update linear warmup to `2e-5` instead requires its own decision and must be paired with a newly matched same-schedule control.

### Experiment 1: Mochi soft targets (top-20 + tail KL + CE) vs hard-label Mochi traces

- **One-hour version:** Replace the `164` added packs with `~164` packs of Mochi-generated coding/agent traces (`T=0.7`, assistant-only loss mask), mixed with general replay in identical examples, order, and masks across two matched `60`-update FP32 arms:
  - **Arm 1A (hard labels):** `L_total = L_CE` averaged over all supervised tokens in the batch (general replay + Mochi assistant tokens).
  - **Arm 1B (soft targets):** `L_total = ce_weight * L_CE + kl_weight * L_KL` at **$T=1$ only** (e.g., `ce_weight = 0.5`, `kl_weight = 0.5`), where `L_CE` keeps the exact same full-batch supervised target set and denominator as Arm 1A (general replay CE remains active with identical masks) and `L_KL` is the weighted mean of coarse-grained forward KL over KL-selected Mochi assistant tokens (normalized by actual valid KL weight mass, with zero contribution on empty selections). For each KL token, validate and deduplicate full-softmax logprobs and mass closure over `{top-20} ∪ {actual token}`, compute the exact non-explicit tail bucket within numerical tolerance using zero-mass limits, and reject invalid rows with coverage reported. Unmodified probability vectors coarsened into explicit singleton bins plus the remainder give a KL lower bound; the tail bin represents omitted mass, not its internal distribution (and cached top-20 logprobs are never rescaled to $T \neq 1$). Log `||grad_KL|| / ||grad_CE||` so step-size scaling is visible.
  - **Comparators:** Newly matched general-only CE control on the same continuation schedule and checkpoint. Existing `E12-B + TMax` runs used fresh state and a different data/mask recipe, so retain them as context only; `1A` vs `1B` estimates the matched objective contrast on identical examples, order, and masks, while comparing `1A` to historical `E12-B + TMax` cannot isolate the teacher/data effect.
- **What it would show:** Compares the mixed CE-plus-soft-target objective with vanilla CE (`1B` vs `1A`) on identical Mochi traces and masks, measured separately on held-out Mochi NLL (imitation), edit-call, BFCL, Micro210, and general retention. With the illustrative `0.5` CE coefficient, the comparison also changes CE scaling (to test adding KL at fixed CE scaling, set `ce_weight = 1.0` in both arms).
- **What it needs:**
  - *Data:* `~164` packs of Mochi traces plus cached top-20 `(token_id, logprob)` entries (`164 × 262,144 = 42,991,616` positions). Assuming `6` bytes/pair (`int32` ID + 2-byte logprob), dense storage across `20–21` slots is `5.16–5.42 GB` before framing/compression overhead; assistant-only storage depends on the measured assistant span share. Measure pilot top-20 mass coverage and alignment coverage before full collection.
  - *Trainer change:* Chunked gather-based `{top-k} ∪ {actual} + tail` KL kernel behind the same trainer interface as Experiment 3 (avoiding `[B, S, V]` logit materialization), with per-source mask and `||grad_KL|| / ||grad_CE||` watch metric; measure actual HBM delta before scaling.
  - *Serve:* Shared Mochi serve (subject to request-level tokenizer/offset parity check; no new GPU serve).
- **Main risk:** (1) Top-20 truncation misses tail mass on high-entropy reasoning tokens (mitigated by CE mix, exact complement tail bin, and a pilot check of top-20 mass closure). (2) Patience and SNR: `60` updates at `5.094738e-6` may be too short to separate `1B` from `1A` on two-repeat Micro210; gate scaling on a fixed one-hour rule across held-out Mochi NLL, edit-call, BFCL, and retention.

### Experiment 2: Mochi soft targets on unpacked general replay only (zero synthetic data)

- **One-hour version:** Train for `60` updates on the same `1,920` general replay packs as the matched general-only CE control — zero `E12-B`, zero Qwen `TMax`, zero new trace generation. Unpack up to `164` agentic/coding general packs (or a smaller assistant-filtered subset bounded by a pilot throughput/payload check) into single conversations, score with Mochi `prompt_logprobs(k=20)` (prefill-only), verify the unpack/repack parity gate and report unalignable-document coverage, and train with `L_total = ce_weight * L_CE + kl_weight * L_KL` at $T=1$. Ordinary `L_CE` keeps identical targets across both arms (including non-assistant spans in general replay) normalized by the full-batch supervised denominator; `L_KL` applies only to validated parsed assistant spans on the scored packs, normalized by actual valid KL weight mass.
- **What it would show:** Compares the mixed CE-plus-soft-target objective with vanilla CE on identical unpacked general replay without constructing synthetic data, testing our broad-transfer hypothesis across held-out Mochi NLL, edit-call, BFCL, Micro210, and general retention. If `ce_weight < 1.0`, the comparison also changes CE scaling (to test adding KL at fixed CE scaling, set `ce_weight = 1.0` in both arms).
- **What it needs:**
  - *Data:* Unpacked single-conversation prefill scoring (`k=20`) on the shared Mochi serve, repacking with `segment_ids`, alignment verification, and chat-template assistant span masks. Run a pilot throughput and payload-size measurement first on the shared proxy (`164` packs = `42,991,616` positions before assistant filtering) to size the one-hour scored slice.
  - *Trainer change:* Reuses the exact same `cached_topk_kl` trainer path as Experiment 1.
  - *Serve:* Shared Mochi serve only (prefill-only).
- **Main risk:** (1) Replay coverage: the sampled screen-1 general replay audit saw no declared native Pi nested edits, and that audit does not establish their prevalence or what the experiment can fix. (2) Shared-proxy throughput and payload volume for `k=20` prefill scoring, bounded by the pilot measurement.

### Experiment 3: Full-vocabulary Ambient SFT self-anchor (`2611.23229`) with per-source mask

- **One-hour version:** At the default cooled-down LR (`5.094738e-6`), compare matched `60`-update FP32 CE and CE-plus-TM arms from `10/05` on the same fixed mixture (`E12-B + TMax` or Experiment 1 Mochi traces) using the same frozen starting scorer (`10/05`) and token lineage. If the higher-LR schedule (`10`-update linear warmup to `2e-5`, subject to its own decision) is approved, compare CE and CE-plus-TM at that same schedule and include a newly matched `60`-update cooled-down-LR CE arm on the exact same mixture and checkpoint. (The `480`-update `Warm A` run is context only, not the matched lower-LR comparator.) Existing one-hour configs use `gradient_accumulation_steps = 4`; run temperature matching on a fixed quarter of accumulation slots (e.g., `1` of `4` microbatches, or freeze a new accumulation split common to all compared arms). Optimize `L_total = L_CE(all microbatches) + (1/3) * L_TM` at `T=2.5` (no Hinton $T^2$ factor), where `L_TM` is the weighted mean over selected eligible general-replay targets normalized by actual weight mass (with zero contribution on empty selections), with the proposed per-source mask ON for general replay and OFF for new-skill rows. The `1/3` coefficient is the proposed scalar on that restricted mean; it is not an exact effective equivalence to Ambient SFT's per-microbatch CE-or-TM switch.
- **What it would show:** Tests whether full-vocabulary `T=2.5` anchoring to frozen `10/05` improves the edit-call / BFCL / Micro210 / retention trade-off relative to matched vanilla CE at the same schedule (and, under the optional higher-LR comparison, relative to the newly matched `60`-update cooled-down-LR CE comparator; context from the historical one-hour pair: Micro210 agent difference `−5.01` pp, missing-outcome bounds `−8.45` to `−0.95` pp, control repeat spread `6.32` pp).
- **What it needs:**
  - *Data:* The existing `E12-B + TMax` option needs no new data generation or Mochi calls. The alternative uses the already collected Experiment 1 traces.
  - *Trainer change:* Unified temperature-matching PR (frozen BF16 `10/05` teacher on `pinned_host` streaming layer-by-layer, chunked full-vocabulary KL scan, per-source mask, `||grad_TM|| / ||grad_CE||` watch metric). At one teacher forward per four equal microbatch slices, ideal additional teacher work is about `25%` of one full student forward, or about `8.3%` of nominal forward+backward training FLOPs under a `3×` convention, before host-transfer, remat, and LM-head costs; actual HBM delta and step time are unmeasured and must be measured before claiming a cost.
  - *Serve:* None (the frozen teacher is evaluated in-trainer on the remote job).
- **Main risk:** (1) Masked-LR illusion: under the optional higher-LR comparison, TM must beat the newly matched `60`-update cooled-down-LR CE comparator on the new-skill vs retention frontier, not only unregularized `2e-5`. (2) MoE routing drift: smooth output KL may not prevent discrete top-4 expert flips across `256` experts.

## Recommended order

1. **First:** Experiment 3 (zero new data once the unified trainer PR lands and HBM/step-time overhead is measured) alongside a small pilot throughput, payload, and alignment check for Experiment 2 (unpacked `k=20` scoring and top-20 mass closure on the shared Mochi serve).
2. **Second:** Experiment 1 (`1A` vs `1B` on matched Mochi traces) once Mochi trace collection reaches `~164` packs, advancing only arms that clear the fixed one-hour decision rule to an eight-hour+ schedule.

# Research

Issue #11724 spans three experiment designs and a new trainer loss. The open long-loop trainer computes weighted cross entropy with a full-batch denominator; it has no teacher loss or per-source teacher mask. The FP32 60-update comparison in [#11687](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11687#issuecomment-7000153313) improved edit-call by 13.45 pp but averaged 5.01 pp lower on Micro210 agent, so that result cannot establish a teacher-loss benefit. [#11717](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11717) is changing stored-parameter precision in the same trainer; the new objectives should use its FP32 policy.

**Relevant code**
- [`train.py#L923-L970`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6676c91efe773f251d455f97c59e060b49faf1b/experiments/post_training/long_loop/sft_runtime/train.py#L923-L970) — CE and accumulation denominator.
- [`model.py#L1414-L1475`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6676c91efe773f251d455f97c59e060b49faf1b/experiments/post_training/long_loop/sft_runtime/model.py#L1414-L1475) — current fused next-token loss.
- [#11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120) — owning long-loop implementation PR.

# Proposed Fix

1. **Pin the comparison.** After #11120 and #11717 settle, record the exact 10/05 checkpoint, carried FP32 optimizer state, cooled-down LR (`5.094738e-6`), 60-update row order, source masks, and held-out IDs in an immutable run manifest. Verify generation, teacher scoring, training, and evaluation sets are disjoint. A higher-LR screen needs its own matched CE control.
2. **Pilot the Mochi input path.** Unpack a bounded sample of general replay conversations and score with `prompt_logprobs(k=20)`. Admit a document only when request token IDs, target offsets, assistant spans, segment boundaries, and repacked positions match exactly. Check duplicate IDs and probability-mass closure over top-20 plus actual token and residual tail; publish rejected-document coverage, top-20 mass, request throughput, and payload size before collecting full targets.
3. **Build and measure temperature matching first.** Add a frozen 10/05 scorer and chunked full-vocabulary KL at `T=2.5`, with CE on all existing targets and KL on eligible general-replay targets only (`1/3` coefficient, one of four accumulation slices). Compare the chunked loss and gradients with a small dense reference, including empty masks and packed boundaries. Measure HBM and step time on the actual Snowball shape before scheduling the full pair.
4. **Run matched 60-update CE and CE-plus-TM arms.** Keep checkpoint, optimizer, LR, examples, order, and CE masks identical. Publish the decision thresholds and missing-outcome rule before launch. Read out held-out teacher NLL, edit-call, BFCL, Micro210, and general retention; advance to 480 updates only if the predeclared rule passes, with repeat variance reported.
5. **Then test external soft targets.** Reuse the validated scorer and add a separate `T=1` top-20-plus-tail KL path. Keep CE weight at `1.0` in both arms so the objective contrast isolates added KL. Run matched hard-label versus soft-target Mochi traces (Experiment 1), then scored general replay versus its CE control (Experiment 2), subject to the pilot's coverage and throughput. Report KL/CE gradient-norm ratio and valid-target coverage for each run.

The first implementation PR should cover the temperature-matching loss and its reference tests; the Mochi scoring and cached-target path can follow as separate changes. No teacher-target experiment has run yet.
