spillover_issues.title: Track run-ready Snowball recipes and Micro eval policy scores

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
## Symptom

Six consecutive 64-H100 Snowball SFT jobs configured with FP32 stored weights and the 2026-11-18 optimizer assignment (routed 4-D expert banks on Adam, stacked RMS-norm weights on Muon-H) compiled on a cache miss in 18.8 to 70.2 s on task 0 and then never completed update 1:

- **Three jobs with the first-step host rebind enabled:** all 64 ranks finished the host rebind across a 13.7 to 17.6 min span (17.6 min, 13.7 min, and 15.0 min; compared with 1.7 min overall / 18 to 103 s per host on a working job with the default optimizer assignment, or 29 to 58 s on 7 hosts plus one slow ~420 s host on another). None completed update 1 after 19 to 21+ min of silence past the last rebind log, and no W&B step or peak-memory line appeared.
- **Three jobs with the first-step host rebind removed:** all three compiled in 18.8 to 25.3 s (cache miss on every rank; FP32 dtype checks logged for 27/27 parameter leaves and 39/39 optimizer leaves) and entered the same stalled state within 4.7 to 6.0 min of compile without completing update 1.

Parent: issue 11535. Related: issue 11440 (first-update stalls on Snowball SFT).

## Setup

- **Model and cluster:** Snowball 67B SFT from the pre-train base, 64 H100 GPUs (8 hosts × 8 GPUs) on `cw-us-east-02a`, FP32 stored weights, fresh optimizer state, warmup 0, learning rate `2e-5` (both Muon-H and Adam).
- **Source and optimizer assignment:** Long-loop runtime at commit `6164fcbd` with `experiments/grug/moe/optimizer.py` (and its test file) reverted to commit `3b291b10`: routed 4-D expert banks assigned to Adam, stacked RMS-norm weights assigned to Muon-H, per-group clipping with `max_grad_norm` 1.0, and `global_grad_norm`, `expert_normalization`, and `use_syrk` omitted.
- **Batch and data:** Three pretraining-replay mixture settings (20.47%, 40%, and 60% replay weight) at 32 packed rows × 262,144 tokens per update; all three settings hung identically in both batches.

## Hang evidence

Measurements across both batches distinguish a hang from slow training compute:

- **GPU power and utilisation:** Across all 48 sampled GPUs (24 GPUs across 3 hosts in the rebind-on batch: 116.1 to 162.5 W, 25 to 37 °C, flat across a 24 s repeat; 24 GPUs across 3 jobs in the rebind-off batch: 116.9 to 165.4 W), every GPU reported 116 to 165 W, 0% memory-bus utilisation, and 100% `utilization.gpu`, with no OOM or `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` log lines.
- **Cross-host InfiniBand traffic:** On two hosts of a hung rebind-off job sampled 127.2 s apart, total InfiniBand port data counters (transmit plus receive across all ports) moved by 1.67 MB on one host (0.05 MB transmit, 1.62 MB receive) and 1.76 MB on the other (0.09 MB transmit, 1.67 MB receive).
- **Host thread dumps:** In native thread dumps of hung tasks, every captured rank main thread (8/8 ranks on one host in the rebind-on batch; 8/8 ranks on one host and 4/8 captured ranks on another host in the rebind-off batch) was blocked in `jax::BlockUntilReadyWithCancel` (`block_until_ready`) waiting for update 1 to complete.
- **Independent of concurrent jobs:** After two of the three rebind-on jobs were cancelled, the remaining job stayed in the same state (121 to 127 W, 0% memory-bus utilisation, no new log lines) for ~9 more minutes until cancelled.

## Controls

- **Same runtime, `6164fcbd` optimizer (routed expert banks on Muon-H), FP32 stored weights:** Four jobs (two compile pre-jobs and two main training runs at 40% and 60% replay weight, in addition to the earlier 20.47% control pair) ran on the same cluster without hanging. For the 40% and 60% arms respectively, the pre-jobs compiled in 20.4 s and 25.5 s and completed update 1 in 710.1 s (including one slow ~420 s host rebind that kept advancing) and 245.5 s; the main runs loaded the cached executable, completed update 1 in 292.5 s and 187.9 s, and ran steady-state updates 3 to 6 at medians of 49.3 s and 52.1 s.
- **Older runtime, `3b291b10` optimizer, BF16 stored weights:** The 2026-11-18 from-base control used the `3b291b10` optimizer assignment with BF16 stored weights on an older runtime and completed training.

## What is not established

The mechanism of the hang is not established. Stopping two of the three concurrent jobs did not unblock the remaining job, and removing the first-step host rebind did not prevent the hang; no further isolation has been run.

## Question

What changes are needed to run the `3b291b10` optimizer assignment (routed 4-D expert banks on Adam, stacked RMS-norm weights on Muon-H, `max_grad_norm` 1.0) with FP32 stored weights and optimizer state on the current long-loop runtime without hanging on update 1?

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The long-loop step JITs gradient accumulation and `optimizer.update` together, so the blocked `block_until_ready` does not identify the stalled operation. Six FP32 runs with routed expert banks on Adam stalled, while FP32 runs with expert banks on Muon-H completed; the BF16/Adam control used an older runtime. This leaves the dtype, optimizer grouping, and runtime interaction unresolved. [#11440](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11440#issuecomment-6923812082) also found a gradient-only stall, and [#11646](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11646#issuecomment-7015968717) separates cache-miss slow steps from the still-open first-step stall. The cited `3b291b10` commit is unavailable in this checkout and from the public GitHub commit API, so the exact reverted optimizer source needs a durable pin.

**Relevant code**
- [`sft_runtime/train.py#L1083-L1100`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6164fcbd/experiments/post_training/long_loop/sft_runtime/train.py#L1083-L1100) — fused gradient and optimizer step.
- [`optimizer.py#L303-L323`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6164fcbd/experiments/grug/moe/optimizer.py#L303-L323) — current per-group clipping and transforms.
- [PR #11639](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11639) — separate expert-MuonH grouping work.
- [PR #11640](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11640) — pending long-loop optimizer selection.

# Proposed Fix

1. Preserve the exact reverted optimizer diff or reachable commit, the per-leaf group mask, consumed config, parameter and optimizer-state dtypes, source/image revisions, XLA flags, and compilation-cache hit/miss for each existing run. Keep the first-update deadline and per-rank progress records with each trial.
2. On the same 64-H100 mesh, checkpoint, data order, fresh state, rebind setting, and cache policy, run the missing **current-runtime BF16 + Adam-expert** cell first. Compare it with the existing FP32 + Adam-expert failures and a matched FP32 + Muon-H control. Repeat only the cells needed to distinguish a reproducible dtype interaction from an intermittent runtime stall.
3. Split the first step at the gradient/optimizer boundary in a diagnostic run. Block after gradient computation, then apply the optimizer to those on-device gradients and block again; preserve both executable fingerprints and per-rank GPU/NCCL evidence. If gradients stall, continue the runtime investigation in #11440/#11646. If the optimizer stage stalls, isolate the routed expert Adam update and per-group clipping separately, checking update/state sharding and the blocked kernel or collective before changing production code.
4. Make the smallest code fix supported by that isolation. Add a regression for the isolated failure, then verify the original FP32/Adam-expert recipe on three fresh bounded 20-update runs: update 1 completes, losses remain finite, and the parameter and optimizer leaves retain FP32 storage. Report cache status and warm-step timing separately from the hang result.

spillover_issues.title: [long-loop] First SFT update hangs on 64 H100s with Adam expert banks and FP32

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Ablations on Snowball (the 10/05 SFT model) to choose SFT and RL settings for the Mochi 535B post-training run. Each experiment has a 1 h version and an 8 h version. Most backlog items have not run yet; current results are under Status.

## Description

Snowball is a smaller Grug MoE with the same post-training stack as Mochi. Each experiment changes one setting of the SFT or RL recipe (data, optimizer, loss mask, precision, tool format, RL task choice) and compares it against a matched control. The arms are read out with Micro210, BFCL ×5 and a retention panel. Experiments that look useful are then checked on Mochi.

Issue 11177 made the long loop runnable from the 10/05 SFT. Issue 11337 tracks run-ready Snowball recipes and Micro eval scores. Issue 11531 tracks Snowball long-loop SFT on TPU v4.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find which recipe settings change Snowball's agentic and tool-use scores enough to carry into Mochi's next SFT/RL stage.

## Sub-issues

Each result is posted on its own issue:
- Snowball long-loop SFT on TPU v4: issue 11531
- Malformed JSON in nested Pi edit calls: issue 11536
- SFT optimizer, Muon-H vs Adam (C150 vs O150): issue 11537
- TMax data, with vs without: issue 11539
- RL samples per prompt: issue 11594
- Mochi BFCL ×5 versus Snowball models: issue 11538
- First expert-Muon-H train step stalls on 64 H100s: issue 11646
- Does teacher closeness predict SFT outcome: issue 11673
- Measured student NLL closeness to teacher traces: issue 11674
- Bug, long-loop SFT screens stored parameters in BF16 (FP32 comparison and affected runs): issue 11687
- Rolling recovery checkpoints and single final saves in long-loop SFT: issue 11714
- What Mochi is similar to (NLL and behaviour against open-weight models): issue 11722
- Mochi SFT (step 400407) weakness analysis and candidate target skills: issue 11723
- Teacher soft targets and temperature matching for Snowball SFT: issue 11724
- GPU train step ~3x slower in the process that compiled it than when loaded from the persistent compile cache: issue 11775
- Pretraining replay share (20%, 40%, and 60% from the pre-train base): issue 11783
- First SFT update hangs on 64 H100s with Adam expert banks and FP32: issue 11793

## Status

- **Tool-call format:** in the FP32 from-base pair (one training run per arm), replacing 41 of 4,800 rows with synthetic Pi edit-call exercises scored 120 of 855 on the edit-call test (higher on 10 of 11 tasks) and Micro210 score mass 97.39 / 99.33 (mean 98.36 of 440), against 63 of 855 and 87.30 / 87.28 (mean 87.29) for the control; native equal-20 overlapped across repeats (20.21% vs 19.12%), AIME24 and OlympiadBench accounted for 11.00 of the 11.07 mass points (the other 18 sources netted +0.07, with tool-use sources not clearly improving), and both arms sat far below the 2026-11-18 from-base control (145.01) and 10/05 (175.75). Earlier 15-update FP32 continuations from 10/05 scored 284 to 293 of 855 against 224 for 10/05 (issue 11687), and a partial Mochi screen found far fewer broken edit calls (7 of 358 against Snowball's 524 of 1,093) but ended undecided. On a weak baseline (one run per arm), the edit-data run scored nearly twice as high on the edit-call test with no measured cost to general ability, so we keep the edit-call rows in the mix; the effect size on a healthy model and any gain on real agent tasks are not yet measured, and earlier BF16 runs through 2026-11-18 carried the BF16 stored-parameter caveat (issue 11687). See issue 11536.
- **SFT optimizer (Muon-H vs Adam):** the two evals disagree—BFCL favors Muon-H (30.2% against 24.6 to 24.7%), Micro210 favors Adam (41.9% against 37.7%), and training loss is about the same. No winner; we kept Muon-H because it matches pretraining and ran no more arms, and both runs had the BF16 stored-parameter precision bug (issue 11687), so this comparison should not be used to choose an optimizer. See issue 11537.
- **TMax pair:** the TMax run fits held-out TMax traces better (loss 0.299 against 0.587) but scores lower on BFCL (209/615 against 262/615 with the training template), and Micro210 is incomplete (two of the three runs failed). No clean answer: these runs stored weights in BF16 (issue 11687) and trained on whole traces rather than only assistant turns, so the question stays open until a redo with FP32 weights and assistant-only loss. See issue 11539.
- **Mochi BFCL ×5 (Pi agent, 123 tasks):** 450/615 (73.17%) record score under the configured retry rule; 449 first-attempt wins, one first-attempt reward unavailable after a timeout (bounding the first-attempt mean at 73.01–73.17%), against 33.98–52.36% for Snowball models. Because serving hardware and code revisions differed between the Mochi and Snowball runs, the comparison is descriptive; attributing the gap to the model alone would require a matched rerun. See issue 11538.

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

- 2026-11-16: Flat edit tool ruled out for reported benchmarks and the default harness. The fix for malformed edits goes on the model side (SFT data).
- 2026-11-16: The SFT training data's tool calls were audited: 452 of 47.4M assistant call spans failed a JSON check. No data repair.

## Conclusion

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 The C150, O150 and TMax SFT arms have trained but still need Micro210 readouts. The E12 one-hour arms also await readout; [#11536](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11536) tracks their nested-edit hypothesis. The two published [long-loop recipes](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337) changed training recipes and have different scoring coverage, so their aggregate scores do not isolate an ablation effect.

Plan:
1. For each SFT or RL setting, pin a control and one-setting treatment at the one-hour and eight-hour budgets. Match the starting checkpoint, source and data revisions outside the tested change, task IDs, seeds, Pi harness, and eval policy. Preserve the consumed configs and checkpoint revisions.
2. Finish the pending C150/O150/TMax and E12 one-hour Micro210 readouts first. Compare matching task IDs and report scored/unscored counts, per-benchmark and aggregate deltas, BFCL ×5, and the retention panel. Include malformed nested-edit rates for E12. Use [#11536's gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11536): at least a 50% rate reduction against its control with no Micro210 or retention loss.
3. Advance arms with a positive paired agentic/tool-use result and no retention regression to matched eight-hour controls. Repeat the same panels, report uncertainty and incomplete coverage, and record null or adverse results. Check surviving settings on Mochi before selecting its SFT/RL recipe.
4. Keep an arm table here with the changed setting, control and treatment pins, both budget readouts, BFCL and retention results, and the carry/drop decision. Add each run-ready recipe, exact data mix, Micro policy, immutable checkpoint, and archive receipts to [#11337](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337).

The two parent judge workers and brokers each had only A0. Their final preemption_count of one accompanies terminal KILLED cleanup after the policy child finished; no native restart gap was found. This does not prove continuous HTTP health or explain the repeat's seven exclusions. The bound vllm_server.py is identical between those runs; a different file in the current checkout is not a run-to-run source change or a deployed-byte readback.

## Historical TMax results

The old RNO control run used eight slots and three-hour child caps. The old TMax arm failed and yielded a conservative recovered subset of 437/440: available macro 52.39%, pooled 44.99%, three unknown. There was no complete native aggregate for that arm. Neither result fills a current-harness row. The superseded failed parent recovery is not used here.

The two current TMax runs bind the original cw-us-east-02a exports without copying: arm 134,181,708,393 B; control 134,181,708,404 B. Both have 87 HF objects and 39 weight shards. Fresh metadata and header checks are not a new full tensor-payload parity audit.

Both current roots and policy children succeeded, each with seven terminal jobs and seven A0 attempts. The arm has one BixBench exclusion; control has one TB2 exclusion. Both remain unknown. The same startup config-parse diagnostic appeared in both completed parent logs and TMax; later scoring superseded the early zero-ready snapshot. Its cause and harmlessness are not established. Terminal accounting does not establish both GPU Pods absent or provider release.

Both RL training arms reached saved step-10 native checkpoints, but their training roots failed during teardown. Both HF exports are structurally verified in cw-rno2a. The two Micro210 repetitions per export and regional parent all have successful roots and policies, seven terminal jobs and seven observed A0 attempts per evaluation. Judge workers and brokers were KILLED after policy completion. No retry or continuous-health inference follows from the one-attempt observations. W&B in-run metrics and teacher-closeness NLL are not Micro210.

Accepted failure/preemption/job-wide retry limits are explicit: root 0/0/0; policy 0/1000/0; judge 1/10/1; broker 0/1000/0; prepare-model 1/100/0; prepare_micro and verify_ready_inputs each 0/100/0. All 39 same-named shard hashes recorded in the two export manifests differ between the RL exports and from the parent's retained verified shard hashes. The harness selects the separately pinned tools tokenizer and template, not the export's embedded template. Contributor SFT is not run and the full run is not planned. Only a two-update smoke existed. comments.body:
🤖 ## Finding: the long-loop SFT ablations used a different optimizer grouping from 10/05 and Mochi

Found on 2026-11-17 while preparing an arm that restores the 10/05 optimizer state: the saved state did not fit the optimizer that the long-loop SFT code builds.

## What differs

| Parameter family | 10/05 (saved optimizer state, logged config) | Mochi SFT (sealed source, hero-EP optimizer) | Long-loop SFT ablations (bound source) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stacked expert `w_gate` / `w_up` / `w_down` (4-D) | MuonH | MuonH | **Adam** |
| Stacked `rms_attn` / `rms_mlp` scales (2-D) | Adam | Adam | **MuonH** |
| Shared expert weights (3-D) | MuonH | MuonH | MuonH |
| Gradient clipping | none | not compared | **1.0** (E12 config) |

## Cause

The long-loop `sft.py` imports the generic `experiments/grug/moe/optimizer.py`. Its MuonH rule accepts only 2-D and 3-D weights and has no rule that sends RMSNorm scales to Adam. With stacked blocks the 4-D expert weights fall through to Adam and the 2-D stacked norm scales go to MuonH. The June TPU optimizer implementation that the 10/05 model card links to, which is consistent with that run's saved optimizer slots and logged config, and the hero-EP optimizer in the sealed Mochi source both handle the stacked case explicitly (RMSNorm scales to Adam, 2-D to 4-D weights to MuonH). The generic file at `main` commit `18ae01ee42` is byte-identical to the one the ablations used.

## Runs affected

- **Affected (bound source and published consumed configs; worker import bytes not separately attested):** the E12 all-weights and general-only arms, the TMax arm and its control, C150, and the low-learning-rate replay rerun of 2026-11-17.
- **Related code, swapped families not trained:** the E12 attention-and-head-only arm freezes the expert and norm families, so the swap does not act on it.
- **Not affected:** Mochi SFT through step 400,407 (from its sealed source, not a fresh worker attestation); O150 (plain Adam by design); the RL arms (Megatron AdamW).

## What this does and does not show

- The E12 all-weights and general-only arms and the TMax arm and control used this grouping in their bound source. None is a matched test of the 10/05 optimizer set-up.
- It is a candidate cause of that drop. It is **not** shown to be the cause; no run with the corrected grouping has been evaluated yet.
- The 10/05 grouping is established from its logged optimizer config (`rmsnorm_to_adam=true`, no clipping) and its saved optimizer slots. The exact commit that run was launched from is not recorded in its W&B run.

## Next

1. A replay-only arm on 10/05 (15 updates, fresh optimizer state, learning rate 5e-6) with the 10/05 grouping and no clipping. The grouping change labels all 27 parameter leaves of the model the same way as the 10/05 optimizer state.
2. The same arm with the uncorrected grouping finished training on 2026-11-17 and is being evaluated; the pair gives the comparison.
3. A fix for the generic optimizer, or a switch of the long-loop SFT code to the hero-EP optimizer, follows as a PR.

spillover_issues.author: mcwitt
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Four `long-context/*` branches implement the context-parallel gaps #8374 lists for Grug main: a `context` mesh axis, context-sharded queries in the production FA4/CuTe attention path, a token-axis policy for MoE routing and loss under a sharded sequence, and an opt-in Transformer Engine CP backend. An integration branch composed them and trained the hero shape at sequence 262144 on one NVL72 rack (EP16xCP4, global batch 16, 4.19M tokens/step) from the hero's step-6000 checkpoint: 8.78% MFU, 113.5 s/step, peak HBM 127.6 of 138.2 GiB, and a drop fraction of 18% that was still rising. The hero's 1.15/1.15 capacity factors, tuned at sequence 4096 with batch 1024, do not carry to 262K at batch 16.

## Description

The 535B-A23B campaign (#8435) plans context extensions to 65K and possibly 262K; #8374 tracks the blockers and names four gaps in Grug main. Each gap has its own branch with a spec, implementation, an independent code review, and a fix round; specs and implementation notes live under `.agents/projects/` on each branch.

* [`long-context/mesh-context-axis`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/long-context/mesh-context-axis): `(replica_dcn, data, context, expert, model)` compact mesh via `compact_grug_mesh(context_axis_size=...)`, ported from the finished 262K TPU CP4 run (commit `b2cf4fe1aa` on `june_tpu_67b_a2b`). Checkpoints record no mesh, so pre-context checkpoints restore onto the 5-axis mesh unchanged.
* [`long-context/fa4-sequence-sharding`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/long-context/fa4-sequence-sharding): all-gather-KV context parallelism in the FA4/CuTe path. A runtime `q_offset` kernel input supplies the causal frontier (the kernel derives it from the local query index), the shard_map transpose provides the dK/dV psum over `context`, and the backward query-tile range is clamped to close an out-of-bounds LSE/dPsum read for key CTAs past a shard's queries. 19/19 GPU tests on GB200 at seq 512 / cp 2, including the hero tile config.
* [`long-context/moe-context-sharding`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/long-context/moe-context-sharding): the flattened token axis is sharded over `("replica_dcn", "data", "expert", "context")` and each context shard routes its tokens independently; EP drop psums, both QB estimators, and the fused cross-entropy loss reduce over spec-derived token axes.
* [`long-context/te-cp-backend`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/long-context/te-cp-backend): opt-in `gpu_te_cp` backend whose striping matches TE v2.17's `reorder_causal_striped` source. Runtime is blocked by the cuDNN `BAD_PARAM` in #8141, and no shipped variant can select it yet: a homogeneous layer scan cannot give TE a static per-layer window.
* [`long-context/262k-rack-experiment`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/long-context/262k-rack-experiment): merges the four, ports the bench launcher flags (`--seq-len`, `--restore-from`, `--context-axis-size`, `--expert-axis-size`, `--qk-mult`), and adds what composition required: composite `("expert", "context")` parameter sharding, a context-sharded residual stream, a left-halo `short_conv` wrapper, and a `MeshConfig` fix for global batch below the device count.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Measure whether the hero shape trains at 262144 sequence length on GB200 and what it costs in memory, throughput, and routing drops from a real checkpoint. This covers gates 1-2 of the early-cooldown list and the docs-per-shard routing risk #8374 calls the unresolved model-quality question.

## Status

Probe complete. Run `lc262k-ep16cp4-08251450` restored the 535B step-6000 checkpoint in 3.5 minutes and trained to the 6100 stop step on one rack; the job sealed `succeeded` with one preemption. Steady state over steps 6000-6012, from raw timestamps: 113.5 s/step, 37,042 tokens/s, 8.78% MFU, peak HBM 127.63 GiB against a 138.22 GiB limit, loss 1.416 median.

`moe/drop_fraction` was 0.18 median (0.081 sender, 0.101 receiver), rising 0.168 to 0.207 over the window. `capacity_overflow_rate_mean` tracks it exactly, so the loss is capacity clipping, not transport. Baselines: 3.5% drops on the live 4K hero, 1.7e-4 on the 4K one-rack restore arm. At batch 16 each expert coordinate routes one 65,536-token document instead of sixteen independent 4,096-token sequences, and expert load within one document is correlated enough that the fixed per-expert capacity clips it.

Caveat: the LR heuristic reads `HERO_MODEL.max_seq_len` (4096), so the probe applied ~6.9e-5, about 2% of the checkpoint's rate. The run measures throughput, memory, and routing; it does not diagnose 262K training stability.

## Links

* Plan and full run record (three failed attempts and their fixes): [`.agents/projects/20260824_262k_rack_experiment.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/long-context/262k-rack-experiment/.agents/projects/20260824_262k_rack_experiment.md)
* W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc262k-ep16cp4-08251450
* Blocker tracker: #8374. TE/cuDNN toolchain: #8141. Hero campaign: #8435.

## Decision Log

* All-gather-KV FA4 is the production CP path; TE stays an opt-in seam until the #8141 toolchain is fixed.
* Parameters, their fp32 pinned-host masters, and Muon state shard over composite `("expert", "context")` so CP does not multiply per-rank optimizer memory; without this, EP16xCP4 needs ~1072 GB/node of host memory against ~850 available. Muon's Newton-Schulz derives its layout from the parameter instead of a hard-coded spec.
* The residual stream is context-sharded end to end, unblocked by a `kernel_size - 1` left halo (carrying neighbour segment ids) above the unchanged `short_conv` Pallas kernel. This took the rack step from an uncompilable 350 GiB/device to 127.6 GiB, and the d768 ladder at seq 262144 / cp4 from 19.71 to 13.59 GiB.
* `--schedule-steps 4470000` holds the mixture's simulated-epoching budget at ratio ~1 so no cell slices empty at sequence 262144.

## Conclusion

The hero shape compiles, restores, and trains at 262K on one rack with 10.6 GiB of HBM headroom. Routing capacity is the open problem: 18% of assignments drop under the 4K-tuned capacity factors, and the rate was still rising when the probe ended.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Handoff.

**State.** The five branches are pushed and review-complete: each went through a spec, implementation, an independent code review, and a fix round, with the full CI suite green on every tip (1964 passed on the integration branch). No PRs are open; that was deliberate while the campaign ran. The probe sealed `succeeded` and the numbers in the body are final.

**Blockers.**

* Routing: 18% drops, still rising, under the 4K-tuned 1.15/1.15 capacity factors. This blocks real 262K training in the current configuration.
* Stability is unread: the LR heuristic computes from `max_seq_len` 4096, so the probe applied ~2% of the checkpoint's LR. A stability read needs the heuristic computed at the real sequence length, or an explicit resume-LR config the way the 67B cooldowns used `GrugMoeMuonHResumeConfig`.
* TE runtime: `gpu_te_cp` cannot execute until the #8141 cuDNN `BAD_PARAM` toolchain issue is fixed. Not on the critical path; FA4 all-gather-KV is the working production path.

**Remaining work, in rough order.**

1. Upstream to main as reviewed PRs: mesh, then FA4, then MoE, then TE. The integration-only commits need proper homes: the `MeshConfig` fix and launcher flags belong with the hero launcher; composite parameter sharding, the context-sharded residual, and the `short_conv` halo belong with the FA4/MoE material.
2. Routing at 262K: a capacity-factor sweep at sequence 262144 (the probe recipe is the harness; only the factor changes), and/or qualify the dropless FSDP path for the 262K phase. The mechanism is docs-per-shard collapse, so more racks at a larger global batch also moves it.
3. A stability probe with corrected LR to read the loss trajectory against the step-6000 baseline.
4. Measured but unfixed performance items: the MoE flatten costs context-group all-to-alls each layer (shard_map over the 3-D activation is the recorded alternative); the cross-shard dK/dV reduction happens in bf16 and its error grows with the CP degree (compare against cp1 before long training); the composite parameter spec triggers ~1 GB/rank/step of involuntary SPMD rematerialization copies.
5. This infrastructure also unblocks the early 65K cooldown probe (CP2 or no CP). The open gates in [`20260824_535b_long_context_cooldown.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/docs/535b-long-context-summary/.agents/projects/20260824_535b_long_context_cooldown.md) still apply, including a retrieval eval beyond 32K (#7638).

spillover_issues.author: mcwitt
spillover_issues.body:
Marin has no way to mark a test as needing a GPU, a minimum device count, or a specific accelerator. Some accelerator tests skip invisibly in CI as a result, and the two that need real device topology were written outside pytest entirely.

`tests/test_utils.py` provides `skip_if_no_tpu` and nothing equivalent for GPUs or device counts. The root `pyproject.toml` markers are `slow`, `integration`, `data_integration`, `cluster`, `requires_cluster`, `docker`, and `manual`; none describes hardware. `tests/cluster/conftest.py` names two clusters, `MARIN_TPU_CLUSTER` and `MARIN_GPU_CLUSTER = "cw-us-east-02a"`, with no entry for the GB200 cluster `cw-us-east-08a`.

Two tests in `lib/levanter/tests/grug/test_grugformer_moe.py` check the ragged all-to-all MoE backend against a dense reference and run nowhere:

```
uv run python -m pytest lib/levanter/tests/grug/test_grugformer_moe.py -rs -k "ragged or granular or clip"
...
SKIPPED test_moe_mlp_ep_backends_match_dense_value_and_gradients_when_available[ragged_all_to_all]
SKIPPED test_moe_mlp_reports_positive_drop_count_in_ragged_a2a_when_over_capacity
5 passed, 2 skipped
```

They skip on `requires an even number of >=2 devices`, and forcing two CPU devices hits the next guard, `ragged_all_to_all is not implemented on XLA:CPU`. Every job in `.github/workflows/` runs on `ubuntu-latest`. The five that pass cover lowering, offset arithmetic against a NumPy simulation of the collective, and capacity clipping in isolation. None runs the real collective or the SM100 expert kernels.

The root `addopts` does not include `-rs`, so these skips never appear in CI output. A green run with full coverage and a green run with no ragged coverage look identical.

Both files that need real accelerator topology avoided pytest. `lib/iris/tests/e2e/gpu_gang_smoke.py` is a standalone `__main__` script with `--target kind|coreweave` and `--i-understand-the-cost`; it mock-labels kind nodes to simulate an NVLink domain instead of requiring one. `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/ragged_ep_check.py` (PR #8549) submits a 4-GPU GB200 job, computes a pass/fail verdict, and raises on failure, but sits under `experiments/` with no scheduled caller.

Two cases need different mechanisms. A test like the levanter one needs N local devices inside the pytest process. A test like `ragged_ep_check` needs no local hardware: it submits a job whose constraint rides in `ResourceConfig.with_gpu("GB200", count=4, ...)`, so what it needs is a cluster fixture and a way to declare that the run is expensive.

#7242 delivered `tests/cluster/`, the `cluster` marker, and `marin-cluster-smoke.yaml` for smokes that submit real jobs. It left open which hardware a test needs and what a test that cannot get that hardware should do.

Done when:

- A test can declare a local device requirement and skip with a named reason instead of an ad-hoc in-file guard.
- Skipped tests are visible in CI output.
- A job-submitting test can target the GB200 cluster through a fixture, and its cost is expressible on the test rather than only in the workflow.
- One existing case is ported as the reference: the levanter ragged EP tests, or `ragged_ep_check.py`.

comments.body:
🤖 Correction to this issue's premise, found while acting on it in #8549.

It says `tests/cluster/` "covers submitting a job to a standing cluster" and that the gap is a GB200 lane and a cost tier on the existing workflow. The workflow no longer exists. #8605 deleted `.github/workflows/marin-cluster-smoke.yaml` on 2026-08-22, and its commit message gives the reason:

> Marin Cluster Smoke had zero successful scheduled runs: all 38 runs from July 17 through August 23 were cancelled around its 100-minute timeout. The workflow and its Grafana lane are deleted. The underlying tests remain directly runnable through the cluster-test runbook.

So nothing runs the `cluster` marker at all now, and this issue covers restoring a runner rather than extending one. The two other gaps it names are unaffected: there is still no way to declare a local device requirement, and `addopts` still carries no `-rs`, so skipped tests stay invisible.

One gap it named is now closed. #8549 moved the 4-GPU ragged transport gate to `tests/cluster/grug/test_ragged_ep_check.py`. That needed only a constant naming the GB200 peer, because `cw-us-east-08a` is already a federation peer of the marin hub and `target_cluster` is a `ResourceConfig` field, so `iris_client` works unchanged. No new fixture was required after all.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Correcting my comment above, which was too absolute. "No workflow runs the `cluster` marker" is accurate; "accelerator tests have no automated vehicle" was not.

Scheduled GPU work does run. `marin-canary-ferry-coreweave.yaml` fires daily at 10:00 UTC against `cw-us-west-04a`, sets `CANARY_ACCELERATOR: gpu`, and runs `python -m experiments.ferries.canary_ferry` on 8x H100 through Iris, with `scripts/ci/validate_canary_metrics.py` asserting the result. That is a real accelerator smoke on a daily cron. It is not pytest and carries no marker.

`iris-smoke-coreweave.yaml` looks like a second GPU lane and is not one. It runs `pytest tests/test_integration_test.py -m integration` on PRs touching `lib/iris/**`, and the workflow comment says it submits "against the shared H100" — but the jobs `tests/integration_test.py` submits are `ResourceConfig.with_cpu()` with `require_accelerator=False`. It exercises a CoreWeave-hosted controller, not a GPU.

The deleted `marin-cluster-smoke.yaml` had two jobs, not one. `marin-tpu-smokes` ran on the schedule; `marin-gpu-smokes` was `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.run_gpu`, so it never ran on a cron at all. The 38 timed-out scheduled runs the deleting commit cites were the TPU job. Standing-cluster GPU tests were therefore never automatic, before or after #8605.

So the gap this issue describes is sharper than "no runner": **no pytest marker anywhere selects GPU work.** The `cluster` marker has no workflow, and the `integration` marker runs only CPU jobs. Every GPU assertion in CI today lives in the canary ferry, outside pytest.

Two facts worth having when someone picks this up. The canary already parameterizes the accelerator (`CANARY_GPU_TYPE`, documented as "H100, GH200, B200", plus `CANARY_GPU_COUNT` and `CANARY_GPU_REPLICAS`), so scheduling GPU work of a given shape from Actions is solved machinery rather than something to build. And `marin-canary-ferry-coreweave.yaml` and `iris-smoke-coreweave.yaml` share the concurrency group `iris-coreweave-ci-shared` because they contend for one host, so any added lane needs a capacity story and not only a config entry.

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Build RiffleEval as a paired long-context evaluation of coherent stream tracking. Each base item keeps the source text, question, answer, distractors, and token budget fixed while changing document chunks from blocked to riffled order. The primary result is the per-item riffle penalty, sliced by foreign-chunk interference count and token distance.

UncheatableEval is a candidate source feed after revision pinning, token-length filtering, license review, and safety filtering. Its current Marin integration is unsuitable: it downloads a stale GitHub fork whose records are capped at 5,000 characters and supplies no questions or evidence annotations. For v0, use frozen natural documents with exact-answer factual overlays; evaluate a filtered UncheatableEval `-Long` subset as one source arm, beginning with English Wikipedia and permissively licensed documents.

## Description

Long-context evaluations such as NIAH often test retrieval of one conspicuous item from a large context. RiffleEval tests whether a model can maintain several ordered information streams whose chunks repeatedly alternate across a 32K–64K prompt, then reconstruct facts within one stream.

For source document \(D_i = [C_{i,1}, \ldots, C_{i,n}]\), generate a legal merge that preserves chunk order within each source. Every chunk receives an opaque, per-example stream ID and ordinal. Questions and evidence annotations are created and verified against the clean document before riffling.

Each base item produces these conditions:

1. Clean target document, for source-task competence.
2. Blocked full context, with the target and distractor documents contiguous.
3. Riffled full context, with identical content and prompt budget.
4. Adjacent-evidence control for multi-evidence items.

The v0 task families are single-stream exact QA and two-evidence within-stream integration. Cross-stream joins and continuation NLL remain follow-ups.

The proposed context-length and stream-count matrix is not a full Cartesian product. With 4K–8K source documents, 32K supports roughly 4–8 streams and 64K supports roughly 8–16 streams. Larger documents or additional filler semantics would be required to hold stream count fixed while scaling total context. The generator must reject infeasible cells instead of silently repeating or padding sources.

## Hypothesis or Goal

At fixed content and question difficulty, riffling causes a measurable accuracy loss beyond the loss caused by the same blocked distractors. The loss increases with the number of intervening foreign chunks after controlling for absolute token distance. Better long-context checkpoints should move the retention curve toward larger interference counts.

## Status

Background research is complete. No implementation or model run has started.

### Proposed v0

- 250–500 verified base items, expanded into deterministic paired variants.
- 32K and 64K contexts; feasible 4/8/16-stream cells; approximately 512-token chunks.
- Exact short answers with one-evidence and two-evidence overlays.
- Opaque opening and closing markers with tokenizer-balanced random IDs.
- Random and same-domain distractors.
- Native-model score with tools disabled.
- Exact match, per-item riffle penalty, blocked-to-riffled penalty, and retention curves by token distance, interference count, evidence count, and active streams.
- Target-stream extraction and oracle-evidence diagnostics to separate stream selection from reasoning.
- Frozen generator version, seed, source revision/hash, tokenizer, prompt, and structural metadata for every item.

### UncheatableEval corpus decision

Use it as an optional source-discovery and freshness feed. Do not use the published collection as the sole corpus or reuse `experiments/datasets/uncheatable.py`.

The current upstream `-Long` snapshots contain 7,500 records across 15 categories and retain source URL, date, category, `content`, and `untruncated_content`. They provide recent natural interference, but no question, answer, stable ID, evidence span, or hop graph. The dataset card declares no dataset license, and source rights differ by document. AO3 has safety concerns; arbitrary GitHub files need license and secret checks; BBC is a poor redistribution default; PDF extraction can corrupt arXiv text. Freshness only protects models whose training cutoff predates the crawl.

A derived arm must:

- pin the Hugging Face revision and content hash;
- filter on benchmark-tokenizer length, language, quality, and safety;
- record URL, collection date, source category, license, and transformed-text hash;
- begin with English Wikipedia and individually cleared permissive sources;
- exclude BBC and AO3 from v0;
- generate exact-answer overlays and frozen evidence spans against the exact transformed text.

## Background Research Brief

- Effort / stop rule / date: medium; 2026-08-24; stopped when the internal, benchmark, corpus, and contradiction passes no longer changed the v0 recommendation.

### Current Marin context

- #7638 owns RULER integration. RiffleEval should not duplicate its eval harness work.
- #4736 specified the closest reusable data contract: frozen long-document QA items with exact answers, evidence spans, and length bins.
- #7181 found that retained MRCR context reduced final-turn PPL from 21.0855 to 10.4012 at 8,192 tokens. Its extraction PR #7203 closed unmerged, so it is prior evidence rather than current infrastructure.
- #5825 previously built 32K/64K long-document PPL slices; the implementation was later removed by #6633.
- No existing issue or implementation tests repeated switching among several coherent streams.

### External prior art

- [RULER](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06654) varies context length and task complexity across multi-needle retrieval, variable tracking, aggregation, and QA. RiffleEval adds coherent natural streams and a paired blocked/riffled intervention.
- [MRCR/Michelangelo](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12640) shows that repeated, similar requests and ordinal selection are harder than unique needles. RiffleEval should include similar competing streams and report random/noise floors.
- [NoLiMa](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05167) shows that lexical overlap makes retrieval easier and normalizes long-context scores to short-context competence. RiffleEval should vary lexical overlap and reject items with weak clean-document accuracy.
- [BABILong](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/c0d62e70dbc659cc9bd44cbcf1cb652f-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf) distributes multi-fact synthetic tasks through natural books. RiffleEval adds several foreground streams, explicit stream identities, and the same task before and after structural transformation.
- [LOFT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13121) found that marker and prompt formatting materially affect retrieval. Marker tokenization and query placement must be fixed or explicitly ablated.
- [UncheatableEval](https://github.com/Jellyfish042/uncheatable_eval) evaluates rolling internet text by NLL. Its freshness method is useful for source discovery; it does not provide RiffleEval annotations.

### Contradiction and shortcut pass

- Random riffles and IDs prevent fixed-order contamination but do not prevent a model from answering public facts from parametric memory. Synthetic counterfactual overlays provide the durable control.
- Opaque IDs expose segmentation but do not prevent keyword search within the target stream. Lexical-overlap and near-neighbor distractor slices remain necessary.
- “Uniform-ish” legal merges do not independently control gap length. Sample examples from explicit interference-count and token-distance strata.
- Marker token lengths can differ across tokenizers and become an unplanned treatment. Balance marker encodings and store their token counts.
- Native QA generation from unannotated documents can admit one-passage shortcuts. Require evidence spans, clean-document verification, and minimal-evidence ablations.

### Recommended next experiments

#### 1. Validate the paired structural signal at 32K

- Minimum experiment / baseline: 100 overlay items, four streams, 512-token chunks; clean, blocked, and riffled conditions on two representative models with different long-context capability.
- Expected signal / falsifier: a nonzero blocked-to-riffled penalty that grows across interference buckets while clean accuracy remains high. Near-zero penalty, floor-level clean accuracy, or prompt-format sensitivity larger than the treatment falsifies the current setup.

#### 2. Add two-evidence integration and 64K

- Minimum experiment / baseline: two controlled facts in widely separated chunks; adjacent-evidence and oracle-extracted-stream baselines; feasible 8/16-stream cells.
- Expected signal / falsifier: two-evidence retention degrades faster than one-evidence retention while oracle extraction recovers most accuracy. Failure of the oracle indicates base reasoning or question-construction problems.

#### 3. Compare source pools

- Minimum experiment / baseline: matched overlays over a pinned filtered UncheatableEval `-Long` arm and one stable, license-cleared long-document corpus.
- Expected signal / falsifier: model ranking and riffle penalty remain stable across source pools. Large domain-specific reversals require a multi-corpus benchmark or removal of the unstable source.

### Source ledger

| Source | Type | Location | Claim used for | Confidence | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RULER | paper | https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06654 | complexity axes and baselines | high | nearest variable-tracking precedent |
| Michelangelo / MRCR | paper and official code | https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12640 | repeated similar needles and order | high | conversation format differs from riffled documents |
| NoLiMa | paper | https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05167 | lexical-overlap shortcut and retention normalization | high | single-association retrieval |
| BABILong | paper | https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/c0d62e70dbc659cc9bd44cbcf1cb652f-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf | distributed multi-fact reasoning in natural text | high | one background stream |
| LOFT | paper | https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13121 | formatting and identifier sensitivity | high | fixed retrieval corpora |
| UncheatableEval | official repo and dataset | https://huggingface.co/datasets/Jellyfish042/UncheatableEval-2026-07-Long | source schema, freshness, and corpus limitations | high | no dataset-level license or QA annotations |
| Marin #4736 | GitHub issue | https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4736 | QA manifest and evidence schema | high | closed before implementation |
| Marin #7638 | GitHub issue | https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7638 | active RULER scope | high | avoid duplicate harness work |
| Marin #7181 | GitHub issue | https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7181 | paired MRCR PPL result | high | extraction PR closed unmerged |

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates: #7638, #4736, #7181, #5825

## Decision Log

- 2026-08-24: scope v0 to paired single-stream exact QA and two-evidence within-stream integration at 32K/64K.
- 2026-08-24: treat UncheatableEval as an optional filtered source arm; reject the current Marin handle and the unfiltered published corpus as the canonical benchmark source.
- 2026-08-24: defer cross-stream joins, continuation NLL, and 128K+ until the primary structural signal is validated.

## Conclusion

Open. Advance to implementation if the 32K pilot produces high clean accuracy, a reproducible blocked-to-riffled penalty, and a stable ordering across source pools and marker templates.

spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

`telemetry_v1` retained 643.5 million rows and 14.94 GiB across 28.54 hours on 2026-08-21, an observed fill rate of 12.57 GiB/day. Levanter supplied 66.2% of rows and node telemetry supplied 28.0%. This experiment will reduce duplicated and low-value writes, retain priority training metrics separately, and validate the result on copied production shards before a production PR.

## Description

Finelog's inherited 15 GiB per-namespace local-cache cap leaves about 28.6 hours of `telemetry_v1` queryable on local storage at the measured rate. A current 704-process Levanter run publishes `step` from every process. Node agents publish about twenty device series per GPU every 30 seconds. vLLM and Iris controller snapshots publish cumulative histogram buckets every 15 seconds.

The detailed commands and raw measurements belong in `.agents/logbooks/telemetry-volume.md` and the linked Loom artifacts. Production objects are read-only inputs; local shard copies stay outside the repository.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Route cheap, frequently queried training metrics to a 50 GiB priority namespace; route other telemetry to a bulk namespace; remove replicated Levanter progress; and reduce the cadence of high-volume bulk snapshots. The combined treatment should cut compressed bytes/day while increasing the locally queryable priority window.

## Status

Phase-a attribution is complete. A 10.08 GiB sample of 110 production Parquets is being copied for byte-level cadence and namespace experiments.

## Links

* Logbook: `.agents/logbooks/telemetry-volume.md`
* W&B Report: none
* Important updates: Loom artifact `telemetry-influx-phase-a`

## Decision Log

## Conclusion

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 In-progress, multi-module experiment with validation pending on copied shards — not opening a PR, since that would preempt the very treatments this issue is set up to measure. Three grounding notes so phase-b lands on real code:

**"Levanter publishes `step` from every process" — confirmed root cause.** `TelemetryTracker._publish` gates tracker metrics on `publish_tracker_metrics = (process_index == 0)`, but `log()` writes `step` and `progress_time_seconds` through `_set` *before* that gate, and `runtime_telemetry.configure(...)` runs on every process. So all 704 processes emit those two series, consistent with Levanter's 66.2% row share.
- [`telemetry.py#L200-L207`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/tracker/telemetry.py#L200-L207) — unconditional `_set("step"/"progress_time_seconds")`
- [`telemetry.py#L167-L169`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/tracker/telemetry.py#L167-L169), [`#L241-L247`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/tracker/telemetry.py#L241-L247) — process-0 gate that `step` bypasses

Gating those two writes on `self._publish_tracker_metrics` is the minimal "remove replicated Levanter progress" treatment (<20 lines).

**Priority vs bulk namespace — the enabling mechanism already exists.** `StoragePolicy(max_bytes / max_segments / max_age_seconds)` is applied per namespace at register time, so the 50 GiB priority namespace is a producer-side namespace split plus a policy value — no server change.
- [`policy.py#L28-L46`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/src/finelog/policy.py#L28-L46) — per-namespace caps on `RegisterTable`

**Cadence knobs are already configurable.** Node/probe intervals are plain parameters, so reducing bulk-snapshot cadence needs no new plumbing.
- [`prometheus.py#L128`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rigging/src/rigging/telemetry/prometheus.py#L128) — `poll_interval`
- [`probes/runner.py#L184`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rigging/src/rigging/telemetry/probes/runner.py#L184) — probe `interval`

Happy to carve any single treatment into its own PR once phase-b picks winners.

comments.body:
🤖 The [production-sample analysis](http://127.0.0.1:7878/s/l7xftsek/artifacts/telemetry-volume-mitigation-analysis) is complete.

The selected producer policy reduced the 10.08 GiB sample by 68.6% compressed bytes and 68.1% rows. The resulting priority tier projects to 2.09 GiB/day, or about 24 days under a 50 GiB local-cache budget. A 60-second compaction policy saved 63.9% and changed five-minute GPU-utilization means by 1.12 percentage points on average and 6.43 at p95. A 300-second policy saved 74.7%, with p95 utilization error of 28.1 points.

The implementation keeps priority training and Zephyr progress in `telemetry_v1`, routes bulk records to `telemetry_bulk_v1`, lowers the high-volume producer cadences, and leaves generic compaction downsampling for a metric-family-aware follow-up.

## Summary

- **Motivation:** Before choosing targeted data to add to Mochi's next SFT mix, we needed a trace-backed picture of where Mochi SFT (step 400407) lags peer open-weight models—such as MRCR-65k (26.49% vs Qwen3.6 92.08%) and IFBench (26.00% strict vs Gemma-4 43.44%)—rather than extrapolating from Snowball-only defects.
- **Goal:** Identify Mochi SFT (step 400407)'s clearest benchmark and trace-level weaknesses against peer open-weight models, check mode and SFT-mix coverage gaps, and test targeted SFT data candidates for Mochi's next SFT mix.
- **Data:** 12 completed full-size benchmark runs, BFCL ×5 (issue 11538), a partial SWE-smith screen (469 retained attempts), three controlled thinking-off versus thinking-on probes, the frozen 216-store SFT manifest (968,596 packs), and two synthetic SFT datasets (multi-needle retrieval and cue-balanced tool abstention).
- **Method:** Audit error traces, run matched thinking-off versus thinking-on probes and zero-training inference checks on Mochi, scan all 216 SFT stores for thinking-off tool coverage and placeholder arguments, and evaluate a 1-hour FP32 Snowball continuation with 120 multi-needle retrieval packs (loss weight 30) against a 1-hour general-only control on full 901-item MRCR-65k.
- **Results:** Clear benchmark gaps were MRCR-65k (26.49% vs Qwen3.6 92.08%), IFBench (26.00% strict vs Gemma-4 43.44%), BFCL live-irrelevance (65.5%), and SWE-smith read calls with an extra `command` key (69/469 attempts). At a matched 4,096-token cap, Mochi scored 81.67% (98/120) under thinking-off versus 96.67% (116/120) under thinking-on on deterministic constraints, and over-called on 57/60 missing-argument tool prompts under thinking-off versus 59/59 abstention passes under thinking-on (a system-prompt guard still over-called on 35/60; empty-think prefill still emitted reasoning on 120/120). The 216-store scan found 14,718 thinking-off rows across non-coding tool stores (vs 506,889 thinking-on rows in `agentic_v1/v2` alone) and 2,485 grounding-filtered explicit placeholder calls in `agentic_v1/tool_calling` (7,383 raw across four agentic stores). On Snowball, the 1-hour multi-needle retrieval run scored 21.20% vs 21.44% control (−0.24 pp) under thinking-off and 22.65% vs 21.59% (+1.06 pp) under thinking-on on MRCR-65k, with 175/901 unclosed think spans under thinking-on.
- **Conclusion:** Multi-needle retrieval data did not transfer to headline MRCR-65k in this single 1-hour Snowball run and stays held out of Mochi's SFT mix. Thinking-off tool abstention data, placeholder-argument filtering across the agentic stores, and a matched thinking-mode check on full IFBench remain the leading candidates for Mochi's next SFT mix, while hard-math, knowledge, and major agentic benchmarks remain unmeasured on Mochi.

Parent: [issue 11535](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535).

## 2. Trace-Backed Failure Analysis

### 2.1 `mrcr-65k` (26.49%, n=901; all 901 classified, 15 read directly)

Mochi prepends the exact requested 10-character random string on **806/901 (89.46%)** of prompts, and **186/901 (20.6%)** score `> 0.9` on MRCR's graded string-similarity metric. Mean `mrcr_accuracy` declines with needle count and across the four length buckets below 40k (`n_chars // 4`); the single 40k+ item scored 80.78%:

| Slice | n | Mean `mrcr_accuracy` |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2 needles | 299 | 36.29% |
| 4 needles | 302 | 28.71% |
| 8 needles | 300 | **14.47%** (graded string similarity) |
| 0–10k (`n_chars // 4`) | 325 | 31.68% |
| 10–20k (`n_chars // 4`) | 283 | 27.15% |
| 20–30k (`n_chars // 4`) | 159 | 20.05% |
| 30–40k (`n_chars // 4`) | 133 | 19.66% |
| 40k+ (`n_chars // 4`) | 1 | 80.78% |

Across the **620** items that hit the exact random prefix with `score <= 0.9`:
- **423 / 620 (68.2%)** matched another same-topic occurrence by a 60-character substring heuristic, with **331** matched occurrences later than the requested one and **92** earlier (measured direction; not opportunity-normalized). Under literal stripped-output equality with the same topic heuristic, **323 / 620 (52.1%)** matched another same-topic occurrence (**275** later, **48** earlier).
- **26 / 620 (4.2%)** matched a different-topic assistant turn under the 60-character substring heuristic.
- **171 / 620 (27.6%)** had no classified alternative-turn match under this heuristic (this residual count does not separate paraphrases from partial or truncated outputs).
- The remaining **95 / 901 (10.5%)** failed the exact-prefix check (`score = 0`).

### 2.2 `ifbench` (26.00% strict / 32.33% loose prompt; 27.91% strict / 34.88% loose instruction; all 300 classified, 15+ read)

Per-category means across all 300 prompts (344 total verifiable instructions; per-prompt category scores can be fractional when a prompt carries multiple constraints of the same type):

| Category | Prompts with category | Strict mean (sum / prompts) | Loose mean (sum / prompts) | Examples from inspected replies |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `repeat` | 9 | **0.00%** (0.0 / 9) | **0.00%** (0.0 / 9) | Misses exact sentence/phrase repetition or adds surrounding prose |
| `sentence` | 28 | **3.57%** (1.0 / 28) | **7.14%** (2.0 / 28) | Violates exact sentence-level structure (boundary words, keyword-per-sentence, bounds) |
| `words` | 85 | **11.76%** (10.0 / 85) | **17.65%** (15.0 / 85) | Violates forbidden words, required word frequency, or letter constraints |
| `ratio` | 44 | **15.91%** (7.0 / 44) | **15.91%** (7.0 / 44) | Misses punctuation/sentence/word ratio targets |
| `custom` | 11 | 27.27% (3.0 / 11) | 45.45% (5.0 / 11) | Extra prose or formatting wrappers break strict checks |
| `format` | 96 | 36.98% (35.5 / 96) | 52.60% (50.5 / 96) | Large strict-to-loose gap (+15.6 pp); inspected replies include markdown wrappers/preambles, wrong nesting depth, or non-emoji glyphs (`❖`) |
| `count` | 62 | 58.06% (36.0 / 62) | 59.68% (37.0 / 62) | Overshoots word/paragraph counts with preambles or closings |

No literal `<think>` tag was found in any of the 300 stored outputs. In inspected failing replies, recurring patterns include conversational preambles/wrappers that break strict format or count checks, inline self-correction text written into the graded reply (e.g. `"Wait — that doesn't indent properly..."`), and explicit refusal/surrender on strict character constraints.

### 2.3 Tool-Contract Sub-Weaknesses: BFCL x5 (165 failed trials audited, 22 raw traces read) and SWE-smith r6 (469 retained audited, 45+ traces read)

**BFCL x5 ([issue 11538](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11538): 450/615 = 73.17% final-selected record score under the retry rule; per-run 92, 92, 91, 86, 89 / 123; 449 known first-attempt wins with 1 unavailable first-attempt reward; 59 tasks 5/5, 12 tasks 0/5):**
- Weakest task categories: `simple-java` **53.3%** (8/15), `parallel` **62.9%** (22/35), `live-irrelevance` **65.5%** (95/145), `live-multiple` **74.3%** (130/175), `live-simple` **75.6%** (34/45), `multiple` **77.1%** (27/35), `parallel-multiple` **77.1%** (27/35).
- Verifier-log classification across all **165** failed trials (from the 615 saved `test-stdout.txt` logs):
  - **44 (26.7%) — residual `irrelevance` category failures** (`39 live-irrelevance + 5 irrelevance` not caught by missing-file or invalid-JSON checks). In inspected traces, Mochi emitted a tool call with guessed arguments instead of `[]`; the residual count itself does not verify the cause of every trial.
  - **44 (26.7%) — `live-multiple` verifier mismatches** (inspected examples include minor argument formatting differences such as `"Santa Cruz, US"` vs `"Santa Cruz, USA"` or selecting a sibling function).
  - **23 (13.9%) — missing `/app/result.json`** (`11 live-irrelevance`, `1 irrelevance`, `2 parallel-multiple`, `2 simple-python`, `2 simple-javascript`, `2 live-simple`, `1 live-multiple`, `1 parallel`, `1 simple-java`). The verifier logs establish file absence; in inspected irrelevance traces Mochi replied in plain text instead of writing `[]`, and in some inspected non-irrelevance traces it called BFCL target function names directly as Pi tools instead of writing `/app/result.json`.
  - **18 (10.9%) — `parallel` (12) and `parallel-multiple` (6) verifier mismatches** (inspected examples include omitted calls, parameter mismatches, or double-nested list syntax `[[...]]`).
  - **11 (6.7%) — `simple-python`**, **8 (4.8%) — `multiple`**, **7 (4.2%) — `live-simple`**, **6 (3.6%) — `simple-java`** (inspected examples emit JSON objects instead of Java constructor strings like `new QName(...)`), **2 (1.2%) — invalid JSON** in `/app/result.json`, **1 — `live-relevance`**, **1 — `live-parallel-multiple`**.

**SWE-smith 128x8 r6 screen (snapshot counts: 469 retained, 463 scored, 184 passed = 39.74%; 115/173 = 66.47% in the audit's exception-free scored bucket; 111/147 = 75.51% in readout-`CLEAN` evidence-complete rows; 69/289 = 23.88% on `AgentTimeoutError` attempts; 184/462 = 39.83% vs Snowball 43604 88/462 = 19.05% on the 462 both-scored join):**
- **Extra `"command"` key and malformed-tool counts (kept in separate denominators):**
  - **69/469** retained attempts included at least one parsed `read` call with an extra `"command"` key (**391/1,707** parsed `read` calls), and **13/469** included an extra `"command"` key on `edit`.
  - The first named malformed-tool category in the readout-`BAD` rows was **`read` for 12/19**, **`edit` for 6/19**, and **`bash` for 1/19** (contrasting with Snowball 43604's malformed nested-`edit` pattern).
  - Raw `<tool_call>` text appeared in assistant messages in **21/58** exception-free `reward=0` attempts (**15 `read`, 6 `edit`**). Inspected examples contain malformed JSON combining `"command":` with `"path":` or `"view_range":` (e.g., `{"name": "read", "arguments": {"command": "view_range": [1, 100]}}`), which suggests a hypothesis of schema bleed from `str_replace_editor`-style training traces into Pi's `read`/`edit` schemas.
- **Exception-free `reward=0` residual (37/58 without raw `<tool_call>` text):** Across all 58 exception-free `reward=0` attempts, 38 had at least one parsed `edit` call and 20 did not (vs 115/115 with a parsed `edit` call in the audit's exception-free passing bucket). In 12 inspected edited failures, Mochi modified code and ran local checks/pytest before finishing, yet failed hidden verifier tests; the audit script does not classify patch defects across all 37.
- **Timeouts (`289/469 = 61.6%` `AgentTimeoutError` at 900 s):** Among the 220 timed-out failures (`reward=0`), median progress is 18 agent steps, only **40/220 (18.2%)** contained a parsed `edit` call (vs **68/69 = 98.6%** of timed-out passes), and **160/220 (72.7%)** ran `git log`/`git show`/`git diff` commands before the 900 s cap.

### 2.4 `ds-1000-local` (27.00% = 54/200; all 200 classified, 25 ATIF trajectories read)

`ds-1000-local` sits inside Snowball 10/05's (`27.85% [23.12–31.00]`, k=6) and Qwen3.6-35B's (`26.75% [23.50–28.50]`, k=9) observed ranges, slightly below Nemotron-3.5-30B's range (`28.46% [27.50–30.50]`, k=9), and below Gemma-4-26B (`41.50%`, k=1). Its error breakdown differs from comparators:
- **Outcome partition (200 tasks):** 43 exception-free pass, 95 exception-free fail, **60 `AgentTimeoutError` at 1,800 s** (49 fail, 11 pass), and **2 `ModelInitiatedTmuxFailure`** (both fail). In the single checked comparator runs from EvalDash, timeouts were 1–6/200 (Qwen3.6: 1, Nem3.5-30B: 3, Gemma-4: 4, Snowball 10/05: 6).
- **Inspected Terminus-2 trajectories (25 total: 10 timeout-0, 10 clean-0, 2 tmux-0, 3 timeout-1):**
  - In the 10 inspected timeout failures (10–20 agent steps, ~7.4k–8.5k completion tokens), Mochi repeatedly rewrote `/workspace/solution/solution.py` (4–9 times) and ran custom import/`runpy` checks until hitting 1,800 s (one passing timeout, `ds-1000/541`, timed out right on Terminus-2's `"task_complete": true` confirmation turn).
  - In the 10 inspected exception-free failures (4–15 steps), Mochi wrote runnable code and marked the task complete while missing part of the prompt or execution contract (e.g., `ds-1000/104` replaced `&` with `&` without evaluating the resulting expression; `ds-1000/127` hardcoded `df.sample(n=1, random_state=0)` instead of sampling 20% of rows).
  - Both `ModelInitiatedTmuxFailure` cases occurred when sending shell control sequences during recovery from a hung command/quote.

### 2.5 `gsm8k-0shot` (83.55% = 1,102/1,319; all 217 failures classified, 20 read) — Extractor-Sensitivity Caveat

- **145 / 217 misses (66.8%) contain the normalized gold number in the final 250 characters under the regex used here.** Of those, **29** also match a verification keyword (`check`/`verify`/`double-check`/`confirm`) and **116** do not. The other **72** did not match the gold-number heuristic.
- This flags candidates for extractor sensitivity (in inspected replies, Mochi stated the gold number and then either restated a prompt quantity or appended a verification equation whose final number the last-number regex picked up). A verified corrected accuracy was not measured, so this audit neither estimates a corrected GSM8K score nor rules out genuine arithmetic errors.

### 2.6 Other Teams' Mochi Evaluations

- **Identity under `/think` ([issue 11418](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11418)):** Reports **222/320 (69.4%)** foreign-maker self-claims (Google/Gemini 129, Anthropic/Claude 41, OpenAI/ChatGPT 23, Zhipu 11) and **43/320** Marin-alone answers with reasoning enabled, versus near-100% Marin with `/nothink`, and proposes adding thinking-mode identity examples (noting `identity-data` is `/nothink`-only). Causality and the effect of adding those examples are untested here.
- **Variant effect prediction ([issue 11181](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11181)):** Closed exploratory evaluation on two 300-variant autosomal Mendelian train panels (10% positive rate). Raw-DNA log-likelihood scored AUPRC 0.178 (no prefix) / 0.189 (healthy prefix) with 61.1% / 60.7% within-group wins on missense, and AUPRC 0.150 / 0.141 with 50.0% / 49.3% within-group wins (near chance) on TSS-proximal variants.

---

## 3. Proposed Candidate Target Skills (with Fast-Eval Proposals and Non-Eval Data Ideas)

*Data hygiene rule:* **Eval-side traces and benchmark prompts/outputs are never used as training data.** Every training data proposal below relies exclusively on freshly synthesized or non-eval open templates verified programmatically. Probe runtimes below are rough estimates and not yet measured on Mochi's serve.

### Proposal 1: Long-Context Ordinal Multi-Needle Retrieval and Verbatim Copy
- **Target gap:** Largest observed deficit vs peers (`mrcr-65k` 26.49% vs Qwen3.6 92.08% and Nemotron-3.5-30B 45.75%), with 423/620 prefix-matching low-score items matching a different same-topic occurrence by 60-character substring (323 under literal stripped-output equality), predominantly later than requested.
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 100–200 item synthetic multi-needle probe at 8K–64K context (2/4/8 repeated-topic needles, querying the *k*-th 1-indexed occurrence with a random prefix), scored deterministically in Python by exact prefix and string similarity without an LLM judge.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Programmatically synthesize multi-turn dialogues (8K–64K tokens) mixing filler turns with 2–12 repeated requests on fresh non-MRCR topics, paired with final-turn ordinal retrieval queries distributed uniformly over *k* from 1 to *N* (covering both `/think` counting chains and `/nothink` direct-copy targets).

### Proposal 2: Strict Verifiable Constraint Following and Output Discipline
- **Target gap:** Strict instruction-following gap vs peers (`ifbench` 26.00% strict vs Gemma-4 43.44%, DeepSeek-V4-Flash 40.00%, Nemotron-3.5-120B 38.00%, Qwen3.6 34.57%), with `repeat` (0.00%), `sentence` (3.57%), `words` (11.76%), and `ratio` (15.91%) lowest.
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 200-item held-out synthetic constraint suite covering word/sentence/ratio/repeat/format/no-preamble constraints, scored purely by deterministic Python verifiers without an LLM judge.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Programmatically compose fresh prompts combining 1–3 verifiable lexical/structural constraints (forbidden/required words, exact sentence/word counts, keyword-per-sentence, ratio bounds, strict JSON/markdown structure, no preamble/postscript), generate candidates, and **rejection-sample strictly using deterministic Python verifiers** (keeping only 100%-passing responses across both `/think` and `/nothink` formats).

### Proposal 3: Tool-Schema Adherence and Abstention Across Diverse Tool Contracts
- **Target gap:** Addresses the concrete tool-contract weaknesses observed in BFCL x5 (`simple-java` 53.3%, `parallel` 62.9%, `live-irrelevance` 65.5%) and the extra-`"command"` `read`/malformed-call defects observed in SWE-smith r6 (69/469 attempts with extra `"command"` on parsed `read`; 12/19 readout-`BAD` first-tool `read`; 21/58 exception-free `reward=0` raw `<tool_call>` text).
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 150–200 item single-turn synthetic tool-calling probe testing: (a) unfamiliar file/code tool schemas deliberately distinct from `str_replace_editor` (checking valid Hermes JSON and zero undeclared keys), (b) irrelevance/abstention prompts requiring an explicit empty tool list or required artifact, and (c) parallel and typed-argument multi-call prompts. Graded deterministically by JSON-schema and AST checks without container spinup.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Synthesize diverse tool definitions (varying parameter names across file readers/editors, SQL/API clients, and typed Java/JS/Python signatures) with programmatically verified trajectories teaching strict adherence to declared JSON schemas, calibrated abstention when no tool applies or required arguments are missing, and parallel call arrays.

---

## 4. What Is Missing to Decide (Absence of Completed Full-Size Scores in This Snapshot)

In the retained EvalDash cache for `mochi-sft-step400407` (46 recorded runs: 23 `succeeded`, 20 `step_failed`, 2 `infra_failed`, 1 `running`), the following benchmarks have no completed full-size score. Recorded failure statuses alone do not establish backend-death causes or rule out model-side behavior, and absence of a row means no run was found in this snapshot (not a proof it was never run elsewhere).

| Benchmark | Snapshot status on Mochi step 400,407 | Snowball 10/05 EP-Oct (k) | Qwen3.6-35B EP-Oct (k) | Why it matters for targeting |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Micro210** (per-source suite) | No completed run found in the reviewed Micro210 ledger or EvalDash snapshot | 41.44% / 40.91% suite pooled (runs 44627 / 44628) | — | Per-source breakdown across internal post-training domains; aligns Mochi with Snowball ablation ledgers |

| `tb2-recovery` / `ot-tblite-recovery` | `1 step_failed` each (`2026-11-17T14:35:25`) | 11.28% (6) / 22.17% (5) | 35.77% (9) / 60.13% (9) | Long-horizon terminal/shell agency |
| `bixbench-pi` / `tau3-pi` | No run found in snapshot | 14.72% (6) / 6.30% (5) | 34.81% (9) / 36.50% (4) | Multi-turn scientific analysis and policy/tool dialogue |
| `aime24` / `olympiadbench` / `math500` (full) | `aime24`: `2 step_failed` (`16:27:39`, `18:18:58`); `olympiadbench`: `1 step_failed` (`14:51:31`); `math500`: `1 step_failed` (`18:18:58`), `1 infra_failed` (`19:12:42`), plus 18- and 20-item `succeeded` smokes at 100% | 79.67% (6) / 22.47% (5) / 96.33% (6) | 94.59% (9) / 35.00% (9) / 98.86% (7) | Hard-math headroom vs peers (cannot be inferred from `gsm8k-0shot`) |
| `gpqa-diamond` | No run found in snapshot | 66.43% (5) | 84.82% (7) | Graduate-level STEM reasoning |
| `mmlu-pro` | `2 step_failed` (`2026-11-16T16:27:39`, `18:18:58`) | 72.38% (5) | 85.26% (7) | Broad 10-way academic/domain knowledge |
| `cruxeval` / `nupa` | `2 step_failed` each (`2026-11-16T16:27:39`, `18:18:58`) | 58.63% (3) / 11.24% (4) | 91.94% (3) / 82.99% (8) | Code-execution reasoning (`cruxeval`) and numeric/algorithmic precision (`nupa`) |
| `mrcr` (128K full) | `1 step_failed` (`2026-11-16T16:27:39`) | 19.25% (5) | 91.40% (7) | Long-context behavior past 65K |

| **Controlled thinking-mode check** on `mrcr-65k` & `ifbench` | Not yet run on the same serve | — | — | Tests Mochi's sensitivity to thinking mode on the same serve before attributing the full gap to model capacity |

**Suggested next decision sequence (read-only recommendations; no jobs launched):**
1. Run a controlled thinking-on vs thinking-off sensitivity check on `mrcr-65k` and `ifbench` on the same serve, alongside completing the missing fast EvalDash benchmarks (`aime24`, `math500` full, `mmlu-pro`, `gpqa-diamond`, `cruxeval`, `nupa`) and a Mochi Micro210 baseline.

🤖

# Research

The step 400,407 audit identifies model and serving hypotheses, but no isolated repository defect: `mrcr-65k` and `ifbench` each have one full-size Mochi run and no matched thinking-mode check. The 145 GSM8K misses with a gold number near the end are extractor-sensitivity candidates, not a verified corrected score. The failed EvalDash records also need their own failure classification before reruns. Tool-call data work is already tracked in [#11536](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11536), and the Micro210 policy is being frozen in [#11686](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11686).

**Relevant code**
- [Evaluation launcher](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/cli.py) — resolves model and evaluation runs.
- [Evaluation records](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/records.py) — preserves run status and provenance.

# Plan

1. Freeze the Mochi export, tokenizer, serve and harness revisions, generation settings, task IDs, seeds, source `record.json` files, and a GPU/time budget. Classify each `step_failed` and `infra_failed` record from its saved artifacts; do not infer backend failure from status alone.
2. On the same serve, run matched thinking-on and thinking-off panels for `mrcr-65k` and `ifbench`, holding prompts, seeds, context limits, and output budgets fixed. Report paired score changes with uncertainty, MRCR needle-count and length slices, IFBench strict categories, truncation, and failures. If mode changes the scores, resolve that confound before attributing the gap to SFT data.
3. Complete the missing full-size fast EvalDash panel (`aime24`, `math500`, `mmlu-pro`, `gpqa-diamond`, `cruxeval`, `nupa`) after the failure classification, using the existing launcher and recording each terminal result. Run a Mochi Micro210 baseline against the frozen policy from #11686 when available. Separately regrade the 145 flagged GSM8K misses against the retained outputs and canonical scorer; open a scoped scorer fix only if a grading defect is reproduced.
4. Start with the ordinal multi-needle proposal if the matched mode check leaves a substantial MRCR gap. Make separate train and held-out synthetic templates, verify no eval prompt or trace enters training, and measure a 100–200 item probe before any SFT run. Compare a matched Snowball control and candidate, then promote to Mochi only if the held-out probe and full MRCR evaluation improve without losing Micro210 or BFCL. If that gate fails, report the negative result and evaluate the strict-constraint proposal next; coordinate tool-schema work with #11536.

| `schema_adherence_non_sre` | **100.00%** (50/50) [92.87–100.00] | **84.00%** (42/50) [71.49–91.66] | All 8 `/think` mismatches (`patch_snippet` 0/7, `pi_edit` 1/7) emitted schema-valid `inspect_file` (7) or `read` (1) calls with 0 undeclared keys and 0 malformed JSON, rather than patching directly |

The single-turn probe did not reproduce the SWE-smith pattern. Multi-turn context is one candidate to test in a matched follow-up.

---

### 3. Updated Targeting Implications (Read-Only Summary)

1. **Multi-needle ordinal retrieval at high needle count (`8 needles`: 52.5% `/nothink`, 50.0% `/think`)** persists under both configurations, alongside lower `<|start_think|>` emission in longer nominal bands (63.3% at 8k down to 20.0% at 56k) and 10 early-EOT unclosed think spans plus 1 cap hit on Probe 1 `/think`.
2. **Tool abstention under `/nothink` (38.0% overall; 0/25 on missing-required-argument prompts)** is a sharp deficit whereas the `/think` configuration passed all 50 abstention items (100.0%). Single-turn `parallel_and_typed` passed 50/50 in both configurations and `schema_adherence_non_sre` passed 50/50 (`/nothink`) and 42/50 (`/think`, with all 8 mismatches being schema-valid `inspect_file`/`read` calls), without reproducing the SWE-smith `command`-key pattern.
3. **Deterministic constraint following scored higher under the `/think` configuration (82.5% -> 96.7%; 19 think-only passes vs 2 nothink-only)**, with three of the four Probe 2 `/think` failures hitting the 4,096-token cap (compared with one 4,096-token cap hit and ten early EOTs on Probe 1 `/think`). This motivates running a controlled configuration check on full `ifbench` and `mrcr-65k` before committing large synthetic-data budget to constraint SFT.
